title: Manufacturing Process Flow & Control DFX Engineer III (Subsystem) — TeraWave Operation
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

Blue Origin's Emerging Systems business unit is building TeraWave, a satellite communications constellation powered by the most advanced optical communications architecture ever attempted: thousands of optically interconnected satellites delivering symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth, providing enterprise and hyperscale customers with resilient, scalable connectivity for critical operations where terrestrial infrastructure cannot reach.

As a Senior Manufacturing Process Flow & Control DFX Engineer (Subsystem), you will own the end-to-end manufacturing process flow and process control design integration at the subsystem level for TeraWave production — bridging subsystem-level production line architecture, process control systems, and volume production readiness. As a foundational element of TeraWave operations, subsystems must be produced through process flows architected not only for throughput but for manufacturability, testability, reliability, and serviceability at constellation scale. This is a hands-on role for an engineer who has designed, optimized, and scaled complex subsystem-level manufacturing process flows and control systems in fast-moving, high-volume manufacturing environments and wants to apply that experience to hardware operating at orbital scale.

Special Mentions:

  • Relocation assistance is available for qualified candidates.
  • Travel: Up to 50%.

Responsibilities:

Subsystem Process Flow & Control Design, Integration & Manufacturing

  • Lead subsystem-level manufacturing process flow design across satellite subsystems: subsystem production line architecture, inter-station workflow sequencing, subassembly integration points, takt time optimization, and material flow between subsystem builds.
  • Own subsystem process control development — including statistical process control (SPC), process monitoring, traveler and work instruction systems, MES integration, and data collection workflows across subsystem boundaries — to ensure robust, repeatable production.
  • Manage subsystem-level process documentation, routing definition, capacity planning, cross-subsystem coordination, and production line oversight.
  • Drive subsystem process validation, control plan development, first-article and production readiness reviews to support production ramp.

Design for Excellence (DFX)

  • Drive Design for Excellence (DFX) principles — DFM, DFT, DFA, DFR, and DFS — across the full subsystem-level manufacturing process flow and control lifecycle to ensure hardware scales from prototype through volume production for TeraWave operations.
  • Design for Manufacturability (DFM): Optimize subsystem process sequencing, station layout, and cross-subsystem workflow to maximize yield, throughput, and minimize cost at constellation-scale production volumes.
  • Design for Test (DFT): Architect subsystem-level in-line test and inspection points, data capture, and process monitoring to enable efficient subassembly acceptance, traceability, and in-field diagnostics.
  • Design for Assembly (DFA): Simplify subsystem process steps, minimize handoffs between subsystem builds, and optimize integration points to reduce cycle time, rework, and error rates.
  • Design for Reliability (DFR): Apply process FMEA, control plans, statistical process control, and reliability prediction to ensure consistent, defect-free subsystem production supporting long-duration operation in the orbital environment.
  • Design for Serviceability/Supply Chain (DFS): Coordinate with supply chain and manufacturing partners to align subsystem process flows with material availability, standardization, and obsolescence mitigation across the production lifecycle.
  • Partner with manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to define subsystem acceptance criteria, drive yield and throughput optimization, and support production ramp for sustained TeraWave operations.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of experience in manufacturing process engineering, process flow design, or production control in a product development and volume production environment.
  • Experience designing and optimizing subsystem-level manufacturing process flows, line balancing, and process control systems for complex hardware.
  • Hands-on experience with statistical process control (SPC), process FMEA, control plans, MES/ERP systems, and production line bring-up.
  • Demonstrated application of DFX principles (DFM/DFT/DFA/DFR) in bringing subsystem process flows from design into volume production.
  • Excellent technical documentation and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Industrial, Manufacturing, or Mechanical Engineering.
  • 15+ years of relevant experience.
  • Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or Black Belt) or equivalent process improvement expertise.
  • Experience with high-mix or high-volume subsystem production line design, automation integration, and Industry 4.0 / smart factory concepts.
  • Experience developing subsystem process flows for space, aviation, or other high-reliability manufacturing environments.
  • Experience with capacity modeling, simulation, and throughput analysis tools at the subsystem level.
  • Background in production hardware including comprehensive DFX practices (DFM/DFT/DFA/DFR), process optimization, supply chain coordination, and yield optimization at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with production ramp and factory scale-up.

Why Blue Origin

At Blue Origin, we are driven by Gradatim Ferociter — "Step by Step, Ferociously." As a Senior Manufacturing Process Flow & Control DFX Engineer (Subsystem), you will design and industrialize the subsystem-level production processes building an orbital constellation at unprecedented scale, alongside world-class engineers solving problems at the intersection of advanced manufacturing, process control, and spaceflight.

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world.

title: Regional Medical Scientific Director (RMSD) - Gynecologic Malignancies – MD, WV, VA, NC, DC
description:
Job Description

The Regional Medical Scientific Director (Regional Medical Scientific Director) is a credentialed (i.e., PhD, PharmD, DNP, MD) therapeutic and disease expert who engages in bidirectional exchange of scientific or medical information with Scientific Leaders (SLs). The role provides balanced, factual, scientific information about non-product areas of interest to the Company and replies to scientific questions from SLs, including questions about Company products. The work of a Regional Medical Scientific Director is aligned to: Scientific Exchange, Research, Scientific Congress Support, and Scientific Insights. Regional Medical Scientific Directors liaise between the scientific community and the Company to enhance the comprehension of scientific foundations and goals for approved, in-development, and active Company-sponsored trials and/or investigator-sponsored research studies. The Regional Medical Scientific Director serves as a role model for other field medical team members in ways that include on-boarding and/or sharing of therapeutic expertise.

Responsibilities and Primary Activities:

Scientific Exchange

  • Develops professional relationships and engages with national and regional SLs to ensure access to company-approved medical and scientific information on areas of therapeutic interest and Company products

  • Conducts peer-to-peer scientific discussions and maintains a reliable presence with those SLs to ensure they have a medical contact within the company

  • Addresses scientific questions and directs SL inquiries on issues outside of Regional Medical Scientific Director scope (e.g., grants) to appropriate company resources consistent with applicable policies

  • Maintains current knowledge and comprehension of dynamic scientific and clinical environment in the Company's Areas of Interest (AOI) for the Regional Medical Scientific Director’s specific therapeutic area.

Research

  • Upon request from Global Center for Scientific Affairs (GCSA),

  • Initiates discussions with SLs and/or potential investigators that include scientific/data exchange within our AOI to determine the alignment with our research strategies, studies concepts, scientific merit, and qualifications for a specific compound or trial

  • Enhances the comprehension of the scientific foundations and goals of investigator-sponsored research

  • Identifies barriers to patient enrollment and retention efforts to achieve study milestones

  • Upon request from Global Clinical Trial Operations (GCTO),

  • Recommends study sites and identifies potential investigators to participate in phase II-IV clinical development programs, conducts Site Initiation Visits (SIVs), and detects barriers to patient enrollment and retention efforts to achieve study milestones.

  • Protocol leadership responsibilities in collaboration with GCTO

  • Addresses questions from investigators and provides information regarding participation in Company-sponsored clinical studies


Scientific Congress Support

  • Engages in scientific congresses and medical meetings, facilitates scientific and data exchange for both Company and competitor data.

Scientific Insights

  • Gathers feedback, data, or information during routine activities that can help the company better comprehend medical or scientific needs, priorities, or concerns of SLs and/or patients

Inclusive Mindset and Behavior

  • Demonstrates eagerness to contribute to an environment of belonging and empowerment

  • Leads by example and serves as a role model for creating, leading, and retaining workforce

Required Location:

  • This role covers the US states of MD, WV, VA, NC, Washington DC

  • Candidates must reside within the territory.

  • Ability for travel up to 50% within the territory

Required Qualifications, Skills, & Experience:

  • PhD, PharmD, DNP, DO, or MD

  • Proven competence and a minimum of 3 years of relevant therapeutic area experience beyond that obtained in the terminal degree program

  • Ability to conduct doctoral-level discussions with key external stakeholders

  • Dedication to scientific excellence with a strong focus on scientific education and dialogue

  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and networking skills

  • A thorough comprehension of FDA, OIG, HIPAA, and other ethical guidelines, laws, and regulations relevant to the pharmaceutical industry and its customers

  • Ability to organize, prioritize, and work effectively in a constantly changing environment

  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams, OneNote)

  • Familiarity with virtual meeting platforms

  • Desire to contribute to an environment of belonging and empowerment

  • Working to transform the environment, culture, and business landscape

  • Ensure business value, per global strategy

  • Ensuring accountability to drive an inclusive culture

  • Strengthening the foundational elements

  • Consistent adherence to field and corporate policies and Global Medical Scientific Affairs (GMSA) strategy, including field standard operating procedures (SOPs), Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines, and administrative/operational responsibilities

Preferred

  • Field-based medical experience (GYN Oncology experience strongly preferred)

  • Research Experienced

  • Demonstrated record of scientific/medical publication

title: Creative Production Technologist
description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

09

The Team:

The 199 is S&P Global's award-winning in-house creative agency that sets the standard for financial industry storytelling through innovative brand experiences. Our tight-knit, globally distributed team values creative excellence, technical innovation, and collaborative problem-solving, working together to transform complex financial insights into compelling visual narratives. You'll join a dynamic environment where creative vision meets cutting-edge technology, supported by colleagues who encourage continuous learning and professional growth.

Responsibilities and Impact:

The Creative Production Technologist offers a unique opportunity to join a small, dynamic team and be the primary technical owner of our new, state-of-the-art studio in Manhattan. This is a blended role for a creative thinker with a strong technical focus. Your primary responsibility will be managing the technical infrastructure of our studio facilities, which includes a green screen/LED wall virtual production stage, a control room, and a self-contained podcast studio.

While technical management is the focus, you are not afraid to pick up a camera, direct a client, or support a podcast recording. You will work closely with a Senior Producer and Associate Producer in New York, as well as our Technical Director in London serving as the main technical expert for the New York facility while also supporting our global teams. You are a self-starter who relishes learning new things and translating creative, story-driven needs into workable technical realities.

  • Serve as the first point of contact for all studio-related technical requests, ensuring equipment readiness for all productions.

  • Look after all studio systems with remote help from our UK based broadcast engineering support team, including the Ross Ultrix Router, Panasonic Kairos vision mixer, and AdderLink KVM network.

  • Log all technical issues, proactively identifying problems to minimize downtime, and act as the main point of contact with our broadcast support vendors.

  • Take ownership of systems administration, ensuring all technical documentation is orderly and up-to-date on Confluence, including technical drawings and asset registers.

  • Administer video-based SaaS systems, including Riverside.fm, CUEZ, Shade.inc, and others.

  • Oversee vendor administration, contractor logistics, and organize site meetings with Facilities Management.

  • Stay updated on industry trends, particularly in virtual production (both green screen and LED wall), and seek opportunities for continuous professional development.

  • You’ll also get to work alongside our local and global production teams to film and edit engaging, customer-focused video and audio projects.

Compensation/Benefits Information: (This section is only applicable to US candidates)

S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $59,212 to $92,566. Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses, and certifications.

In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive bonus.

What We're Looking For:

Basic Required Qualifications:

  • 3-5 years of experience in corporate or broadcast video production, with hands on technical and video production experience.

  • Must provide a portfolio of exceptional work that demonstrates your technical and creative production skills.

  • A strong understanding of modern broadcast and virtual production technologies. You are not phased by terms like Dante, BitFocus Companion, 1.5mm pixel pitch, 12G SDI, Ultrix Router, ArtNet, and reference sync.

  • Experience in a corporate video, broadcast television, or live production environment, with proficiency in lighting, audio, camerawork, editing, and graphics.

  • A proven ability to work calmly and effectively under pressure.

  • Experience with both Mac and PC environments and familiarity with the Adobe Creative Suite.

  • You’re security-savvy and have experience looking after systems in a corporate IT environment.

  • Good written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills with a high degree of craft and attention to detail.

  • A keen learner and problem-solver who uses initiative to get the job done.

  • This is an onsite role with the expectation to work in office 5 days per week at our 55 Water Street location.

Additional Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Broadcasting, Media Production, Communications, or equivalent technical experience in corporate video or broadcast video environments.

  • Deep knowledge of control systems, specifically BitFocus Companion for system integration.

  • Familiarity with virtual production on green screen and LED walls; concepts like those used at the Brain Bar are not new to you.

  • Expertise in multi-camera video podcast production and remote shooting setups.

  • Experience with camera tracking systems (e.g., MRMC) and gaming engines for production.

Right to Work Requirements:

This role is limited to persons with indefinite right to work in the United States.

We require all external candidates who reach the final stage of our interview process to attend at least one in-person interview, which is ordinarily at your nearest S&P Global office. This must be completed before we can proceed to an offer.

What’s In It For You?

Our Mission:

Advancing Essential Intelligence.

Our People:

We're more than 35,000 strong worldwide—so we're able to understand nuances while having a broad perspective. Our team is driven by curiosity and a shared belief that Essential Intelligence can help build a more prosperous future for us all.From finding new ways to measure sustainability to analyzing energy transition across the supply chain to building workflow solutions that make it easy to tap into insight and apply it. We are changing the way people see things and empowering them to make an impact on the world we live in. We’re committed to a more equitable future and to helping our customers find new, sustainable ways of doing business. Join us and help create the critical insights that truly make a difference.

Our Values:
Integrity, Discovery, Partnership


Throughout our history, the world's leading organizations have relied on us for the Essential Intelligence they need to make confident decisions about the road ahead. We start with a foundation of integrity in all we do, bring a spirit of discovery to our work, and collaborate in close partnership with each other and our customers to achieve shared goals.

Benefits:

We take care of you, so you can take care of business. We care about our people. That’s why we provide everything you—and your career—need to thrive at S&P Global.

Our benefits include:

  • Health & Wellness: Health care coverage designed for the mind and body.

  • Flexible Downtime: Generous time off helps keep you energized for your time on.

  • Continuous Learning: Access a wealth of resources to grow your career and learn valuable new skills.

  • Invest in Your Future: Secure your financial future through competitive pay, retirement planning, a continuing education program with a company-matched student loan contribution, and financial wellness programs.

  • Family Friendly Perks: It’s not just about you. S&P Global has perks for your partners and little ones, too, with some best-in class benefits for families.

  • Beyond the Basics: From retail discounts to referral incentive awards—small perks can make a big difference.

For more information on benefits by country visit: https://spgbenefits.com/benefit-summaries

Global Hiring and Opportunity at S&P Global:

At S&P Global, we are committed to fostering a connected and engaged workplace where all individuals have access to opportunities based on their skills, experience, and contributions. Our hiring practices emphasize fairness, transparency, and merit, ensuring that we attract and retain top talent. By valuing different perspectives and promoting a culture of respect and collaboration, we drive innovation and power global markets.

title: Product Management, AVP - Alpha End-to-End Product Solutions
description:
The Opportunity

State Street Alpha’s End-to-End Product Solutions organization is seeking an Assistant Vice President of Product Strategy, Governance & Reporting Enablement to strengthen how Alpha plans, governs, reports, and communicates its product strategy.

This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who thrives at the intersection of product management, data, technology, and execution. You will own Alpha’s product roadmap and release-note processes, support Service Catalog governance, develop executive and client-facing materials, and build automated reporting solutions that connect product strategy, investment, delivery, and client value.

About the Team

This role sits within the Product Strategy, Planning & Enablement group and works closely with senior leadership across Product, Technology, Finance, Sales, Global Delivery, Alpha Data Services, and Charles River Development.

Key Responsibilities

As AVP of Product Strategy, Governance & Reporting Enablement, you will help provide the structure, data, and reporting required to manage Alpha’s end-to-end product portfolio:

Own the Alpha product roadmap

  • Lead the quarterly collection, validation, and publication of product roadmaps across Alpha service families
  • Maintain internal, executive, sales, and client-facing roadmap views
  • Coordinate roadmap content across Alpha Services, Alpha Data Services, and Charles River Development

Lead roadmap and reporting automation

  • Develop scalable Power BI, Jira, Excel, SharePoint, and Power Platform solutions
  • Connect strategic initiatives to product features, funding, delivery milestones, applications, and client demand
  • Improve data quality, reporting consistency, and historical tracking
  • Replace manual presentation and reporting processes with governed, repeatable workflows

Manage release notes and product communications

  • Lead the quarterly Alpha release-note process
  • Reconcile roadmap commitments against completed delivery
  • Convert technical releases into concise client and business-impact narratives
  • Coordinate leadership review, publication, and organization-wide distribution

Support product investment and financial analysis

  • Analyze business cases, product features, capabilities, estimates, approved funding, and impacted applications
  • Build reporting at the business-case, feature, service-family, client, and application levels
  • Support annual planning, budget scenarios, funding prioritization, and product P&L analysis
  • Partner with Finance and product leadership to improve investment visibility and decision-making
  • Lead product P&L analysis; develop and refine methodologies for allocating product revenue, expenses, and investment across Alpha service families

Support Service Catalog governance

  • Coordinate governance meetings, agendas, materials, decisions, and action items
  • Review catalog changes with product owners and cross-functional stakeholders
  • Maintain clear standards for service capabilities, offerings, and supporting documentation
  • Improve transparency and auditability through structured governance workflows

Develop executive and client-facing materials

  • Prepare materials for executive meetings, QBRs, Client Advisory Boards, product offsites, and client presentations
  • Distill complex product, financial, and technical information into clear executive narratives
  • Create polished visualizations, dashboards, and decision-support materials
  • Support rapid-turnaround strategic requests from senior leadership

Drive continuous improvement of cross-functional product operations

  • Coordinate initiatives across Product, Technology, Finance, Sales, Global Delivery, and Client Solutions
  • Organize product forums, town halls, offsites, and strategic planning sessions
  • Document processes and build sustainable operating models
  • Reduce manual effort while improving reporting speed, accuracy, and usability
  • Track decisions, owners, dependencies, and action items through completion
  • Coach and coordinate analysts and junior team members supporting reporting and automation

What We’re Looking For

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, economics, finance, technology, information systems, or equivalent experience
  • Experience in product operations, business analysis, portfolio reporting, governance, or financial-services technology
  • Strong ability to translate complex product and financial data into compelling executive and client narratives
  • Proficiency with Power BI, including Power Query, DAX, data modeling, and dashboard development
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint
  • Experience with Jira, Jira Analytics, Jira Product Discovery, Confluence, Power BI, including dashboard development. SharePoint, other Microsoft 365 tools and Co-pilot suite
  • Understanding of product roadmaps, development lifecycles, funding processes, and governance
  • Proven ability to influence stakeholders across functions and organizational levels
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to reconcile information across multiple systems
  • Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, matrixed environment
  • Experience in investment servicing, asset-management technology, or front-to-back financial platforms is preferred
  • Familiarity with State Street Alpha, Alpha Services, Alpha Data Platform, or Charles River

$65,000 - $113,750 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

description:

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is a trusted provider of mission-enabling solutions for global security. Our Engineering and Sciences (E&S) organization pushes the boundaries of innovation, redefines engineering capabilities, and drives advances in various sciences. Our team is chartered with providing the skills, innovative technologies to develop, design, produce and sustain optimized product lines across the sector while providing a decisive advantage to the warfighter. Come be a part of our mission!

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems' Baltimore and Partnered Sites (BaPs) division is seeking a Staff Systems Engineer to join our team of qualified and diverse individuals. This position supports the Advanced Radar Systems (ARS) business unit. This position will be located in Baltimore, MD.

What You’ll get to Do:

  • Customer and program management office (PMO) point of contact for all systems integration & test activities regarding technical details and effort progression
  • Managing technical experts and subordinates, ensuring team has resources required to complete tasks
  • Lead integration, testing & troubleshooting for radar systems engineering program(s) including mode integration and flight test, qualification test, acceptance testing, and design verification testing
  • Drive technical decisions and issue resolutions, as well as manage risks and opportunities
  • Support cross-functional engineering teams during proposal, design, manufacturing, and delivery phases of products in development and production phases
  • Supporting proposal development and new program acquisition efforts
  • Interpret statements of work assigned by program leadership
  • Interface with functional departments to secure team staffing
  • Work with suppliers and be able to articulate project requirements

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science in a STEM discipline with 12 years of experience; or 10 years of relevant experience with a Masters degree; or 7 years of relevant experience with a Ph.D. 4 additional years may be considered in lieu of a degree
  • U.S Citizenship with active DoD Secret Clearance or higher
  • Expert in leading a multi-disciplinary team environment
  • Expert verbal and written communication skills to effectively communicate internally and external team members
  • Strong understanding of Systems Engineering concepts, including requirements analysis and verification planning and execution
  • Knowledge and experience with RF Hardware and test equipment
  • Knowledge and experience with Agile principles, tools, and implementation
  • Ability to qualify for program access based on customer requirements (SAP/SAR)

title: VIE Consumer Insights Analyst
description:
What is a VIE?

It’s an international graduate program for European citizens having graduated from a University School. This is an initiative created, designed, and supported by the French Government primarily to provide professional international work experience for European citizens aged between 18-28 recently graduated from University or Business School.

To apply for this V.I.E assignment you need to fulfil the following criteria:

  • International Graduates (European citizens) between 18 - 28 yo with an average of 12 months of professional experience

  • Higher education level (master’s degree)

  • Fluent in English

  • International profile (work experience or studies abroad)

  • Eager to continue your career abroad

This is a V.I.E position based in Stockholm, Sweden and lasts 12 months with possibility for extension of another 12 months. The position is not open to applicants already based in Stockholm, Sweden.

For more information on the V.I.E program’s specificities please visit Mon Volontariat International : site officiel du V.I.E | V.I.A (businessfrance.fr)

ABOUT US

The Absolut Company oversees the production, packaging and marketing of Absolut Vodka, Kahlúa and Malibu as part of the Pernod Ricard Group, a global leader in spirits and wine. Based in Stockholm, Sweden, and part of Pernod Ricard’s Crystal Brand Unit, we uphold the Group’s commitment to excellence by offering some of the world’s most renowned and enduring spirits.

We aim to redefine the global spirits market by inspiring people from all backgrounds to connect, share ideas and enjoy our products responsibly. We are also committed to long-term sustainability, acting in the best interests of consumers, society, the environment and our employees.

We seek talented, bold individuals to join our team and drive innovation. After all, our brands are defined by lifestyle and mindset, but it is our people who define who we are. So, whether you are just starting your career or looking to take it to the next level, we offer a dynamic and supportive work environment that will help you grow.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Starting in December 2026, this V.I.E position is based in Stockholm, Sweden and lasts 12 months with possibility for extension of another 12 months.

The Global Consumer Insights role in the Crystal Brand Unit exists to support and work with the Absolut Global Insights Manager working as a strategic business partner to the Absolut Brand Team, leveraging consumer understanding to guide and challenge strategy, planning & activation development.

In addition, the role will help drive Consumer Centricity, a key ingredient in The Pernod Ricard brand building model, across the business by putting consumers and shoppers at the heart of all decision making. As such, this role is an ambassador for the consumer and shopper voice, both in and externally.

Ultimately, they will develop and share actionable insights & enhance consumer knowledge, leading, and partnering with Marketing / Brand teams to unlock new approaches / frameworks for insights adoption.

KEY TASKS & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Contribute to the development of Absolut’s long-term ambition and strategy based on robust consumer, shopper and category insights

  • Help identify innovation opportunities based on consumer insights

  • Support the Brand Team in testing and validating the global portfolio strategy, leading communications campaigns, winning brand concepts, packaging, design, format innovation, wetgoods, and optimal portfolio ranges with consumers

  • Actively engage in industry research and trends, anticipating future consumers or market needs and share those insights and learnings throughout the team

  • Help manage our Absolut Consumer Councils to gain valuable qualitative insights on our initiatives on an ongoing basis

WHY JOIN US

We aspire to foster an authentic, open, challenging and innovative culture that supports your long-term professional development. And so, we have created a working environment at The Absolut Company that allows you to thrive.

We champion inclusion and value different perspectives. We want our people to be their own authentic selves and we are committed to building a workplace that reflects our global consumer base. We are proud to be recognised among Forbes World's Best Employers and Equileap's top 100 Employers for Gender Equality. Conviviality is in our DNA and connects us beyond borders – you will always be welcomed for who you are and the strengths you bring.

This role could be for you if you:

  • Hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification in Marketing, Business, or a quantitative field (e.g. Statistics, Mathematics, Economics)

  • Demonstrate strong analytical skills, with the ability to identify patterns or irregularities in large quantities of data

  • Have experience with social media, including usage and analysis, social listening tools, and website analytics

  • Possess design skills to create easy-to-read reports and real-time dashboards, and effectively showcase insights and data to support the brand team’s understanding

  • Be fluent in English; additional languages are a plus

  • Have experience in project management

OUR OFFER

We want to help you through everyday challenges, encourage you to make healthy choices, take care of your well-being and enjoy work-life balance (we have a great canteen and a well-equipped gym in case you want to shake the day off!). We also provide you with opportunities for professional development and career progression that you’d expect from a global leader in the beverage industry.

Read more about us at Careers | The Absolut Group (theabsolutcompany.com)

APPLICATION

If this role sounds like it is for you, don’t hesitate to apply. As an international company, our working language is English, so please submit your application in English. All new employees are subject to a six-month probationary period and some positions may require a background check.

We look forward to hearing from you.

As a skills-based organisation, we ensure fair processes and equal opportunities. If you need extra support or accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact us. We are here to support you and welcome your application.

title: PT Outbound Freight Handler
description:
As a PT Outbound Freight Handler, you will load and unload freight onto and off of equipment, as well as assist in the recouping of damaged freight.

Prepare, sweep, inspect and cleans trailer(s) before loading freight. Use safe lifting techniques to properly load and unload freight. Select and use proper freight handling equipment to load and unload freight. Such equipment may include forklifts with appropriate hardware, hand trucks, drum trucks, pallet jacks, rollers, and any other available equipment to move, load, arrange, rearrange, and unload freight. Weigh and dimension shipments to ensure proper classification, freight rating, and safe handling. Plan cube utilization and proper weight distribution when loading freight. Count and inspect the condition of freight, documenting any shortages or damage. Review freight bills for special instructions. Check manifests for existing exceptions and check the label and the destination code on manifests against freight bills. Check for special instructions, weight distributions on headloads, and check headloads against the freight bills when loading freight. Verify the hazardous material product description, determine any discrepancies in the paperwork, and verify proper placarding when loading hazardous material. Properly block and brace freight to prevent shifting during transport.

For this role, we prefer you have a High School Diploma or GED. You must have the ability to satisfactorily pass a background check and an alcohol and drug test. We would prefer for you to have prior experience as a Forklift Operator, Dock or Warehouse Worker, or Material Handler. We would also prefer you to have previously held a Forklift Certification. title: Summer 2027 Intern: AI Enablement & Forward-Deployed Engineering
description:
About Us

Live Oak Bank is a digital bank that serves small business owners across the country. Our groundbreaking spin on service and technology has fueled our mission to be America’s Small Business Bank. Our products help customers buy, build, and expand their business, and our high-yield savings and CD products help them grow their hard-earned money. At Live Oak, we never lose sight of the well-being of our people. We believe our employees are the heart of our company. Our commitment to our customers and culture is intertwined, and we seek those who embody and embrace what it takes to empower the American dream.

Ready to make an impact? We're looking for an intern to join our team for the onsite 10-week Summer 2027 Internship Program (May 17 - July 23, 2027) at our headquarters in Wilmington, NC. Applications are due by 11:59 p.m. ET on Wednesday, September 23.

How This Role Impacts Live Oak and Its People

Live Oak is putting AI in the hands of every employee, not just engineers. That creates a gap most banks never staff: someone who can sit with a lending team for two days, understand what actually slows them down, and leave behind a working solution — then turn around and teach forty people how to build the next one themselves.

This internship is that gap. You will spend the summer embedded with real teams across the bank, building AI solutions alongside them and making the people around you more capable than they were before you arrived. You will ship things employees use, and you will strengthen the AI champions and skills librarians who carry this work forward after you leave.

We hire interns who build. Ex: a successful 2026 intern was a business major who had founded a company, shipped production websites for paying clients, and used AI as core infrastructure rather than a novelty.

What You'll Do at Live Oak

Forward-Deployed Engineering — roughly half your time

  • Embed with business teams across lending, deposits, credit, and operations to find the workflows where AI removes real friction — then build the solution with them, not for them.
  • Ship working tools fast using Claude, Claude Code, Power Automate, and low-code platforms. Prototype in days, not quarters. Expect what you build to be in real use before your first month ends.
  • Translate between worlds by turning a lender's challenge into a scoped problem statement, and turning a technical constraint into language a business leader can act on.
  • Document what you build so the team maintains it after you leave. A solution that dies when the intern leaves was never a solution.

Enablement & Training — roughly a third of your time

  • Support our AI champions and skills librarians by enhancing the training materials, reusable skills, and internal documentation they need to scale adoption inside their own business units.
  • Run hands-on training for employees at every level — from people who have never opened an AI tool to power users who want to build their own agents.
  • Create artifacts that outlast the session including prompt libraries, reusable skills, quick-reference guides, and short video walkthroughs.

Support & Measurement — the remainder

  • Field questions and unblock employees on our enterprise AI tools. Every recurring question is a signal about missing training or missing tooling; you will spot the pattern and close the gap.
  • Measure whether any of this is working by defining and tracking adoption, usage, and time-saved metrics so leadership can tell genuine impact apart from enthusiasm.
  • Bring back what you find in a summer-end readout to senior leadership: where AI is creating value at Live Oak, where it is stalling, and what you would do next.

Required

  • Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program
  • A portfolio, GitHub, or set of shipped projects you can walk us through. Side businesses, automations, websites, bots, and tools you built
  • Demonstrated fluency with AI tools as part of how you work — not just as something you have tried. Be ready to show us the last thing you built with one.
  • Ability to write and speak clearly to non-technical people.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and self-direction.

Preferred

  • Experience building with modern web or automation stacks.
  • Experience teaching, tutoring, mentoring, or leading a team — formally or otherwise.
  • Exposure to a regulated industry, or real curiosity about why banks work the way they do. Understanding the constraint is what makes a solution usable.
  • Enough data analysis ability to build a measurement framework and defend the numbers in it.

    #LI-DNI

Our Values

  • Dedication: Possess a deep commitment to Live Oak Bank’s mission and core values, exemplified through a strong work ethic, adaptability and pride in your work.

  • Ownership: Take initiative to deliver positive results by proactively and creatively solving problems, while maintaining a high degree of quality.

  • Respect: Treat everyone with courtesy, politeness, and kindness.

  • Innovation: Embrace fresh ideas and fearlessly contribute new solutions to emerging or existing problems.

  • Teamwork: Foster collaboration, accountability, and trust with others and understand that together, we do more

For a detailed overview of our employee benefits please visit:

Equal access to programs, service and employment is available to all persons.   • Participating in occasional travel for in-person instruction and live procedure coverage.

title: [MSO] Senior OpenStack Engineer
description:
Project – the aim you’ll have

You will join an internal OpenStack team that designs, deploys and operates private and sovereign cloud platforms for enterprise clients in Western Europe, including a Benelux managed service provider exiting VMware. Environments range from multi region platforms across several data centres to compact telco and edge clusters. Key selling points: you own the architecture, the same team operates the platform afterwards, and you cooperate directly with client architects.

Role – how you’ll contribute

  • Own the platform architecture across control plane, compute, storage and network, including the high availability model and resource sizing.
  • Produce the design documentation: High Level Design, Low Level Design, as built documentation and operational runbooks.
  • Deploy and upgrade the platform with Kolla-Ansible, with configuration maintained as code in Git.
  • Integrate storage, networking, identity and load balancing: Cinder, OVN and Open vSwitch, Keystone with OIDC federation, Octavia and Barbican.
  • Set up metrics and logging, and integrate the platform with the client ServiceNow CMDB.
  • Run technical workshops, design reviews and acceptance testing with client representatives.
  • Act as third line escalation for platforms under management and lead root cause analysis.
  • Support pre sales as technical expert and provide technical guidance to engineers in the team.

    Expectations – the experience you need

    • At least 6 years in infrastructure, virtualisation or cloud platforms, including 3 years with OpenStack in production.
    • Experience designing OpenStack architecture, with at least one full implementation from design to production handover.
    • Strong command of the core services: Nova, Neutron, Keystone, Glance, Cinder, Placement and Horizon, plus Octavia and Barbican.
    • Deployment and upgrade experience with Kolla-Ansible, including playbook customisation and containerised service lifecycle.
    • Advanced Linux administration, KVM and libvirt virtualisation, and container runtimes such as Docker.
    • Troubleshooting experience across MariaDB or Galera, RabbitMQ, HAProxy, Keepalived, Redis and Memcached.
    • Solid cloud networking background: OVN and Open vSwitch, GENEVE or VXLAN overlays, VLAN provider networks, NAT and floating IP addresses.
    • English at C1 level, sufficient to run technical workshops and design reviews with client architects independently.

    Additional skills – the edge you have

    • VMware exit and migration programmes towards OpenStack, including migration tooling and wave planning.
    • Enterprise storage integration through Cinder drivers, for example NetApp ONTAP over NFS, or Ceph.
    • Telco workloads on OpenStack: SR-IOV, DPDK, CPU pinning, huge pages and NUMA aware scheduling.
    • Terraform or OpenTofu, Kubernetes on OpenStack, GPU enabled compute nodes.
    • ServiceNow, in particular ITOM Discovery and the CMDB model, or experience in an ITIL based service model.
    • Familiarity with sovereign cloud regulatory requirements in the public sector and financial services.

      • Flexible and remote cooperation options
      • International projects with leading global clients
      • Travels related to international projects
      • Non-corporate atmosphere
      • Access* to language classes
      • Access* to knowledge-sharing initiatives
      • Access* to private healthcare and life insurance

title: Associate Scientist or Scientist- dos Santos's Lab
description:
Join our Team!

The dos Santos laboratory in the Department of Oncology at St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital is seeking a highly motivated Associate Scientist or Scientist to support and advance research investigating cancer initiation and progression, epithelial–stromal interactions, and systemic influences on cancer risk.

The successful candidate will provide scientific and technical leadership for animal-model and organoid-based studies. This individual will work closely with the principal investigator, trainees, research staff, and institutional shared-resource teams to design, execute, analyze, and document rigorous experiments. The position is intended for an experienced scientist who can independently manage complex projects while also helping laboratory members troubleshoot experiments, implement new approaches, and maintain high standards of reproducibility and animal welfare.

The selected candidate will be appointed at the Associate Scientist or Scientist level, based on their experience, demonstrated scientific independence, technical expertise, and leadership achievements.

Who We’re Looking For

  • Demonstrated experience with mouse models and animal experimentation.

  • Experience with primary cell culture, three-dimensional culture, organoids, or tissue-derived experimental systems.

  • Strong understanding of experimental design, biological controls, reproducibility, and quantitative data interpretation.

  • Ability to independently plan, execute, troubleshoot, and document complex experiments.

  • Strong organizational and oral-communication skills.


What You Will Do

Animal Studies

  • Design, coordinate, and execute studies using genetically engineered, syngeneic, transplantation, and treatment-based mouse models of mammary gland biology and breast cancer.

  • Manage mouse breeding strategies, cohort generation, genotyping plans, experimental randomization, and longitudinal monitoring.

  • Perform or oversee animals procedure and tissue collection

  • Develop and maintain detailed experimental timelines and animal-cohort records.

  • Assist with preparation, implementation, and amendment of IACUC protocols.

  • Ensure compliance with institutional animal-welfare policies, biosafety requirements, and approved experimental procedures.

  • Support the training of laboratory personnel in relevant animal procedures and confirm technical competency.

Organoid and Ex Vivo Models

  • Establish, maintain, and optimize primary mammary epithelial and tumor organoid cultures from mouse and human specimens.

  • Design and conduct organoid assays evaluating growth, differentiation, lineage plasticity, hormone response, extracellular-matrix interactions, and therapeutic sensitivity.

  • Develop co-culture systems incorporating fibroblasts, immune cells, extracellular-matrix components, or other microenvironmental populations.

  • Perform organoid-forming, branching, invasion, viability, differentiation, and drug-response assays.

Molecular, Cellular, and Tissue Analysis

  • Perform or supervise molecular and cellular assays, including flow cytometry, immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, microscopy, quantitative image analysis, western blotting, qPCR, ELISA, and related approaches.

  • Support thre preparation of high-quality specimens for bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial profiling, epigenomic assays, proteomics, and other molecular analyses.

  • Maintain detailed, accurate, and reproducible experimental records.

Scientific and Project Leadership

  • Collaborate with the principal investigator to develop experimental strategies, establish project priorities, and evaluate feasibility.

  • Analyze and interpret data using appropriate statistical and computational methods.

  • Identify technical or conceptual problems and develop practical solutions.

  • Present findings at laboratory meetings, departmental seminars, and collaborative meetings.

  • Promote communication and coordination among laboratory members and external collaborators.

Minimum Education and/or Training:

  • Bachelor's degree in relevant scientific areas such as cancer biology, cell biology, molecular biology, developmental biology, biomedical sciences, or a related discipline is required.

  • PhD, or equivalent doctoral degree strongly preferred.

Scientist Minimum Experience:

  • Eight (8) years of relevant work experience is required

  • Six (6) years of relevant work experience is required with a Master's degree

  • Three (3) years of relevant work experience is required with a PhD

Salary range: $86,320.00 - $154,960.00

Associate Scientist Minimum Experience:

  • 7 + years of research experience is required

  • 5 + years of research experience is required with a Master’s degree

  • 2 + years of research experience is required with a PHD

Salary range: $65,520.00 - $114,400.00

title: Medic - Hospital at Home - Days/Evenings
description:
VCU Health at Home delivers mobile, integrated health services as part of its Continuum Integration service line to enhance the patient experience by providing comprehensive, safe and efficient in-home care as an alternative to an emergency department visit or bricks and mortar hospitalization. The Home Hospital Medic for VCU Health at Home is an interdependent member of the care team who is responsible for performing comprehensive assessments, diagnostic testing and medical treatments in a patient’s home or current residence. The practice of the Home Health Medic is focused on longitudinal assessment, participation in an existing, multidisciplinary, interprofessional treatment plan; communication with and referral to other members of the treatment team based on changing patient needs are essential functions.

Essential Job functions:

A leader in the provision of mobile healthcare using patient-centered resources in the out-of-hospital environment, the Home Health Medic examines, screens, treats, performs diagnostics, and coordinates health services for patients in the VCUMC Home Hospital program.

Performs under the direct supervision of the Nurse Manager to ensure quality care during daily in-person visits to patients receiving acute care at home through Home Hospital which includes daily assessments, vital sign monitoring, and patient education; lab draws, wound care, and medication administration may also be necessary and will be closely coordinated with the Home Hospital nursing and provider teams.

Provides quality acute/inpatient level of virtual support to the Home Hospital healthcare team if needed including triage of calls, virtual medication administration, virtual visits, telephone outreaches, education, and escalation of services both clinical and non-clinical.

Provides high level clinical care through the ability to perform phone and in-person triage and intervene or escalate appropriately using critical thinking skills for both inpatients and complex adult and/or geriatric patient populations.

Ensures acute inpatient individuals are receiving appropriate services during their Home Hospital stay including but not limited to therapy, food, consultative, mobile imaging, labs, and medical equipment to prevent un-necessary hospital readmissions.

Using strong communication skills, provides patient/caregiver education and ensures patients and/or caregivers are confident and comfortable in self-care management through use of in-person or virtual teach back education strategies.

Provides quality patient care and education in accordance with VCUMC Home Hospital policies and state regulations, as approved by the Medical Directors of Home Hospital and professional standards of care.

Provides accurate and legible documentation of patient care with attention to detail to accurately reflect assessment and interventions.

Maintains the ability to understand, utilize and efficiently integrate technology for longitudinal patient assessment, clinical interventions, physician consults and data collection related to paramedicine.

Performs other duties as assigned and/or participates in special projects in order to support the mission of VCUHS and department. Provides assistance to team members. Accepts alternate assignments, as required, graciously.

title: Supply Chain Coordinator
description:
Job Title:

Supply Chain Coordinator


Location:

Irving, Texas


Compensation:

Pay is commensurate with experience.


Worker Type:

Employee


Time Type:

Full time


Job Description:

The Supply Chain Coordinator supports Team Car Care's field network of Jiffy Lube service centers by managing the day-to-day purchasing lifecycle across store-level supplies, bulk fluids, equipment, and outside services. This role is the primary point of contact between stores, distributors/vendors, and the Procurement team, ensuring purchase orders are accurate, requisitions are properly managed, delivery and billing issues are resolved quickly, and vendor contracts and catalogs are kept current. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, comfortable managing a high volume of transactional requests, and skilled at coordinating across store operations, facilities, and outside suppliers.


Key Responsibilities
Purchase Order & Requisition Management

  • Review, approve, and process purchase orders (POs) and change orders submitted through Workday for store equipment, parts, and supplies.
  • Monitor and process weekly Auto Ordering requisitions; identify and cancel duplicate, stale, or unneeded requisitions across stores (mass cancellations).
  • Investigate and resolve PO discrepancies flagged by vendors (pricing mismatches, duplicate orders, order confirmations) before releasing for fulfillment.
  • Coordinate change orders with vendors to prevent full PO resubmission and unnecessary reprocessing.

Vendor & Distributor Coordination

  • Serve as day-to-day liaison with fuel/lubricant distributors (e.g., Shell/Pennzoil), parts suppliers (e.g., O'Reilly, AutoZone), equipment vendors (e.g., Samson Corporation), and other national account partners.
  • Resolve delivery exceptions — refused deliveries, cancelled or backordered items, low-stock/urgent fill escalations from stores — working directly with distributors and store/DM contacts.
  • Troubleshoot vendor billing and remittance issues (e.g., unapplied payments, account holds) in partnership with Accounts Payable and the vendor.
  • Support contract and rate negotiations for outside services (e.g., landscaping/snow removal vendors), including reviewing SOWs and proposed agreements alongside Facilities.

Catalog, Systems & Data Management

  • Maintain and update the Workday procurement punchout catalog, including restricting discontinued or unavailable SKUs to prevent store ordering errors.
  • Monitor tank/inventory levels and coordinate on equipment issues such as tank leaks and tank replacements.
  • Pull and prepare ad hoc reports for procurement and operations leadership (e.g., YTD spend, cost comparisons for capital projects, store staffing/headcount data).
  • Track vendor fill reports and store status changes (e.g., temporary closures for remodel) that affect ordering and delivery.

Cross-Functional Support

  • Partner with Facilities & Capital Projects, Store Operations, District/Regional Managers, and RVPs to resolve store level procurement issues.
  • Support special projects and initiatives on behalf of the Director of Procurement (e.g., vendor onboarding, employee recognition/gift fulfillment logistics, ad hoc team requests).
  • Respond to internal procurement questions from store and field teams regarding ordering processes, system access, and vendor account setup.

Qualifications

  • 1–3+ years of experience in procurement, purchasing, supply chain, or a related operations/analyst role; multi-unit retail or automotive services experience a plus.
  • Experience with an ERP/procurement platform (Workday preferred) and purchase order workflows.
  • Strong Excel skills; comfortable working with vendor data, cost reports, and spend analysis.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to manage competing requests from stores, vendors, and leadership simultaneously.
  • High attention to detail and strong follow-through on open items (POs, tickets, vendor escalations).
  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, high-volume environment with frequent day-to-day problem solving.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, or related field preferred, or equivalent experience.

What Success Looks Like

  • POs and requisitions are accurate, timely, and free of unnecessary duplication or cancellations.
  • Store-level delivery and billing issues are resolved quickly with minimal disruption to operations.
  • Vendor catalogs and systems reflect current product availability and pricing.
  • Procurement leadership and store teams view the Analyst as a responsive, reliable point of contact.

Team Car Care does not offer support or sponsorship of job applicants for employment-based visas or any other work authorization for this role now or in the future. You must have the right to work in the United States and not require Team Car Care support or sponsorship for immigration-related employment now or in the future.

This position is based at the Team Car Care Headquarters in Irving, TX, with onsite work Tuesday-Thursday and remote work on Mondays and Fridays.

WHAT IS KIDSTRONG?
At KidStrong, we help parents build stronger, smarter, more athletic kids. KidStrong is a milestone accelerator for kids walking through 11 years old. We help parents discover their child’s superpowers and build future-ready kids who are confident making friends running the playground and raising their hands high in the classroom.   • Joining a workplace where you can be part of a fun, energetic, and professional team that loves what they do!
  • Coaching and mentoring children to make an impact on their lives!
  • Teaching parents how to make their children smarter, stronger, and more confident!
  • Having flexibility for a part-time or full-time schedule
The KidStrong Childrens Coach - Role and Schedule Details:
  • We are looking for a coach with athletic or coaching experience who ideally has experience coaching kids ages 12 months to 11 years old.
  • KidStrong Coach would focus on coaching children on brain, physical, and character development that stems from the evolving monthly curriculum
  • The ideal candidate must also be comfortable speaking to parents/guardians regarding “the why” behind the KidStrong curriculum
  • Our classes run typically weekdays, 9 am -11 am and evenings until 7 pm, and weekends are typically from 8 am through lunch/noon.

  • Additional opportunity to increase scheduled hours through private party coaching hours.
  • Prior experience as a pediatric OT/PT is a plus but not required!

  • Coach class sizes of 6 to 15 children, age groups range from roughly 12 months old to 11 years old
  • Teach the KidStrong curriculum as provided by the HQ programming team
  • Must be able to ensure classes both start and end on schedule and follow the appropriate pace of curriculum
  • Greet students as well as the parent(s)/guardian(s) individually prior to and at the beginning of class
  • Maintain a dynamic, fun, motivational, and professional demeanor when leading the class
  • Demonstrate and manage the implementation of various exercises
  • Ensure cleanliness of the center, including the lobby, bathrooms, and blue floors - this includes taking out the trash, sweeping and mopping, wiping down equipment, and sanitizing the mat at the end of a shift
  • Effectively use the KS Coach’s App to record class data and provide records of data for parents (attendance, awards, etc.)
  • Communicate professionally with co-workers in Slack, our company messaging system, including periodic checks of messages when not in centers
  • Complete training through FranConnect as required by the HQ Training and Certification team
  • Must be able to work in a physically intensive environment - coaches may cover multiple miles in a shift moving through class, lifting and repeatedly moving equipment up to 25 pounds in weight.
  • Must be comfortable working "hands-on" with kids to ensure proper technique and ensure student safety.
  • Assist parents of students ages three and younger with the direction and flow of a class

The Northrop Grumman Classified Solutions team is seeking a Classified Cybersecurity Analyst to support information system lifecycle activities. The selected candidate will be required to work on-site, full-time at our [City, State] location.

The responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Conduct system audits and continuous monitoring activities, covering all security controls, configurations, and operational processes to evaluate the security posture of the information systems.

  • Perform assessments of systems and networks within the networking environment or enclave and identify where those systems and networks deviate from acceptable configurations, enclave policy, or local policy.

This includes process support, analysis, coordination, security certification testing, security documentation, investigations, software research, hardware introduction and release, emerging‑technology research, inspections, and periodic audits.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity or related field

  • Experience in cybersecurity compliance (ex., Assessment & Authorization under RMF)

  • Top Secret, SAP/SAR access, SCI access, and/or a Polygraph

  • Knowledge of security tools such as ACAS, Nessus, Splunk, Trellix, and SCAP

  • Knowledge of security frameworks and documentation such as NIST, JSIG, DAAG, SSPs, POA&Ms, and SCTMs

title: Fuel Technician
description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

POSITION OVERVIEW

A Fuel Technician is responsible for the installation, maintenance, inspection, and repair of fuel storage and dispensing systems. In this role, you’ll work hands-on with underground and above-ground tanks, pumps, dispensers, and monitoring systems to ensure safe and reliable operation. As a key part of the fuel operations team, you will support compliance with all regulatory and environmental standards while minimizing downtime and maximizing efficiency across all assigned locations.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The following and other duties may be assigned as necessary:

  • Performs scheduled and emergency maintenance on fuel dispensers, tank monitors, submersible pumps, and associated systems.
  • Installs, tests, and calibrates fuel equipment and system components in accordance with manufacturer and company specifications.
  • conduct leak detection, line testing, and tank inspections to ensure compliance with EPA and state regulations.
  • Troubleshoots and repairs electrical and mechanical issues related to fuel systems.
  • Completes service orders (SWOs), maintenance logs, and regulatory documentation accurately and in a timely manner.
  • Responds to fuel alarms, spill events, or equipment failures to minimize environmental and operational impact.
  • Works with site personnel to instruct them on the proper use and care of fuel equipment.
  • Assists in equipment upgrades and system retrofits.
  • Maintains parts inventory, tools, and service vehicle in a clean and organized manner.
  • Ensures all work is performed safely and in compliance with company, local, and federal standards.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position does not typically have direct supervisory responsibilities but may mentor junior technicians or assist in training new team members as assigned.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below represent the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • High school diploma or GED required; technical or trade school certification preferred.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in fuel systems maintenance, petroleum equipment service, or a related technical field.
  • Familiarity with dispensers, tank monitors, submersible pumps, and vapor recovery systems.
  • Proficiency with digital multimeters and other diagnostic tools.
  • Ability to read schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical manuals.
  • Experience working with fuel monitoring systems (e.g., Veeder-Root, Incon) is preferred.

title: Technical Program Manager, RFIC and mmWave Development - TeraWave
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based communications with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This multi-orbit constellation will consist of optically interconnected satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO), providing enterprise-grade connectivity for critical operations worldwide.

Blue Origin is seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to lead development and execution of advanced RF/mmWave front-end integrated circuit FEIC programs for TeraWave.

This role will own program execution from early requirements definition through architecture, IC development, tapeout, silicon bring-up, characterization, qualification, OSAT engagement, and production transition. The TPM will collaborate with foundry, product, test and packaging engineers to monitor third-party IP providers, foundry and EDA partners, OSATs, packaging suppliers, test partners, and system stakeholders to ensure FEIC deliverables align with TeraWave product and mission objectives.

The ideal candidate combines formal technical program management discipline with sufficient technical knowledge of RFIC development, semiconductor execution, phased-array systems, and/or satellite communications to credibly lead cross-functional teams, manage complex dependencies, and drive programs from concept to qualified production hardware.

Special Mentions:

- Relocation provided

- Travel expected up to 10% of the time

- Interviews will include a technical assessment

- This role is based on site in San Diego, CA (preferred) or in Cupertino (CA). A temporary remote work exception is approved while our San Diego site is being developed.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead end-to-end technical program execution for TeraWave Q/V-band FEIC developments supporting phased-array antenna and digital beamforming systems.

  • Coordinate internal engineering teams in the execution of various development lifecycle phases from market and mission requirements through tape out, silicon qualification and reliability testing.

  • Build and maintain integrated schedules, milestone plans, deliverables, dependency maps, risk registers, and executive-level program dashboards.

  • Drive alignment between FEIC deliverables and system-level PAA/DBF requirements and production cost.

  • Manage third-party IP deliverables, including technical specifications, licensing, delivery schedules, documentation, integration collateral, verification expectations, support models, and risk mitigation.

  • Drive cross-functional risk management for schedule, resources, technical maturity, supplier performance, foundry readiness, IP availability, test coverage, package performance, qualification, and production ramp.

  • Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, collaboration, technical excellence, and disciplined execution.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, or related technical discipline.

  • 10+ years of formal experience in technical program management, engineering program management, or equivalent technical leadership roles.

  • Experience managing RF IC programs across multiple lifecycle phases, from requirements and architecture through development, validation, qualification, and production.

  • Experience creating and maintaining integrated schedules, risk registers, dependency maps, milestone plans, and executive-level program reporting.

  • Ability to work effectively with highly technical RF, IC, systems, packaging, test, and manufacturing teams.

  • Experience coordinating external partners, vendors, suppliers, foundries, IP providers, OSATs, test houses, or labs.

  • Strong communication, decision-making, stakeholder management, and cross-functional leadership skills.

  • Ability to manage ambiguity, establish structure, and drive closure across complex technical programs.

  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or higher in electrical engineering, or related technical discipline.

  • Experience with Q/V-band, Ka-band, Ku-band, or other microwave/mmWave RF front-end ICs.

  • Experience with FEICs or RFICs used in phased-array antennas, SATCOM user terminals, payloads, radar, or high-frequency communications systems.

  • Experience coordinating third-party IP integration.

  • Experience with RF production test strategy, wafer probe, final test, socketing, load boards, calibration, test correlation, yield ramp, and test time reduction.

  • Knowledge of qualification and reliability standards relevant to aerospace, defense, space, automotive, or high-reliability semiconductor products.

  • PMP, PgMP, Agile, Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent formal program management training/certification.

The Fleet Operations Supervisor plays a key role in ensuring the safe, efficient, and reliable performance of Smithfield’s private fleet. In this role, you will oversee daily fleet operations and provide direct leadership to private fleet staff, ensuring consistent service levels, effective problem resolution, and strong communication across drivers, Smithfield facilities, and corporate teams.   • Fleet Optimization: Analyze and evaluate private fleet operations to identify routing adjustments, network efficiencies, and cost-savings opportunities.

  • Routing & Scheduling: Coordinate and develop daily/weekly routes and schedules to support business needs.

  • Dispatch Management: Oversee the dispatch process, ensuring efficient planning and scheduling of drivers and deliveries to maximize equipment utilization, reduce miles, and meet shipment timelines.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Build and maintain strong working relationships with Transportation, DC/Plant Management, Customer Service, and Supply & Demand Planning teams to resolve scheduling changes and transportation issues.

  • Operational Analysis: Review transportation activity data, identify trends, and recommend or implement improvements to enhance efficiency and reduce cost.

  • Reporting & Performance Tracking: Develop and maintain reporting on transportation metrics, including cost per mile, operating ratio, equipment utilization, driver availability, and delivery performance.

  • Equipment Utilization: Ensure procedures related to equipment operation and utilization are followed; address issues promptly to maintain operational efficiency.

  • Process Improvement & Compliance: Create, maintain, and update operational policies, procedures, and processes to ensure efficiency and regulatory compliance.

  • Driver Performance Management: Optimize performance of assigned drivers, including on-time pickup/delivery, Hours of Service (HOS) compliance, availability, and scheduling alignment.

  • Leadership: Drives a positive employee experience through leadership by way of employee development and coaching.

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited four-year college or university and 2+ years of operational experience in driver management, route planning, and a working understanding of DOT regulations; or equivalent combination of education and experience, required.

  • Leadership: Experience acting as a lead by providing training, coaching or mentoring to less experienced staff or through managing a process or project.

  • Technical Skills: Basic competency with Microsoft Office programs, including Excel, Outlook, and Word.

  • Interpersonal Skills: Ability to work effectively and demonstrate strong interpersonal skills in a cross-functional environment with both internal and external team members.

  • Collaboration & Culture: Ability to work well with others in a fast-paced, dynamic environment; ability to be respectful, approachable, and team-oriented while building strong working relationships and a positive work environment.

description:
