title: Proposal Development Specialist
description:
The Talent Acquisition department hires qualified candidates to fill positions which contribute to the overall strategic success of Howard University. Hiring staff “for fit” makes significant contributions to Howard University’s overall mission.

At Howard University, we prioritize well-being and professional growth.

Here is what we offer:

  • Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus mental health support
  • Work-Life Balance: PTO, paid holidays, flexible work arrangements
  • Financial Wellness: Competitive salary, 403(b) with company match
  • Professional Development: Ongoing training, tuition reimbursement, and career advancement paths
  • Additional Perks: Wellness programs, commuter benefits, and a vibrant company culture

Join Howard University and thrive with us!

JOB FUNCTION

Howard University’s Office of Research is seeking a Proposal Development Specialist as part of the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) team. The Specialist will provide proposal development support to faculty and research team pursuing external funding. The Specialist will also work across Howard’s research enterprise to help investigators transform promising ideas into clear, compelling, sponsor-responsive proposals and build sustainable funding strategies.

This role is well suited for a research development professional, research administrator, or proposal writer who enjoys working across disciplines, engaging directly with faculty, and helping teams communicate the significance and impact of their work. The position offers the opportunity to contribute to proposal development across a broad portfolio of federal and non-federal sponsors while helping strengthen grantsmanship capacity within a dynamic R1 research environment.


NATURE AND SCOPE

  • Serve as a dedicated proposal development contact for an assigned portfolio of schools/colleges, supporting multiple concurrent engagements against sponsor deadlines.
  • Analyze funding opportunities, sponsor priorities, review criteria, and relevant prior awards to help investigators assess fit and position proposals competitively.
  • Consult with faculty from early concept development through proposal refinement, helping translate research ideas into compelling, sponsor-responsive applications.
  • Provide writing, editing, and organizational support for proposal narratives and non-technical proposal components, including project summaries, management plans, mentoring plans, sustainability plans, education and outreach components, data management plans, budget justifications, and interdisciplinary narratives that integrate contributions across disciplines.
  • Develop outlines, writing plans, templates, checklists, and guidance that help investigators organize strong applications and respond fully to sponsor requirements.
  • Review proposal drafts for clarity, organization, consistency, responsiveness to review criteria, and alignment with sponsor expectations, while preserving the author's scholarly voice and technical ownership.
  • Support investigators in developing resubmission strategy, including interpretation of reviewer feedback and development of responsive revision plans.
  • Build sustained working relationships with faculty and researchers and provide individualized consultation on funding mechanisms, proposal readiness, and funding strategy.
  • Identify and share targeted funding opportunities aligned with faculty research interests and goals.
  • Help faculty identify collaborators, institutional resources, and expertise needed to strengthen proposed projects and research teams, and support early-career and established investigators in building competitive external funding portfolios.
  • Facilitate proposal kickoff meetings, concept-development sessions, and writing meetings, and support multidisciplinary and multi-investigator teams through early-stage planning, team organization, and clarification of project goals, investigator roles, and proposal requirements.
  • Contribute to and help deliver workshops, webinars, resources, and other faculty development activities focused on grantsmanship and proposal competitiveness.
  • Contribute to RDI programs such as the Proposal Development Institute, Research Grants Academy, sponsor information sessions, and other faculty-facing initiatives, including sessions and campus visits involving funding agency representatives.
  • Contribute to and maintain reusable proposal development resources, templates, guides, and FAQs, and to unit-level funding opportunity briefings and limited-submission announcements.
  • Collaborate closely with Research Development colleagues, College Research Administrators, schools/colleges, and Sponsored Programs/Pre-Award staff to provide coordinated service to investigators.
  • Support structured internal peer review and provide proposal development support to faculty applicants in intramural funding programs and limited-submission competitions.
  • Maintain current knowledge of proposal preparation requirements and funding trends across federal, foundation, and other sponsors relevant to the assigned portfolio.
  • Maintain records of faculty engagements in designated systems and track submission activity and funding outcomes for the assigned portfolio, preparing periodic activity and outcome reports.

PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES

  • Provide high-quality, timely, and faculty-centered proposal development support for an assigned portfolio while handling multiple concurrent engagements and sponsor deadlines.
  • Work collaboratively across Research Development, schools/colleges, Sponsored Programs/Pre-Award, and other Office of Research units to support clear roles, effective handoffs, and coordinated service to investigators.
  • Apply sponsor guidance, review criteria, and research development best practices to strengthen the competitiveness and responsiveness of proposals.
  • Support the integration of all proposal components and help confirm that assigned proposals are complete and responsive to sponsor solicitation requirements in advance of institutional review and submission by Sponsored Programs/Pre-Award.
  • Maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment in handling pre-submission concepts, proposal materials, reviewer feedback, and other sensitive information.
  • Contribute to an RDI culture of collaboration, knowledge sharing, continuous improvement, and commitment to faculty and institutional research success.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

CORE COMPETENCIES

  • Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to translate complex research concepts for varied audiences.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to interpret complex sponsor requirements and identify implications for proposal strategy.
  • Intellectual curiosity and the ability to engage effectively with research across multiple disciplines.
  • Strong consultation and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility with faculty, researchers, and research teams.
  • Ability to provide constructive, tactful, and actionable feedback on proposal concepts and written materials.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, including the ability to handle multiple concurrent proposal engagements and deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team-based research development environment.
  • Ability to build consensus and work effectively across academic and administrative boundaries without direct supervisory authority.
  • Strong service orientation and commitment to faculty success, research competitiveness, and institutional research growth.
  • Sound judgment, discretion, professionalism, and attention to detail in handling confidential proposal and institutional information.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and collaborative document platforms, and the ability to learn and effectively use funding databases, sponsor systems, and institutional research administration tools.

WHY JOIN HOWARD

Howard University offers the opportunity to work within a broad, interdisciplinary research enterprise and to contribute directly to faculty success and institutional research growth. The Proposal Development Specialist will engage with investigators across disciplines, build relationships throughout the University, and help strengthen the competitiveness and impact of externally funded research and sponsored programs.

Howard University offers a comprehensive benefits package, professional development opportunities, and a collaborative environment committed to excellence in research, education, and service.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
  • At least three years of progressively responsible experience in research development, proposal development, grant writing, research administration, scientific or technical writing, sponsored programs, or a related field, including experience with federally sponsored programs.
  • Demonstrated experience developing, writing, editing, reviewing, or coordinating federally funded proposals, other externally funded proposals, or complex professional, scientific, or technical documents.
  • Ability to interpret funding announcements and translate sponsor requirements into clear guidance and actionable proposal development plans.
  • Experience working collaboratively with faculty, researchers, technical professionals, or other subject-matter experts.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master's degree, PhD, or other advanced degree.
  • Experience in a research-intensive university, academic medical center, federal funding agency, foundation, national laboratory, research institute, or similar research environment.
  • Experience supporting proposals across multiple federal agencies (e.g., NIH, NSF, DoD, DOE, NASA, HRSA, USDA, NEH, IES), as well as foundation, industry, or state sponsors.
  • Experience supporting interdisciplinary, multi-investigator, training, instrumentation, or other complex proposal mechanisms.
  • Experience providing substantive proposal editing, grantsmanship coaching, faculty consultation, or training.
  • Familiarity with funding databases and proposal/research administration systems such as Pivot, InfoReady, Grants.gov, Research.gov, eRA Commons, or institutional electronic research administration and routing systems such as Cayuse.

COMPLIANCE SALARY RANGE DISCLOSURE

  • Department: Office of Research / Research Development and Innovation
  • Employment Type: Full-time, Exempt
  • Location: Howard University, Washington, DC
  • Expected Pay Range: $72,727 - $80,000

Compliance Salary Range Disclosure

As a member of our non-profit organization, you can be impact-inspired to provide vital clinical services to communities nationwide, vital products to those in need of a donor's generosity, or vital scientific research that advances blood safety worldwide.

Job Description:

Bring your expertise to work that helps make a difference.

At Vitalant, our work is more than laboratory testing—it’s part of a larger mission to help save and improve lives. As a Clinical Laboratory Specialist in our HLA Laboratory, you’ll perform high-complexity clinical laboratory testing and provide skilled technical support to help deliver accurate, timely and high-quality results.

You’ll join a collaborative laboratory team where precision, quality and continuous improvement are essential to the work we do and the patients and healthcare partners we serve. The position is classified as CLIA high-complexity testing personnel.

What You Can Expect

Work Location: Phoenix, AZ
Schedule: Wednesday–Sunday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Scheduled Days Off: Monday & Tuesday
Hourly Pay Range: $26.39–$34.84/hour, depending on experience
Weekend Shift Differential: 8%

What You’ll Do

As a Clinical Laboratory Specialist, you’ll perform routine testing of biological specimens while providing skilled technical support and working with other team members to ensure timely, quality test results.

In this role, you will:

  • Prepare and prequalify reagents and perform routine testing of biological samples.
  • Perform preventive maintenance and quality control on laboratory equipment.
  • Identify equipment malfunctions, perform basic troubleshooting and notify appropriate personnel when needed.
  • Perform equipment calibration.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation while protecting donor, patient and employee confidentiality.
  • Monitor laboratory supplies and reagent levels to help ensure operational readiness.
  • Maintain clean equipment and work areas while adhering to established safety guidelines.
  • Assist with required competency assessments and documentation.
  • Assist with evaluations of reagents, equipment and new methods.
  • Participate in process-improvement initiatives.
  • Perform assigned responsibilities in compliance with internal SOPs and external regulations.

What You Bring

You’re a detail-oriented laboratory professional who understands the importance of accuracy, quality and consistency in a high-complexity testing environment. You bring strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, communicate effectively and enjoy contributing as part of a collaborative team.

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • Meets CLIA requirements for high-complexity testing.
  • One year of HLA clinical laboratory experience.
  • Strong analytical, statistical, organizational and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to organize, prioritize and execute a variable workload with multiple priorities.
  • Proficient computer skills.
  • Effective oral and written communication skills.
  • Strong customer service and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and work effectively as an active member of a team.

Preferred:

  • Two years of HLA clinical laboratory experience.
  • Certified Histocompatibility Technologist (CHT).

Why Vitalant?

At Vitalant, your talent has purpose. Our laboratory professionals are an important part of a mission-driven organization committed to providing high-quality testing and specialized services that patients and healthcare partners depend on.

Here, you’ll have the opportunity to apply your HLA laboratory expertise to meaningful work, strengthen your technical skills and collaborate with professionals who share your commitment to quality.

If you’re looking for an opportunity where your laboratory expertise can contribute to something bigger, we invite you to bring your talents to Vitalant.

REQUIREMENTS:

KNOWLEDGE/EDUCATION

title: Principal Product Manager, Compliance and Payments (New Markets)
description:
We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to join Procore's Product & Technology organization, supporting our Procore Pay business. In this role, you'll identify, size, and validate the next set of markets and segments for Procore's Compliance and Payments products, turning early signals into fully formed strategies backed by evidence. Your primary goal is to determine where Procore Pay can win next — and to prove product-market fit in those markets before we scale investment behind them.

As a Principal Product Manager, you'll partner with Engineering, UX, Product Marketing, Sales, Finance, Risk & Compliance, and Payments leadership to move opportunities from a hypothesis to a funded, launched, revenue-generating product line. Use your opportunity assessment and market sizing rigor, customer discovery expertise, and ability to operate independently in ambiguity to expand the Procore Pay product and open new revenue streams for Procore. This is a rare chance to shape a strategically critical, high-growth part of Procore's business with real autonomy and executive visibility — apply today.

This position reports into the Director of Product Management, Procore Pay and will be based in our Austin, TX office. We're looking for someone to join us immediately.

What you'll do:

  • Lead opportunity assessments for new markets and segments, sizing the opportunity and making a clear, defensible recommendation on whether and how Procore should enter.

  • Validate product-market fit for existing Procore Pay capabilities in new markets, defining the discovery plan, entry criteria, and evidence required before we commit resources.

  • Craft the vision, opportunity assessments, and product briefs for your area, explaining the "why" with sound logic that holds up to executive scrutiny.

  • Take large, ambiguous strategic initiatives and break them into logical, sequenced phases that deliver value to customers along the way.

  • Lead discovery with customers, prospects, and industry participants, facilitating workshops with department leaders and directors and synthesizing findings into actionable insights.

  • Partner with Engineering and UX as a peer leader to translate market strategy into requirements, anticipating risk factors across outcome potential, competitive landscape, technical feasibility, and user experience.

  • Drive go-to-market readiness with Marketing, Sales, Enablement, Support, Risk, and Compliance, designing release plans that generate fast learning through pilots and betas.

  • Define initiative-level customer and business outcomes, track progress against them, and communicate results in a compelling way across Procore.

  • Mentor product managers and contribute to hiring panels, raising the bar for product craft across the team.

What we're looking for:

  • 7+ years of product management or equivalent experience, including ownership of a large or strategically important product area.

  • Demonstrated track record of new market or new product entry: taking a small, unproven idea and developing it into a funded, launched, revenue-generating initiative.

  • Expertise in opportunity assessment, market sizing, and product-market fit validation, with the judgment to recommend against an opportunity when the evidence doesn't support it.

  • Expert command of discovery techniques through customer interviews, market and competitive analysis, prototype testing, and the ability to synthesize findings into trends others can act on.

  • Strong quantitative skills, with the ability to pull and analyze data independently and combine it with qualitative insight to make high-leverage decisions quickly.

  • Proven ability to work autonomously amid significant ambiguity, serving as the connective tissue when ownership is unclear and biasing toward forward progress.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with a history of building buy-in among senior stakeholders across multiple functions without formal authority.

  • Construction Compliance, Payments, fintech, or B2B marketplace experience strongly preferred; construction industry experience is a plus.

Additional Information

Base Pay Range:

198,240.00 - 272,580.00 USD Annual

This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location.

For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates:

Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

title: FT Inbound Freight Handler
description:
As a FT Inbound Freight Handler, you will load and unload freight onto and off of equipment, as well as assist in the recouping of damaged freight.

Prepare, sweep, inspect and cleans trailer(s) before loading freight. Use safe lifting techniques to properly load and unload freight. Select and use proper freight handling equipment to load and unload freight. Such equipment may include forklifts with appropriate hardware, hand trucks, drum trucks, pallet jacks, rollers, and any other available equipment to move, load, arrange, rearrange, and unload freight. Weigh and dimension shipments to ensure proper classification, freight rating, and safe handling. Plan cube utilization and proper weight distribution when loading freight. Count and inspect the condition of freight, documenting any shortages or damage. Review freight bills for special instructions. Check manifests for existing exceptions and check the label and the destination code on manifests against freight bills. Check for special instructions, weight distributions on headloads, and check headloads against the freight bills when loading freight. Verify the hazardous material product description, determine any discrepancies in the paperwork, and verify proper placarding when loading hazardous material. Properly block and brace freight to prevent shifting during transport.

For this role, we prefer you have a High School Diploma or GED. You must have the ability to satisfactorily pass a background check and an alcohol and drug test. We would prefer for you to have prior experience as a Forklift Operator, Dock or Warehouse Worker, or Material Handler. We would also prefer you to have previously held a Forklift Certification. title: Konsernjuridisk direktør
description:
Vil du lede Storebrands konsernjuridiske miljø – og bruke jussen til å skape muligheter for forretningen?

Storebrand opererer i en bransje preget av omfattende og kompleks regulering – samtidig som teknologi, nye forretningsmodeller og endrede kundebehov skaper nye muligheter. Som konsernjuridisk direktør får du en sentral rolle i å sikre at det juridiske arbeidet både understøtter forretningsutvikling og strategisk retning, samtidig som konsernet håndterer juridisk risiko på en god måte.

Du vil lede konsernjuridisk avdeling, som består av 19 dyktige advokater/advokatfullmektiger, og 2 advokatassistenter. Som juridisk direktør vil du være en sentral rådgiver for konsernledelsen og lede et juridisk fagmiljø som arbeider tett på forretningsområdene i strategiske, regulatoriske og forretningsmessige spørsmål.

Vi ser etter en leder som kombinerer solid juridisk tyngde med god forretningsforståelse og gjennomføringsevne. Du ser muligheter innenfor regelverket og finner gode, praktiske løsninger, samtidig som du er tydelig når regulatoriske hensyn setter grenser. Du er trygg på å utfordre beslutninger og etablerte perspektiver når det er nødvendig, og står støtt i dine faglige vurderinger.

Stillingen rapporterer til Group CFO og inngår i CFOs ledergruppe. Rollen gir stor påvirkningskraft på konsernets strategiske utvikling og på hvordan juridiske hensyn integreres i virksomhetens beslutninger. I tillegg får du mulighet til å bidra i utviklingen av rammebetingelsene for finans- og forsikringsbransjen.

Sentrale ansvarsområder

Som konsernjuridisk direktør vil du:

  • ha det overordnede personal-, fag- og budsjettansvaret for konsernjuridisk avdeling

  • lede, utvikle og sette retning for en sterk juridisk funksjon med tydelig forretningsfokus

  • videreutvikle avdelingens bruk av teknologi og AI for å modernisere konsernets juridiske funksjon, inkludert effektiv bruk av teknologi, digitalisering og nye arbeidsformer for å gjøre den juridiske funksjonen mer effektiv, relevant og fremtidsrettet

  • sikre riktig bruk og prioritering av interne og eksterne juridiske ressurser, herunder utvikle relevante nettverk og strategiske samarbeid med eksterne advokatfirmaer

  • være en strategisk rådgiver og sparringspartner for konsernledelsen og forretningsområdene

  • sikre god juridisk risikostyring og tydelige beslutningsgrunnlag i sentrale saker

  • identifisere handlingsrom og muligheter innenfor et komplekst regulatorisk landskap, og bidra til at disse blir omsatt til gode forretningsmessige løsninger

  • delta i styrer og utvalg i konsernet

  • bidra til utviklingen av rammebetingelser for finans- og forsikringsbransjen

  • delta aktivt i CFOs ledergruppe

Hvem ser vi etter?

Vi ser etter deg som har mastergrad i rettsvitenskap, advokatbevilling og minst ti års erfaring fra forretningsjuridisk arbeid. Du har solid ledererfaring og god forståelse for hvordan juridiske vurderinger inngår i forretningsmessige og strategiske beslutninger. Erfaring fra regulerte virksomheter, børsnoterte selskaper eller finans-, forsikrings- eller kapitalmarkedsrelaterte miljøer vil være en fordel.

Det viktigste er likevel hvordan du bruker din faglige kompetanse til å skape verdi for virksomheten. Du kombinerer sterk regulatorisk forståelse med et tydelig forretningsperspektiv. Du evner å se flere handlingsalternativer, finne løsninger som ivaretar virksomhetens interesser og utfordre etablerte sannheter når det er nødvendig. Samtidig er du trygg på å ta tydelige standpunkt i krevende avveininger og si fra når risiko eller regelverk tilsier det.

Du har interesse for teknologi og ser hvordan digitalisering, nye teknologiske løsninger og nye arbeidsformer kan bidra til å utvikle både den juridiske funksjonen og virksomheten som helhet.

Hva skal til for å lykkes?

For å lykkes i rollen er du en kommersiell, nysgjerrig og handlekraftig leder. Du ser helheten, forstår forretningen og liker å være tett på beslutningene. Du er opptatt av å finne gode løsninger og forbedre måten ting gjøres på, og har energi og gjennomføringsevne til å få ting til å skje. Du involverer deg aktivt når du synes det er nødvendig.

Du involverer aktivt andre, bygger relasjoner og skaper oppslutning rundt endring. Som leder er du tydelig og trygg, samtidig som du gir rom for faglig utvikling, initiativ og ansvar.

Du kombinerer faglig tyngde med god forretningsforståelse, og evner å omsette komplekse juridiske problemstillinger til tydelige råd, vurderinger og handlingsalternativer. Du bygger troverdighet gjennom godt skjønn, høy integritet og evnen til å stå støtt når det kreves.

Kort sagt ser vi etter en konsernjuridisk direktør som både kan spørres «hva er mulig – og hvordan kan vi få det til?» og «bør vi gjøre det?».

Hvorfor velge Storebrand?

Hos oss får du rom til å ta plass, bli hørt og utvikle deg i et konsern med mange muligheter. Vi er stolte av kulturen vår, drivkraften vår og den felles retningen vi jobber mot: En fremtid å glede seg til.

Vi tror på verdien av ulike perspektiver og bakgrunner, og jobber aktivt for et inkluderende og mangfoldig miljø. Det blir lagt merke til: I 2025 rangerte Equileap Storebrand som nummer én i Norge og blant de tre beste selskapene i verden på likestilling. I 2026 vant vi ODA Champions.

Som fremtidsoptimister tenker vi langsiktig og investerer i løsninger som styrker oss og samfunnet rundt oss. Det er én grunn til at vi er ett av to norske selskaper i Dow Jones Best-in-Class World Index. Hos oss på Lysaker jobber du sentralt, med gode kollektivmuligheter, sykkelparkering og garderober.

Har du spørsmål til stillingen? Ta kontakt med Kjetil R. Krøkje, Group CFO, mobil: 934 12 155, e-post: kjetil.r.krokje@storebrand.no.

Søknadsfrist: 4.oktober

Vi gleder oss til å høre fra deg!

Å søke jobb i Storebrand skal være enkelt. Derfor trenger du ikke å skrive et søknadsbrev. Vi ønsker kun din CV og svar på noen få spørsmål i søknadsprosessen.


Vi tror på at mangfold styrker oss, og ønsker alle kvalifiserte søkere uansett bakgrunn og erfaring velkommen. Trenger du tilpasninger i søknadsprosessen? Ikke nøl med å gi oss beskjed – slik at vi sammen kan finne en løsning som fungerer for deg.


Storebrand samarbeider med Semac for bakgrunnssjekk av aktuelle kandidater. Bakgrunnssjekken utføres etter samtykke fra deg som søker og innebærer at vi verifiserer CV og annen søknadsdokumentasjon i forbindelse med ansettelsen. I forbindelse med bakgrunnssjekk må politiattest fremlegges for stillinger som krever autorisasjon og/eller godkjenning av egnethet.

title: Environmental Health & Safety(EHS)-  Safety Professional (Healthcare and Research)
description:
The EHS Safety Professional supports a safe and compliant environment by conducting risk assessments, safety inspections, exposure monitoring, incident investigations, and safety training across healthcare and research operations. The role helps identify and mitigate hazards, supports regulatory compliance, and develops recommendations to strengthen workplace safety.

Working closely with our Safety Officers, this role is responsible for developing and maintaining environmental health and safety (EHS) programs, policies, procedures, and compliance processes that support safe healthcare and research operations. Key responsibilities include conducting risk assessments, safety inspections, occupational exposure monitoring, and ventilation evaluations to identify hazards and implement effective control measures.

The position also investigates employee safety concerns and workplace injuries, performs root cause analyses, and develops detailed reports with recommendations to ensure compliance with institutional policies and regulatory requirements.

Job Description

  • Coordinate and perform, with guidance, day-to-day workflow of program and operational responsibilities within safety area (e.g., industrial hygiene, infection prevention).
  • Respond to or escalate safety-related questions and issues raised by cross-departmental stakeholders.
  • Assist leaders within safety areas with preparation of reports around work progress and identified areas of improvement.
  • Assist departmental safety teams with institutional education and training.
  • As directed, execute tasks related to assessment and remediation of risks within safety area including data gathering, analysis, and trending.
  • Assist in clarification and implementation of safety policies and procedures for assigned teams/areas.
  • Support departmental processes to enhance the quality and safety of patient care.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to meet the goals and objectives of the department and institution.
  • Maintains regular and predictable attendance.

Minimum Education and/or Training:

  • Bachelor's degree in liberal arts, science, engineering or related safety discipline required,
  • Hazardous Materials Technician training (24-hour) preferred (or obtain training within 1 year of hiring).
  • DOT/IATA Dangerous Goods training preferred (or obtain training within 1 year of hiring).

Minimum Experience:

  • Prior relevant experience in applicable area preferred (e.g., applied health physics in radiation safety programs; infection prevention and control; EHS).
  • Prior experience in implementation of federal and state regulations and license conditions preferred.
  • At least one year of experience working in an Environmental Health & Safety role strongly preferred.

Additional Responsibilities:

  • Develop EHS operating procedures, policies and process guidelines.
  • Conduct risk assessments for clinical and research activities. Develop and steer implementation of control measures.
  • Conduct and/or lead PETRA Physical Environment risk assessment rounds, under the direction of the General Safety Officer.
  • Conduct multi-disciplinary safety inspections of laboratories and other work areas (including NIH biosafety inspections and PETRA Physical Environment risk assessment rounds) to identify safety risks and ensure compliance with SJCRH safety policies and regulatory standards. Develops risk assessment reports containing observations, commentary and recommendations.
  • Respond to employee safety concerns (including those reported in the EERS system). Investigate hazards and generate reports, as needed, in the EERS system.
  • Investigate employee injuries and conduct root cause analyses as deemed necessary.
  • Develop and accurately apply a strong working knowledge of health and safety standards and guidelines, such as those set by TOSHA (Tennessee Occupational Safety and Health Administration), DNV (Det Norske Veritas), EPA (Environmental Protection Agency), NSF (National Sanitation Foundation), TDEC (Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation), ACGIH (American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists) and NIOSH (National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health)
  • Conduct occupational exposure assessments using industrial hygiene air and noise sampling equipment.
  • Conduct ventilation assessments of air handling equipment and other engineered systems.
  • Develop and deliver safety training programs for clinical and research staff.
  • Serve as a member and Incident Commander of the institutional Hazardous Materials Response Team.
  • Serve as an authority and resource regarding Dangerous Goods/Hazardous Materials shipping practices.
  • File and maintain regulatory permits and other compliance documents.
  • Maintain records and documents, evaluate/interpret data, and resolve related issues.

Preferred Analytical Skills:

  • Demonstrates strong communication, problem-solving, and analytical skills while effectively translating complex technical information for diverse audiences.
  • Applies safety and quality standards, evaluates risks, supports investigations and corrective actions, and develops innovative solutions to improve safety performance.
  • Builds collaborative relationships across teams, executes safety assessments and technical tasks with limited guidance.
  • Effectively manages priorities, resources, timelines, and deliverables while continuously seeking opportunities to improve quality and efficiency.

Compensation

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the salary range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $78,000 - $139,360 per year for the role of Environmental Health & Safety(EHS)- Safety Professional (Healthcare and Research).

title: Senior Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO)
description:
US Citizenship is Required. This position requires a current TOP SECRET clearance. Candidate must be SAP program eligible.


This position is in-person in our Arlington, VA office.


Toyon Research Corporation is seeking a Senior ISSO to lead the full Risk Management Framework (RMF) lifecycle for assigned information systems, from security categorization through authorization and continuous monitoring. This is a hands-on, customer-facing role — the successful candidate will be comfortable wearing multiple hats, collaborating closely with a small team, and engaging directly with DoD CIO Security Control Assessors (SCAs) and internal stakeholders with a service-oriented mindset. The role carries responsibility for producing and maintaining RMF artifacts, coordinating remediation across system owners and engineering teams, and providing mentorship on RMF, compliance, and risk management best practices.


Responsibilities

  • Lead the full RMF lifecycle for assigned systems: security categorization, control implementation, assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring
  • Develop and maintain RMF artifacts, including SSPs, SARs, POA&Ms, Security Impact Analyses, Contingency Plans, and ATO documentation
  • Conduct vulnerability assessments using tools such as Tenable Nessus, SCAP Compliance Checker, and STIG Viewer
  • Validate compliance with DISA STIGs, CIS Benchmarks, NIST SP 800-53, and organizational baselines
  • Coordinate remediation efforts with system owners, administrators, and engineering teams
  • Support security monitoring and incident response through Splunk Enterprise, including reviewing audit logs and privileged account activity
  • Assess cloud security configurations in AWS and Microsoft Azure
  • Evaluate network and endpoint security controls
  • Support audits and inspections; manage POA&M tracking
  • Provide cybersecurity guidance and mentorship on RMF, compliance, risk management, and security best practices
  • Interface directly with DoD CIO Security Control Assessors (SCAs)

title: Temporary Administrative Program Coordinator
description:
ABOUT WILLAMETTE UNIVERSITY:

Willamette University, founded in 1842, is a nationally-renowned private university enrolling 2800 students across five colleges. Our historic campus, adjacent to the Oregon State Capitol, hosts a distinguished undergraduate liberal arts college in Salem, Oregon. Our downtown Portland campus is home to the Pacific Northwest College of Art (PNCA). We offer a wide range of professional graduate programs, including Oregon’s top-ranked MBA program, the Northwest’s oldest law school, as well as MA/MFA programs at PNCA and master’s degrees in data science and computer science.

Willamette University provides a high-value and comprehensive benefits package to eligible employees. Our Benefits Summary includes options for health, dental, life insurance, retirement, substantial paid time off, tuition and more. If you need assistance applying for a job or have any questions on recruitment at Willamette, please contact our HR Department, hr@willamette.edu or call us at 503-370-6210.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Temporary Administrative Program Coordinator (APC) provides administrative support to various academic departments in the Willamette College. The APC actively participates in critical management activities (financial, operational and personnel related) in support of the faculty and students in the department. The APC is supervised by the Executive Assistant to the Dean, College of Arts & Sciences but resides near the departments where the day-to-day work is performed. The Department Chair is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day work and partners with the Executive Assistant to assess the APC’s performance.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Essential Functions: as this position supports a portfolio of units, departments may not need all of these functions performed. However, it is the expectation that the administrative staff be able to perform these tasks if required by their department(s). The result may be that the staff performs one set of tasks for one department and another set of tasks for the other department(s). Further, as department chairs/program directors turnover approximately every three years, an incoming chair may require a different set of tasks to be performed. Administrative staff are expected to be flexible in handling changes in departmental support needs and expectations. It is recommended that the APC meet with each Chair/Director to review the job description and discuss tasks to ensure that expectations are aligned.

Administrative Management & Operations: Supports the units as office manager and uses business acumen to make decisions on behalf of the units; serving on various committees as well as acting as liaison to areas across campus, such as Facilities, Accounting, Admissions, Campus Safety, WITS, and the Dean’s Office. Requires ability to work independently and prioritize workload to meet varying schedules.

  • Coordinates the training and work assignment of work-study student employees; may be the supervisor in some situations.

  • Ensures that all maintenance needs for equipment are attended to in a timely manner. Also ensures the cleanliness and upkeep of unit spaces by communicating issues with the appropriate office on campus and/or submitting work orders to facilities. May serve as building captain.

  • Complete office tasks including opening/closing, establishandmaintainfiles (electronic and paper), supply ordering, mail, copying, scanning, management of online departmental calendar(s) and other clerical activities

  • Facilitation of assignments of offices, key requests, computers, telephones, signage, printers, etc. Coordinates details in preparation for departmental and program meetings; prepares agenda and other materials, presents reports as appropriate, takes and transcribes minutes, and performs necessary follow-up.

  • Prepares and maintains various handbooks

  • Composes letters, reports, minutes and other materials as directed

  • Coordinates access to restricted classrooms, labs and storage

Budget & Personnel: Is responsible for ensuring that revenues and expenses are appropriately categorized so that the Chairs, faculty and the Dean’s Office have an accurate assessment of financial status in all accounts. Understands university policy, process and procedures in order to ensure compliance and facilitate efficient financial management.

  • Reconciles general fund and special accounts to ascertain appropriate balances and make adjusting entries as needed; prepares periodic financial reports; processes invoices, procurement cards, requisitions, expense claims, vouchers and journal entries; assists with budget preparation.

  • Organizes, maintains records, and directs correspondence for annual evaluation of adjunct faculty.

  • Supports searches for visiting faculty, adjuncts and new tenure track faculty.

  • Supports Language Assistants

  • Maintains student employee personnel files and payroll records; approves timesheets

Academic Support: Provides hands-on academic support to the Chairs, full-time faculty and adjuncts. This position has capacity to support future faculty/personnel growth in the units. Requires ability to work independently and prioritize workload to meet varying schedules.

  • Accesses information on major/minors and fulfillment of degree requirements, faculty, course rotations and faculty assignments in order to supply data/reports to faculty and/or chair/director.

  • Facilitates assessment and accreditation activities

  • Assists department chairs in organizing and coordinating class schedule each semester. Maintains or obtains enrollment statistics for class planning purposes.

  • Assists faculty with the timely preparation of course materials (including syllabi, exams and handouts), grant proposals and reports, annual reports, committee materials, course and sabbatical proposals.

  • Assists with transportation needs for field trips and special events as requested

Events and Communication: Serves as the primary point of contact on behalf of the units in a friendly and cheerful manner so that interactions positively portray departmental and university programs, personnel and philosophies. Event coordination is approached in a self-motivated style so that tasks are driven by one’s initiative yet in collaboration with faculty.

  • Responds to inquiries and requests from students and parents (both current and prospective), faculty, staff, and the public.

  • Maintains unit bulletin boards, display cabinets, directories, email groups, websites, list serves, and social media. Submits information to university and/or external outlets to advertise and promote events

  • Assists with scheduling of unit events and provides information to campus community and general public. Assists in the planning, budgeting, advertising, and execution of conferences, workshops, guest lectures, and other events. Oversees related travel arrangements and hospitality.

  • Coordinates the collection of and contributes to content for publicity materials including newsletters, posters, brochures, press releases and various social media platforms. Serves as liaison with the University Office of Communications.

​

Other Duties:

  • Safeguards the confidentiality of departmental or office administration by exercising discretion in communicating information to faculty, students and staff, and handling departmental records and files, personnel actions, performance evaluations, grade reports, merit, promotion and tenure decisions, and similar confidential materials.

  • Other duties as assigned including serving on college-wide or university committees on behalf of the department.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Experience: Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of three years of general office experience of a progressively responsible nature, including bookkeeping, record keeping, navigating organizational policies and procedures to ensure compliance with rules and regulations, and providing excellent customer service to those whom the applicant supports. In lieu of a Bachelor’s degree, five years or more of the required experience will be considered.

Computer Skills: Proficient knowledge of Microsoft Office programs, particularly Word and Excel. Familiar with bookkeeping software and/or enterprise-wide information systems. Skills in internet navigation and email and calendaring systems. Willingness and ability to learn new technologies associated with the job. Ability to type accurately at 40 wpm.

Competencies:

  • Must be able to work autonomously to fulfill the expectations of the position.

  • Proactively seek training and knowledge in order to perform tasks as well as seek ways to improve how work is accomplished.

  • The ability to anticipate the expectations and needs of the faculty.

  • Strong bookkeeping/budget/financial skills.

  • Superior organization skills, extreme attention to detail, quick and at times creative problem solving.

  • Strong collaboration skills and an aptitude for managing conflict. Must have a positive and pleasant attitude and establish and maintain harmonious relations with staff, faculty and students.

  • The ability to develop a deep understanding of policies and procedures in order to successfully interpret, communicate and navigate them and to ensure compliance with university rules and regulations.

  • Must comport oneself with a high degree of responsiveness and respect toward others.

  • Ability to work with diverse people and maintain a professional, collegial atmosphere.

  • Capable of working in a fast-paced environment and can adapt to changing situations.

  • Demonstrated ability to work on routine tasks while juggling special projects and to set priorities and meet deadlines despite frequent interruptions.

  • Must have a professional and respectful style for both written and verbal communication.

  • Excellent record keeping, proofreading, and writing skills as well as a high degree of accuracy.

  • Ability to exercise good judgment and diplomacy and to maintain confidentiality.

  • Complete assigned tasks in a timely manner.

Preferred

  • Experience in higher education

  • Website and social media maintenance

  • Budget development

  • Event coordination

You can also take advantage of our salary packaging program including motor vehicles, eligible portable electronic devices and professional memberships.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance.

Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-10-01 11:59 PM

CBC Saskatchewan is hiring a reporter-editor in our Prince Albert bureau, an area that is a vital link in the social, cultural and political infrastructure of north-east Saskatchewan. Your reporting will share undertold stories with audiences in Saskatchewan and across Canada.

Adaptability is key to the role of reporter-editor. One day you could be covering a hyper-local story that matters to residents of Prince Albert and the north, or working behind the scenes to line up interviews for a morning radio program. The next day you’re off to a federal announcement on agricultural support and contributing to broadcast and digital platforms live. Central to all of your coverage is ensuring voices from the region are reflected in our journalism across digital, radio, social, streaming and TV.

In this role, you’ll operate independently, under the direction of the CBC Saskatchewan assignment desk. While you’re comfortable taking the initiative and working solo to get things done, you will have a lot of daily support from your colleagues at both the CBC Saskatoon and CBC Regina stations, as well as from the CBC bureaus provincewide. We’re a collaborative group, here to help you in your daily assignment. You will also have access to ongoing training opportunities to support your development with CBC News.

Affordable housing, short commutes and easy-access to year round activities make this an ideal location for those who prioritize quality of life. Outdoor enthusiasts will love the easy access to lakes, river trails, fishing and snowmobiling to name just a few. Located on a major highway, Prince is a 90-minute drive from Saskatoon.

The role requires you to be full-time on-site in our Prince Albert bureau. You will be provided with a vehicle to get to stories throughout the region.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Pitch, research, gather and produce original story ideas for digital, social, radio, streaming and TV programming that will engage and inform audiences, deepen community connections and elevate a range of voices, especially those who have typically been underrepresented in media.

  • Respond quickly to breaking news events as they unfold.

  • Distill large amounts of complex information under tight time constraints.

  • Cultivate and develop working relationships with a large pool of contacts and community members.

  • Collaborate with colleagues across CBC to develop and break stories, plan and produce features and coordinate long-term coverage.

  • Ensure CBC journalistic standards are met and that our stories are fair, balanced, accurate, thoughtful, immediate and resonate with the communities we serve.

What you bring:

  • Demonstrated experience working in a fast-paced daily news environment, or an equivalent position in a deadline driven environment with transferable skills.

  • Ability to work independently with superior problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to generate, pitch and pursue strong, original stories that meet the needs of audiences.

  • A proven track record of connecting with local communities.

  • Superior writing skills, and experience in gathering, editing and packaging audio and video for multiple platforms.

  • Ability to present stories live on-air, from within the studio and out in the field.

  • A willingness to embrace change and take on new tasks as the media industry evolves.

  • A strong desire to live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture.

  • Possession of a valid driver’s licence and a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio Canada’s insurance company.

  • Ability and willingness to work flexible hours, including weekends, as required.

  • University degree or college certificate in journalism or equivalent, with a minimum of three years of recent, related experience.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

CBC/Radio-Canada is committed to being a leader in reflecting our country’s diversity. That’s because we can only create and tell the stories that connect Canadians, by having a workforce that mirrors the ever-changing makeup of our country. That’s why we, as an employer, value equal opportunity and nurture an inclusive workplace where our individual differences are not only recognized and valued, but also extend to and pervade all the services we provide as Canada’s public broadcaster. Holly Springs, North Carolina

Does the thought of building an entirely new site from the ground up excite you? Do you love cultivating sustainable systems and high performing teams? If you want to be a part of Amgen’s mission to serve patients – every patient every time – then check out this exciting new opportunity.

Amgen, one of the world’s leading biotechnology companies is investing $550 million to build a new multi-product drug substance biomanufacturing facility in Holly Springs, North Carolina, a biomanufacturing “hub” known for their life sciences industry. The new plant will combine two production formats, traditional stainless steel-fed batch and single use technology. This combination of capabilities is an approach that Amgen calls “FleX Batch” manufacturing, which makes the facility more dynamic and efficient, as well as requiring a smaller physical footprint than a traditional plant. title: Senior Demand Planner, Performance - North America
description:
POSITION TITLE: Senior Demand Planner, Performance - North America

REPORTS TO: Director, Planning

BUSINESS AREA: Merchandising & Planning

LOCATION: Ogden, UT

OVERVIEW

This role owns the development and delivery of a strong, market-driven demand plan for the North American business. The Senior Demand Planner, Performance is responsible for creating a clear, accurate forecast that aligns commercial goals with inventory investment and financial targets.

Sitting within the merchandising & planning function, this role connects sales, merchandising, and global planning teams to drive a single, aligned view of demand. You will use data, market insight, and category knowledge to guide buying decisions, improve forecast accuracy, and support overall business performance.

This is a strategic, high-impact role that goes beyond building a forecast — it requires challenging assumptions, influencing stakeholders, and ensuring the business is aligned to the right demand plan to drive growth while managing risk.

WHAT MAKES THIS A GREAT PLACE TO WORK & PLAY:

  • Hybrid work schedule
  • A generous PTO policy, plus 15 paid annual holidays and 3 floating holidays
  • Half-day Fridays for 5 months of the year
  • An exceptional employee discount on all our products and sister brands (Arc’teryx, Armada, Atomic, Wilson)
  • “Powder Bell” powder days throughout the winter season
  • Healthy Lifestyle Benefit designed to support your well-being and active lifestyle
  • Opportunities to engage in the community and with industry partners

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility satisfactorily:

Demand Planning & Forecast Ownership

  • Own the end-to-end demand plan at model, color, size, and monthly levels
  • Develop and maintain a consensus-based forecast aligned to service level targets, inventory goals, and commercial plans
  • Translate forecast into actionable inputs for open-to-buy and supply planning
  • Analyze, challenge, and refine market forecasts to balance growth ambition with inventory risk
  • Manage complex categories, including new product launches and variable demand patterns

Category & Inventory Management

  • Drive category-level performance against inventory, productivity, and service KPIs
  • Monitor inventory health, turns, and sell-through, identifying risks and opportunities proactively
  • Apply SKU productivity frameworks (e.g., 80/15/5) to inform demand and buy recommendations
  • Partner with merchandising to support assortment productivity and lifecycle decisions

Cross-Functional Leadership & Consensus

  • Lead or play a key role in demand consensus forums, providing data-driven recommendations
  • Align stakeholders across sales, merchandising, marketing, finance, and supply chain to a single demand plan
  • Act as the key point of contact between market and global planning teams
  • Influence decision-making to ensure alignment between demand, supply, and financial goals

Sales Order & Buy Management

  • Participate in sales order deadline booking processes and key planning checkpoints.
  • Lead market conversations with global demand and supply planning to ensure timely buys and provide market input on blind buys.
  • Collaborate on capacity constraints and available mitigation actions.
  • Represent buy cadence within the market and organize teams to make timely, informed buy decisions.

Team Leadership & Development

  • Mentor junior and newly onboarded team members, building foundational demand planning capabilities.
  • Support onboarding through coaching on tools, processes, and best practices.

Process Improvement & Tools

  • Identify and lead process improvements to enhance forecast accuracy and planning efficiency
  • Support development of tools, reporting, and frameworks to scale demand planning capabilities
  • Drive adoption of standardized planning processes across teams

KPIs Owned – Demand Planning

  • Inventory targets and turns by category
  • SKU productivity (80/15/5 framework)
  • Shipment and revenue forecast accuracy
  • Buy plan adherence and inventory risk management

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORKING ENVIRONMENT

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to travel, talk and hear. The employee is frequently required to sit, stand and walk. The employee must occasionally kneel, stoop, crouch, twist and lift to 30 pounds, with or without accommodations.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate, but can involve exposure to varying noise levels, ranging from moderate to loud, as well as flashes of light.

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • 5–8+ years of experience in demand planning, merchandise planning, or supply chain planning
  • Prior experience in the lifestyle, outdoor or athletic industry with a focus on softgoods preferred; previous merchandising experience is advantageous, but not required
  • strong analytical capabilities with the ability to translate data into strategic and tactical actions
  • Advanced Excel skills; experience with planning systems strongly preferred
  • Experience in apparel, footwear, outdoor, or consumer goods industries preferred
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders

title: Natural Resources Specialist I/II - Public Works, Clean Water
description:
Job Summary

The Clean Water Division of Clark County Public Works is currently seeking a Natural Resource Specialist I/II. Positions in this class are responsible for performing a variety of field and office assignments to carry out monitoring requirements of Clark County’s NPDES phase I municipal stormwater permit. Work requires the application of standard principles for assessing and evaluating water quality and overall stream health. Duties and activities include applying standard operating procedures over multiple monitoring projects, project management skills that are necessary to successfully complete work assignments, detection and elimination of illicit discharges to the storm system and interacting with the public and outside agencies.

The primary tasks and responsibilities of this position are to provide technical support for monitoring related activities including water quality and habitat assessments, perform stream discharge measurements, operate and maintain remote logging equipment, and maintain and calibrate multiparameter sondes.

The Natural Resource Specialist classification is the fully experienced level within the job family. Work assignments are performed with limited technical instruction and require considerable independence in the selection of courses of action and resolution of complex or unique problems within the framework of departmental policy and procedures, applicable regulations, accepted best practices and operating procedures.

The Public Works department values our community’s diversity and seeks ways to promote equity and inclusion within the organization and with the public. The department encourages applications from candidates with knowledge, ability and experience working with a broad range of individuals and communities with diverse racial, ethnic, and socio-economic backgrounds.

This position is represented by Local 307CO - Washington State Council of County and City Employees.

Qualifications

Education and Experience:

• Four (4) year degree with major coursework in a natural science or related field. Two (two) years of experience working in areas related to natural resource science or environmental science.

• On a year‑for‑year basis, any combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted for educational requirements.

- AND -

Qualified candidates must have a valid driver’s license.

Knowledge of: State and local regulations pertaining to water quality and stormwater management; standard operating procedures regarding water quality monitoring; project management related to water quality and habitat assessments; principles, practices and techniques of stormwater management; detection and elimination of illicit discharges; collecting and assessing stream health data.

Ability to: Effectively plan and organize work and complete tasks within prescribed timeframes; comprehend, interpret, and implement applicable regulations governing stormwater management and assessing water quality; analyze and evaluate water quality data; independently exercise sound judgment; establish effective working relationships and communication with regulatory agencies, county departments and the public; prepare detailed documentation and communications in the form of written reports, memos, email; maintain a valid driver’s license.

Selection Process:

Resume and other documents must be attached together in the 'Resume Upload' section of the application. Multiple files are allowed, but all applicant attachments must be uploaded simultaneously, as there is no way to edit or append uploaded materials after submitting the application.

Application Review (Pass/ Fail) - An online application is required. Attaching a resume does not substitute for a completed application; incomplete applications will not pass the application review. Candidates deemed most qualified will be invited to participate in the remainder of the selection process.

Practical Exam (Pass/Fail) - This recruitment may require a practical exam which will be job related and may include, but not limited to, the qualifications outlined in the job announcement. Candidates deemed most qualified will be invited to participate in the remainder of the selection process.

Oral Interview - The interview will be job related and may include, not limited to, the qualifications outlined in the job announcement. Top candidate(s) will continue in the process.

Employment references will be conducted for the final candidates and may include verification of education.

It is general policy of the County that new employees should be hired at the lower steps of the applicable range and advance through the range at the normal progression.

First review of candidates will be September 30th. This recruitment may close at any time on or after the first review date with no additional notice.

Examples of Duties

Duties may include but are not limited to the following:

  • Support the work of the Clean Water Division staff and other agencies as it relates to NPDES permit compliance.
  • Assists in implementing a variety of environmental monitoring programs and projects.
  • Perform water quality, sediment and benthic macroinvertebrate monitoring using established standard operating procedures.
  • Operate and maintain remote temperature and stream stage loggers and data recorders.
  • Calibrate and maintain equipment to conduct stream water quality and discharge measurements.
  • Observe and measures stream physical habitat characteristics using a variety of equipment and instruments.
  • Prepare for field work, communicate with laboratories and ships and tracks water, sediment and macroinvertebrate samples.
  • Manage water quality and continuous data using a variety of software.
  • Interpret applicably county code to apply water quality requirements, laws, codes and policies to assure county permit compliance.
  • Assists in communicating, verbally and in writing, water resources issues in a concise manner.
  • Research grant funding opportunities, assist in grant proposal preparation and administration.
  • Knowledge of stormwater best management practices.
  • Knowledge of RStudio and ArcGIS Pro.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

title: Senior Product Designer (we have office locations in Cambridge, Leeds and London)
description:
As a Senior Product Designer at Genomics England, you will bring cutting-edge new genomics products to life. You will take the lead on the design of products from end-to-end and help to establish first class design standards.

This is a core role in our organisation and will consist of designing innovative, intuitive products and collaborating with Product Managers and Engineers to define and realise the product vision and roadmap. You will develop a deep understanding of user needs working with User Research and combine this with business objectives and domain knowledge derived from subject matter experts to ideate, build and iterate products.

Everyday responsibilities include:

  • Get to know the Services: What they are, how they work, and how they could transform research and healthcare. You’ll also get to know our users and their needs. We have lots of qualitative research to get you started. You’ll start with the Cancer Decision Support squad and then move on to the Accelerating Data Exploration squad, focusing initially on Public Data Exploration, providing a solid grounding in the services we provide across Healthcare and Research.
  • Design the Products: You’ll work as part of a cross-functional squad including engineering, research, product management and subject matter experts to iterate designs, ensuring usability, feasibility and viability to deliver quality outcomes.
  • Problem solving: You'll be designing interactions and product experiences surrounding complex data, delivering well-crafted designs rooted in user needs in line with relevant design standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Input into the product vision: You will work closely with the Product Manager to translate qualitative and quantitative insights into a product roadmap to deliver user value.
  • Champion accessibility: You’ll design accessible, experiences with a content designer to ensure everyone can access and use the product.
  • Apply frameworks: You'll have knowledge and experience of applying NHS design systems and frameworks and utilise these in your design.
  • Contribute to the wider design community: Collaborate with other designers to share design patterns and best practice and shape our design ways of working, collectively improving delivery of design quality.
  • Facilitate decision making and co-creation: Bring together diverse perspectives, including the product squad, internal and external stakeholders and users, through appropriate methods to solve problems together.

Essential skills:

  • Substantial experience as a Senior Product Designer with examples of live delivery.
  • Experience working as part of a cross functional product squad.
  • Demonstrable knowledge of product design processes and methodologies.
  • Able to work end-to-end, from discovery to launch, and beyond.
  • Understanding of how to evaluate and interpret user research findings to wireframe and prototype solutions.
  • Knowledge of the WCAG 2.2 accessibility guidelines and ability to work with engineers to implement.
  • Proactive collaborator who embraces working with a diverse range of people such as designers, engineers, product managers, and researchers.
  • Strong organisational skills, including the ability to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.
  • Desire to continually improve work through giving and receiving feedback.
  • Advanced proficiency with design and prototyping tools including Figma and Miro.
  • Experience using NHS design systems and applying regulatory best practice desirable.
  • Advanced storytelling skills, with the ability to clearly communicate complex problems, decisions, and outcomes to diverse audiences, influencing understanding and alignment across multidisciplinary and senior teams.

Desirable skills:

  • Experience working under Government Digital Service Standard.
  • Experience of front-end engineering, and an ability to work with architects to ensure solutions we design are feasible.
  • Comfortable and effective when working with ambiguity and able to support others to navigate uncertainty and find focus to deliver value.
  • Experienced in creating patterns and defining boundaries for other areas to adopt.
  • Strong influence and experience building and navigating relationships to ensure collaboration and adoption of best practice in other areas of the organisation.
  • Strong understanding of engineering constraints and feasibility considerations with experience of working collaboratively with technical colleagues.
  • Experienced balancing tactical delivery with supporting overarching and long-term product strategy to ensure scalability and sustainability of solutions.
  • Experience working confidently within highly regulated, risk-sensitive contexts.
  • Awareness and sensitivity to ethical, compliance, and regulatory considerations when designing and delivering products with sensitive data.

Salary from £65,300

Closing date for applications - Thursday 1st October at midnight

Being an integral part of such a meaningful mission is extremely rewarding in itself, but in order to support our people, we’re continually improving our benefits package. We pride ourselves on investing in our people and supporting them to achieve their career goals, as well as offering a benefits package including:

  • Generous Leave: 30 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, additional leave for long service, and the option to apply for up to 30 days of remote working abroad annually (approval required).
  • Family-Friendly: Blended working arrangements, flexible working, enhanced maternity, paternity and shared parental leave benefits.
  • Pension & Financial: Defined contribution pension (Genomics England double-matches up to 10%, however you can contribute more if you wish), Life Assurance (3x salary), an Electric Vehicle salary sacrifice scheme and a Give As You Earn scheme.
  • Learning & Development: Individual learning budgets, support for training and certifications, and reimbursement for one annual professional subscription (approval required).
  • Recognition & Rewards: Employee recognition programme and referral scheme.
  • Health & Wellbeing: Subsidised gym membership, a free Headspace account, and access to an Employee Assistance Programme, eye tests, flu jabs.

Equal opportunities and our commitment to a diverse and inclusive workplace

Genomics England is actively committed to providing and supporting an inclusive environment that promotes equity, diversity and inclusion best practice both within our community and in any other area where we have influence. We are proud of our diverse community where everyone can come to work and feel welcomed and treated with respect regardless of any disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, sexual orientation, or social background.

Genomics England’s policies of non-discrimination and equity and will be applied fairly to all people, regardless of age, disability, gender identity or reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, being pregnant or recently becoming a parent, race, religion or beliefs, sex or sexual orientation, length of service, whether full or part-time or employed under a permanent or a fixed-term contract or any other relevant factor.

Genomics England does not tolerate any form of discrimination, harassment, victimisation or bullying at work. Such behaviour undermines our mission and core values and diminishes the dignity, respect and integrity of all parties. Our People policies outline our commitment to inclusivity.

We aim to remove barriers in our recruitment processes and to be flexible with our interview processes. Should you require any adjustments that may help you to fully participate in the recruitment process, we encourage you to discuss this with us.

Culture

We have four key behaviours that represent what we would like Genomics England to feel like and the culture we want to encourage, in order for us to achieve our mission. These behaviours help us all work well together, deliver on our outcomes, celebrate our successes and share feedback with each other. You can read about these and other aspects of our culture here Culture | Genomics England

Blended working model

Genomics England operates a blended working model as we know our people appreciate the flexibility that hybrid working can bring. We expect most people to come into the office a minimum of 2 times each month. However, this will vary according to role and will be agreed with your team leader. There is no expectation that people will return to the office full time unless they want to, however, some of our roles require full time on site attendance e.g., lab teams, reception team.

Our teams and squads have, and will continue to reflect on what works best for them to work together successfully and have the freedom to design working patterns to suit, beyond the minimum. Our office locations are: Canary Wharf, Cambridge and Leeds.

Onboarding background checks

As part of our recruitment process, all successful candidates are subject to a Standard Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. We therefore require applicants to disclose any previous offences at point of application, as some unspent convictions may mean we are unable to proceed with your application due to the nature of our work in healthcare.

  • Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Computer Vision principles

  • Cloud & API Integration for deploying AI models

  • Understanding of advanced AI concepts related to data relationships and reasoning.

  • Some level of proficiency with common AI and data science languages (e.g., Python, R, SQL) with exposure to scripting for automation and data manipulation.

  • Ability to adapt quickly, learn new skills quickly, and work effectively in ambiguous situations.

  • Strong analytical thinking, sound judgment, and problem solving skills.

  • Collaboration and leadership capability; works well in a team environments.

  • Initiative driven, intellectually curious, and motivated to deliver results.
