title: Hardware Integration Technician
description:
Hardware Integration Technician


Location: Madison, AL

Position Summary

The Hardware Integration Technician performs mechanical and electrical assembly, hardware integration, inspection, testing, and basic troubleshooting of computer systems, equipment racks, chassis, and related hardware. The position works from engineering drawings, work instructions, and established procedures using standard hand tools, manufacturing equipment, and electronic test equipment.

This is a developmental technical position that performs routine assignments with increasing independence while collaborating with Engineering, Production, Quality Assurance, and other functional teams to meet technical, quality, and production requirements.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

· Assemble and integrate mechanical, electrical, and electronic systems, including equipment racks, computer hardware, cabling, and related components.

· Perform assembly and installation activities in accordance with engineering drawings, schematics, bills of material, work instructions, and established procedures.

· Route, dress, secure, and label power, network, and other cabling in accordance with applicable requirements.

· Use hand tools, manufacturing equipment, and electronic test equipment to perform assembly, inspection, functional testing, and basic troubleshooting.

· Identify and report nonconforming material, workmanship issues, and documentation discrepancies affecting product quality or performance.

· Complete required production travelers, assembly checklists, inspection records, and test documentation.

· Support equipment handling, staging, packing, unpacking, and preparation for production and shipment.

· Collaborate with Engineering, Production, Quality Assurance, and other personnel to resolve production issues and support process improvements.

· Follow applicable ISO 9001, CMMI, configuration-control, ESD, safety, and quality procedures while maintaining a clean and safe work environment.

· Perform other related duties as assigned.


Required Education, Training, and Experience

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • Completion of a trade or technical school program in electronics, electrical systems, electro-mechanical technology, industrial technology, or a related technical discipline; or
  • Four (4) years of relevant U.S. Navy or other military technical experience involving electronics, electrical systems, communications equipment, computer systems, maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, or hardware integration; or
  • An equivalent combination of relevant education, military technical training, certifications, apprenticeship, and work experience.
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience with electronic or electro-mechanical equipment, including assembly, installation, testing, maintenance, troubleshooting, or repair.

Relevant military technical schools and occupational training may be credited toward education and experience requirements.


Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

· Working knowledge of mechanical, electrical, and electro-mechanical assembly practices and related hardware, cabling, connectors, and components.

· Ability to read and follow engineering drawings, schematics, bills of material, work instructions, and documented procedures.

· Ability to safely use hand tools, manufacturing equipment, and basic electronic test equipment.

· Basic knowledge of electrical testing and troubleshooting, including identifying and reporting workmanship, component, or documentation discrepancies.

· Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately complete production, inspection, and test documentation.

· Ability to prioritize work, adapt to changing production requirements, and perform routine assignments independently or as part of a cross-functional team.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience integrating equipment racks, ruggedized computer systems, servers, network equipment, or similar electronic systems.
  • Experience with cable installation, routing, dressing, labeling, and wire management.
  • Experience using electronic test equipment such as multimeters, cable testers, oscilloscopes, or analyzers.
  • Experience in defense, aerospace, military, industrial electronics, or other controlled manufacturing environments.
  • Familiarity with ISO 9001, CMMI, ESD controls, and configuration-controlled production environments.
  • Technical certification or training in electronics, electro-mechanical assembly, cable fabrication, soldering, or a related discipline.

Physical Requirements


· Ability to stand, sit, kneel, bend, reach, and perform assembly work for extended periods, including overhead work.

· Manual dexterity to use hand tools, install components, and route cabling.

· Ability to safely lift and move materials or equipment weighing up to 50 pounds, with assistance when appropriate.


Scopre and Responsibilities


Performs hardware and electro-mechanical assembly and integration, integration, testing, and basic troubleshooting using established procedures. Performs routine assignments with increasing independence, works to complete assigned objectives within target schedules, and elevates non-routine issues to appropriate Production, Engineering, or Quality personnel.

Responsible for accurate and timely completion of production documentation and timekeeping, including proper recording of labor to assigned projects and activities.


Work Environment

Work is primarily performed in a production, integration, warehouse, or laboratory environment. The standard work schedule is four (4) 10-hour days per week. Activities and priorities may vary based on production schedules, customer requirements, testing, and delivery commitments. The employee must adapt to changing priorities while maintaining quality, safety, and documentation requirements.

title: Zorgconsultant bij een Scale-up in Zorgtech (Alle regio's in Nederland – 32 tot 40 uur)
description:
Jouw rol

Als Zorgconsultant ben jij de onmisbare schakel tussen de zorgvloer en onze technologie. Omdat jij zelf uit de praktijk komt, hoeven we jou niet uit te leggen onder welke druk de teams werken. Jij spreekt hun taal, snapt wat er nodig is om goede zorg te verlenen en weet precies hoe je zorgmedewerkers zover krijgt dat ze onze technologie met vertrouwen omarmen.

Je krijgt bij ons geen dichtgetimmerd handboek: Je ziet wat er bij een klant of binnen Sensara nodig is, neemt initiatief en pakt het op.

Wat ga je doen?

  • Implementeren & Trainen: Je begeleidt implementaties bij nieuwe klanten en traint en coacht de zorgteams op de vloer in het gebruik van Sensara.

  • Adviseren: Je neemt zorgorganisaties bij de hand en adviseert (zorg)managers en teamleiders over de optimale inzet van zorgtechnologie in hun dagelijkse processen.

  • Pionieren & Signaleren: Je spot kansen voor procesverbeteringen, zowel bij de klant als intern bij Sensara.

  • Doorontwikkelen: Je haalt klantfeedback op, test nieuwe functionaliteiten en vertaalt jouw praktijkkennis naar concrete verbeteringen voor ons platform.

  • Vertegenwoordigen: Je bent het gezicht van Sensara tijdens bijeenkomsten, congressen en evenementen.

Wie ben jij?

Jij bent een zorgprofessional in hart en nieren met een ondernemende drive. Je vindt het heerlijk om te innoveren en krijgt energie van het begeleiden van mensen in verandering. Je voelt je thuis in de dynamiek van een snelgroeiend bedrijf en jij wilt morgen al impact maken.

Je brengt mee:

  • Echte zorgervaring: Je hebt minimaal 2 jaar daadwerkelijk in de zorg gewerkt en beschikt over een relevante, afgeronde opleiding in de zorg. Je weet precies hoe het er op de werkvloer aan toe gaat.

  • Scale-up mentaliteit: Je bent flexibel en gedijt goed in een omgeving die volop in beweging is. Je vindt het leuk om mee te bouwen en niet in vastgeroeste kaders te werken.

  • Eigenaarschap: Je bent daadkrachtig, neemt initiatief en durft de kar te trekken voor jouw eigen projecten en implementaties.

  • Overtuigingskracht: Je hebt sterke communicatieve vaardigheden en weet mensen (van verpleegkundige tot bestuurder) mee te krijgen.

  • Affiniteit met innovatie: Je hebt een duidelijke visie op de toekomst van de zorg en ziet technologie als een prachtig middel om ouderen te ondersteunen.

  • Goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal en minimaal 32 uur per week beschikbaar. (Ervaring met Sensara is mooi meegenomen, maar zeker geen vereiste).

Waarom werken bij Sensara?

Omdat je hier de kans krijgt om jouw zorgervaring in te zetten op een manier waarmee je duizenden zorgmedewerkers én cliënten helpt. Je blijft dichtbij de zorg, maar staat tegelijkertijd aan het roer van de innovatie ervan.

Wij bieden:

  • Een betekenisvolle functie met directe impact op het welzijn van ouderen.

  • Veel vrijheid, autonomie en de verantwoordelijkheid om écht eigenaarschap te tonen in je rol.

  • Een innovatieve, ambitieuze en dynamische werkomgeving waarin jouw ideeën tellen.

  • Een enthousiast team met een open cultuur, gezellige borrels en regelmatige teamactiviteiten.

  • Goede arbeidsvoorwaarden, inclusief ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling en groei.

  • Een leaseauto (ook privé te gebruiken) omdat je regelmatig door heel Nederland naar klanten reist.

Interesse?

Ben jij klaar om jouw ervaring in de zorg in te zetten voor innovatie die écht verschil maakt, en krijg jij energie van de dynamiek van een scale-up? Solliciteer direct via onderstaande link.

Wil je eerst meer weten over de functie of aftasten of we een goede match zijn? Neem dan contact op met Carolien, Teamleider Zorgconsultancy, via 06-15384605.

title: Machine Shop Shift Leader - C Shift
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

Description:

We are a mission-driven team of collaborators, action-takers and problem solvers relentlessly committed to a culture of safety and success. Working as an integral part of a passionate and accomplished team of experts, you will directly impact the future of space flight and ensure the progression of building the road to space through reusable rockets. Through dedication and leadership, your influence will help guide your team to define the future of space flight production. In coordinating all aspects of machining flight vehicle components, you will support various spaceflight systems in the production of parts with high-value, tight tolerance and impeccable quality: driving towards on time delivery and first article success. This position will directly influence the history of space exploration and will require your unwavering commitment and unfaltering focus towards safe and repeatable spaceflight.

Responsibilities:

  • Ownership of machine shop personnel and day-to-day operations

  • Conduct performance reviews

  • Responsible for establishing work station assignments, employee training, overtime assignments and back-up for absent employees

  • Maintain and communicate machine shop schedule status to ensure meeting customer expectations

  • Provide first level escalation support to employees regarding HR issues (employee relations, worker’s compensation, disciplinary actions, time cards, PTO requests)

  • Identifying Continuous Improvement opportunities and implementing change to improve process, reduce cycle and setup times

  • Maintain shop measuring equipment calibration program ensuring all relative equipment is calibrated according to schedule

  • Maintain all shop programs. These programs include 5S, Lean, Cleaning and Safety

  • Ensure all team members follow work instructions, quality requirements and processes

  • Ensure accurate machine shop staff data recording. Namely clock-in/clock-out activities

  • Provide continued training and skills development for team members, and mentor early career team member

  • Ensure start-up readiness for production

  • Maintain machine shop organization, safety and cleanliness

  • Support design for manufacturing and provide job planning estimates

  • Ability to perform interviews, evaluate talent and provide hiring recommendations

  • Safely work within an industrial environment

Qualifications:

  • 4 years minimum of leadership experience

  • 7 years minimum experience in machining aerospace components

  • Root cause and corrective action analysis experience

  • Familiarity with KPI metrics

  • Excellent blue print reading skills including GD&T per ASME Y14.5M-1994 standard

  • Strong communication skills with a heavy customer focus

  • Must have a continuous improvement mindset

  • Clear understanding of production versus development environments

  • Fluent in use of precision hand tools

  • Familiar with use of personal computers

  • Self-motivation and ability to prioritize projects to meet completion dates

  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Desired

  • Experience machining nickel-based stainless steel alloys, copper, titanium

  • Tooling and fixture design

  • 5S, Lean Manufacturing or Kaizen experience

  • Knowledge of CAD/CAM tools

  • Experience operating heavy lifting equipment such as cranes and forklifts around flight critical hardware

  • Knowledge and understanding of CMM programming/operation

  • Outside processing knowledge (heat treat, plating, coating, EDM, grinding, etc.)

  • Experience machining tight tolerance, high value components

Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.


Export Control Regulations

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


Background Check

  • Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
  • Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
  • Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
  • Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

  • Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
  • Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
  • Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
  • Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.

title: AR Specialist 2
description:
Here at Savista, we enable our clients to navigate the biggest challenges in healthcare: quality clinical care with positive patient experiences and optimal financial results. We partner with healthcare organizations to problem solve and deliver revenue cycle improvement services that enable their success, support their patients, and nurture their communities, all while living our values of Commitment, Authenticity, Respect and Excellence (CARE).

The Medical Insurance Accounts Receivable Representative is responsible for ensuring the timely collection of outstanding government or commercial healthcare insurance receivables.

Responsibilities:

  • Verifies or obtains patient eligibility and/or authorization for healthcare services performed by searching payer web sites or client eligibility systems, or by conducting phone conversations with the insurance carrier or healthcare providers.
  • Updates patient demographics and/or insurance information in appropriate systems.
  • Conducts research and appropriately statuses unpaid or denied claims.
  • Monitors claims for missing information, authorization and control numbers (ICN//DCN).
  • Researches EOBs for payments or adjustments to resolve claims.
  • Contacts payers by phone or through written correspondence to secure payment of claims.
  • Accesses client systems for information regarding received payments, open claims and other data necessary to resolve claims.
  • Follows guidelines for prioritization, timely filing deadlines, and notation protocols within appropriate systems.
  • Secures medical documentation as required or requested by third party insurance carriers.
  • Obtains billing guidelines and requirements by researching provider billing manuals.
  • Writes appeal letters for technical appeals.
  • Verifies accuracy of underpayments by researching contracts and claims data.
  • In the event of an authorization, coding, level of care and/or length of stay denial, prepares claims for clinical audit processing.
  • Supports nThrive’s Compliance Program by adhering to policies and procedures pertaining to HIPAA, FDCPA, FCRA, and other laws applicable to nThrive’s business practices. This includes: becoming familiar with nThrive’s Code of Ethics, attending training as required, notifying management or nThrive’s Helpline when there is a compliance concern or incident, HIPAA-compliant handling of patient information, and demonstrable awareness of confidentiality obligations.

Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • At least two years of experience in healthcare insurance accounts receivable follow up, working with or for a hospital/hospital system, working directly with government or commercial insurance payers.
  • Experience identifying billing errors and resubmitting claims as well as following up on payment errors, low reimbursement and denials.
  • Experience reviewing EOB and UB-04 forms to conduct A/R activities.
  • Knowledge of accounts receivable practices, medical business office procedures, coordination of benefit rules and denial overturns and third-party payer billing and reimbursement procedures and practices.
  • At least two years of experience with accounts receivable software.
  • Experience navigating payer sites for appeals/reconsiderations, benefits verification and online claims follow up.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate Internet Explorer and Microsoft Office, including the ability to input and sort data in Microsoft Excel and use company email and calendar tools.
  • Demonstrated success working both individually and in a team environment.
  • Demonstrated experience communicating effectively with payers, understanding complex information and accurately documenting the encounter.
  • Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams to achieve goals.
  • Demonstrated ability to meet performance objectives.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience with Epic, Meditech, Cerner, Invision, Paragon, Soarian, Collections Management or STAR.
  • Experience working with or for a hospital/hospital system with more than 250 beds.
  • Experience with both hospital (facility) and physician (pro-fee) A/R.

title: Head of Legal - Property and Projects
location: NSW - Sydney, CBD, Inner West and Eastern Suburbs
description:
Job Description:


Lead the legal strategy behind the projects, infrastructure and partnerships that help deliver better healthcare.

  • Drive legal leadership across nationally significant property and infrastructure projects: Lead legal oversight of complex property transactions, developments, construction projects and strategic initiatives across one of Australia's largest health and aged care organisations.
  • Influence major decisions at the highest levels of the organisation: Partner with executive leaders, Boards, senior operational stakeholders and external advisers to manage legal risk and enable strategic growth across public hospitals, private hospitals, aged care and virtual care.
  • Shape the future of healthcare through property and project excellence: Use your expertise to support the facilities, infrastructure and developments that allow St Vincent's to deliver life-changing care to patients, residents and communities.


About St Vincent's Health Australia

At St Vincent's Health Australia, we are shaping a future health and aged care system that supports people with life-changing care, wherever and whoever they are.


Founded by the Sisters of Charity in 1857, St Vincent's is one of Australia's leading not-for-profit health and aged care organisations. Our 30,000 dedicated people provide compassionate care through public and private hospitals, aged care residences, virtual care and services delivered at home across New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria.


Our vision is for every person to receive excellent and compassionate care through a better and fairer health and aged care system. Together, we are focused on enhancing our impact, connecting care and transforming the system. Our work is grounded in our values of Compassion, Justice, Integrity and Excellence.


About the Opportunity

We are seeking a highly experienced Head of Legal – Property and Projects to join our National Legal Team in Sydney or Melbourne.


Reporting to the National Director Legal and Risk, this executive leadership role is responsible for leading the Property and Projects Practice Group and providing strategic legal direction across St Vincent's extensive national property, infrastructure and capital works portfolio.


You will advise on some of the organisation's most significant legal and commercial matters, including property acquisitions and disposals, leasing arrangements, major redevelopment projects, construction contracts, strategic partnerships and infrastructure investments.

Leading a specialist team of lawyers and legal professionals, you will work closely with executive leaders, Board committees, operational stakeholders and external advisers to manage legal risk and enable the delivery of projects that support the future of healthcare and aged care across Australia.


This is a rare opportunity to combine sophisticated legal practice, people leadership and strategic influence within a purpose-led organisation making a meaningful difference to communities nationwide.



Your Key Responsibilities

As a senior member of the National Legal Team, you will:

  • Lead the Property and Projects Practice Group and provide strategic legal advice across St Vincent's national operations.
  • Oversee legal matters relating to property acquisitions, disposals, leasing, licensing and land use arrangements.
  • Advise on major capital works, infrastructure developments, construction projects and redevelopment initiatives.
  • Develop and implement legal frameworks, systems and processes that support effective project delivery and risk management.
  • Provide legal oversight across the full project lifecycle, from planning and procurement through to delivery and completion.
  • Identify, assess and manage legal and regulatory risks associated with property and projects activities.
  • Partner with executive leaders and senior stakeholders to support organisational priorities and strategic initiatives.
  • Manage external legal providers and ensure the delivery of high-quality, commercially focused legal services.
  • Contribute specialist expertise to broader legal, governance, risk and commercial matters across the organisation.
  • Lead, mentor and develop lawyers and staff within the Property and Projects Practice Group.
  • Build trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including government bodies, consultants, contractors and development partners.


About You

You are a highly accomplished legal leader with 15+ years' post-qualification experience and a proven track record advising on complex property, construction, infrastructure, projects and commercial matters. You have successfully led legal strategy on major transactions, developments and business-critical initiatives, balancing legal risk with commercial outcomes in complex and highly regulated environments.


You are a trusted adviser to executive leadership teams, Boards and senior stakeholders, recognised for your sound judgement, strategic thinking and ability to influence critical decisions. Combining deep technical expertise with strong commercial acumen, you deliver practical solutions that support organisational priorities while safeguarding long-term interests.


An experienced people leader, you have built, led and developed high-performing legal teams and foster cultures of collaboration, accountability and excellence. You are comfortable operating at both strategic and operational levels, navigating competing priorities and leading through complexity.


Most importantly, you are motivated by the opportunity to apply your expertise within a purpose-led organisation. You understand that hospitals, aged care facilities and healthcare infrastructure are fundamental to delivering exceptional care, and you are inspired by the opportunity to help shape the projects, partnerships and investments that will support patients, residents and communities for generations to come.

You Will Bring

  • A tertiary qualification in Law.
  • Admission as a Solicitor or Barrister in Australia.
  • Eligibility to hold a practising certificate without supervision requirements.
  • Significant post-qualification experience in property, construction, infrastructure, projects or commercial law.
  • Experience gained within a leading law firm, major corporation, government organisation or complex in-house legal environment.
  • Demonstrated expertise across property transactions, leasing, development projects, construction contracts and infrastructure matters.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to provide practical, risk-based legal advice.
  • Experience partnering with executive leaders and senior stakeholders.
  • Proven leadership capability, including mentoring and developing legal professionals.
  • Highly developed negotiation, communication and relationship management skills.
  • Strong organisational and project management capability within a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
  • The ability to work strategically while maintaining a practical and solutions-focused approach.
  • A commitment to St Vincent's values and an appreciation of the social purpose of healthcare and aged care services.



Why Join St Vincent's?

  • Lead work that leaves a lasting legacy
    Help shape the hospitals, healthcare facilities and infrastructure that support communities across Australia.
  • Work on high-profile and complex matters
    Advise on property transactions, major developments, construction projects and strategic initiatives across a large and diverse national organisation.
  • Influence at the executive level
    Partner with senior leaders, Board committees, operational executives and key external stakeholders on critical organisational decisions.
  • Lead a specialist legal practice
    Develop and guide a high-performing team while contributing to the broader success of the National Legal function.
  • Join a values-led organisation
    Build your career in an organisation guided by Compassion, Justice, Integrity and Excellence, with a longstanding commitment to delivering better and fairer care.
  • Make a Meaningful Difference
    This is more than a property and projects leadership role. It is an opportunity to help create and maintain the infrastructure, facilities and partnerships that enable life-changing healthcare and aged care services for generations to come.

If you are a senior property, construction or projects lawyer seeking executive exposure, complex legal work and a stronger sense of purpose, we would welcome your application.


Apply Now

Join St Vincent's Health Australia and help us build the environments, facilities and services that support better healthcare outcomes across Australia.


Applications may close before the advertised closing date.

Important Information

Employment is subject to satisfactory pre-employment checks, including identification, right-to-work, reference and nationally coordinated criminal history checks. The successful applicant must also comply with applicable St Vincent's Health Australia policies and screening requirements.



St Vincent's Health Australia welcomes people from all backgrounds and beliefs. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued and empowered to contribute their unique experiences.

The candidate will be expected to apply their expertise and knowledge of aircraft systems for development and analysis of system requirements and usage scenarios.   • Bachelor's Degree in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathamatics and 5 years of Engineering experience, 3 years with a Master Degree or 1 year and PhD.
  • Must have an Active In-Scope DoD Secret Security Clearance that has been granted/renewed within the past 6 years.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an Active Program Specific SAP clearance
  • Experience with Systems Engineering V-Model of development including leadership of Systems Engineering Technical Review (SETR) events

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in technical engineering requirements analysis, development, verification and/or validation.

title: Volunteer Coordinator
description:
Who We Are

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description:

Position Purpose summary:

The Volunteer Coordinator provides support to the Manager of Volunteers, coordinating delivery of all required volunteer administrative support services for The Salvation Army (TSA) Ontario Distribution Centre (ODC) ‘Behind the Shield’ Volunteer Program and as an assist to the Manager of Volunteers other duties where needed. They perform daily tasks related to volunteer administration operations and responds to volunteer inquiries via phone and email and provides a welcoming atmosphere for volunteers entering ODC.

ACCOUNTABILITIES:

  • Triage volunteer scenarios, specifically pre-screening processes for new volunteers, ensuring alignment with volunteer registration acceptance criteria.
  • Ensure all volunteer warehouse supplies inventory levels are maintained, and re-orders are placed in a timely manner to outages.
  • Ensure effective and accurate management of inbound and outbound emails received through the ODC volunteer email account etc.
  • Assist Manager, Volunteers and Durable Goods with the maintaining accurate records of group volunteer opportunity planning where needed.
  • Manage administration of the volunteer shifts in the MyImpact volunteer platform with case-by-case adjustments for corporate team requests.
  • Assist Manager, Volunteers and Durable Goods with yearly strategic volunteer plans and Volunteer Appreciation event.
  • Provide onboarding to new volunteers; ensures volunteers receive, complete, and return required forms in a timely manner.
  • Maintain filing systems for volunteer documentation.
  • Provide orientation of the ODC Warehouse Health and Safety measures to volunteers and provide specific sorting activity orientation.
  • Provide documentation of completed volunteer hours to volunteers, upon request.
  • Seek continually to improve the Volunteer program, processes and policies, and volunteer activities and facilitation documentation, as needed.
  • Ensure ODC volunteer standards and policies are upheld.
  • Responsible for reporting any volunteer problems per policies and procedures.

Volunteer Warehouse Operations:

  • In consultation with the Manager, Volunteers and Durable Goods prepares Volunteer Rooms with snacks, cleanliness, aprons and glove supplies, volunteer orientation documentation.
  • Maintain a clean and organized environment for volunteers in the workplace, such as the volunteer rooms and production areas where volunteers perform activities.
  • Ensure effective and accurate management of volunteers.
  • Facilitate Volunteer Sorting and Bagging Activities and TSA ODC Durable Goods order fulfillment with the volunteers.
  • Ensure the smooth operation of the ODC volunteer functions.
  • Generate daily volunteer outbound reports for both Inventory Management and Manager of Volunteers as required for groups.
  • Provide group volunteer outbound reports to group volunteer team and leader (following the shift). Performs other duties as required.

Warehouse:

  • Perform shipping and receiving of goods using a forklift or other power equipment as certifications allow.
  • Pickup, sort, put-away, pack and ship.
  • Fulfill TSA Ministry Unit requests for durable goods for delivery.
  • Accurately count and weigh product being delivered or shipped.
  • Assist with inventory reconciliation.
  • Use Warehouse Management System to record / facilitate warehouse operations.
  • Perform general cleaning and maintenance tasks of warehouse, yard and equipment as required.
  • Ensure that work is completed in a safe manner, in accordance with the Ontario Occupational Health & Safety Act (OHSA) and TSA policy,

Perform other related duties as required.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • This is a regular full-time position based on 40 hours per week.
  • Overtime will be required during the Christmas season.
  • The Supervisor will set the hours of work and work schedule.
  • Ability to adapt to a flexible work schedule during peaks and/or seasonal times.
  • Work typically performed in an office and warehouse environment with exposure to monotony of work (repetitive tasks).
  • Ability to lift/move up to 39 lbs. without assistance.
  • Responsible for working in compliance with the Ontario Occupational Health & Safety Act (OHSA) and regulations.
  • Comply with warehouse safety and security.
  • Wear the appropriate safety, Personal Protective Equipment, and maintain a clean uniform.

Normal hours of work: Monday to Friday, 6:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., and include an ½ hour unpaid meal break. Shifts may change during the Christmas season.

The above responsibilities must be performed in keeping with The Salvation Army’s Mission, Values, Vision and Values, is a professional manner, upholding our code of conduct.

Education, Qualifications and Certifications:

  • Completion of a formal post-secondary program of two academic years in Warehousing, Supply Chain Management, Inventory Control and Materials Management preferred.

Experience and Skilled Knowledge Requirements:

  • At least 3 years of previous experience, including volunteer management, some supervisory experience, and proven track record of communicating clearly both orally and in writing.
  • Administrative, general clerical and Customer Service.
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office suite.
  • Experience with Volunteer Coordination and Management platform software, such as MyImpact, is an asset.
  • Experience with Inventory Management software, such as Fishbowl, is an asset.

Alternative combinations of education and experience may be considered.

Skills and Capabilities:

  • A high level of integrity, good judgment, and ability to maintain appropriate confidentiality.
  • Represent the organization in a positive, professional, and engaging manner.
  • Lead by example, demonstrate a positive attitude, a strong work ethic, and a willingness to learn.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and independently when required Self-motivated/disciplined; a flexible self-starter with the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills. Must be fully fluent in English reading, writing and verbal.
  • Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills.
  • Self-motivated and disciplined.
  • Ability to work with minimal supervision and demonstrates strong leadership skills.
  • Maturity and ability to exercise good judgment.
  • Strong administrative, time-management and organizational skills.
  • Attention to detail, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
  • Strong integrity and ability to maintain confidentiality with professional ethics and a balanced sense of fairness.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development and training.
  • Ability and willingness to undergo applicable screening and background checks successfully that are satisfactory to The Salvation Army, in its sole discretion (i.e., The Salvation Army Abuse Registry) and provide an original copy of a Background Check screening.
  • Ability and willingness to develop an understanding and support for the mission and purpose of The Salvation Army in Canada and its implications as related to position responsibilities.

Compensation:

The target hiring range for this position is $50,897.60 to $63,627.20 with a maximum of $76,356.80.

Placement in the salary range will be based on factors such as market conditions, internal equity, and candidate experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the role.

Job Description:
This job is responsible for developing and delivering complex requirements to accomplish business goals. Key responsibilities of the job include ensuring that software is developed to meet functional, non-functional and compliance requirements, and solutions are well designed with maintainability/ease of integration and testing built-in from the outset. Job expectations include a strong knowledge of development and testing practices common to the industry and design and architectural patterns.

Job Profile Summary
We are seeking an experienced Front Office Software Developer with a strong focus on Python development to join the Equity Linked Structured Notes Technology team, supporting the Pricing and Booking platform. This role provides an opportunity to work on complex, business-critical systems that have significant visibility across Trading, Structuring, Sales, Quantitative Services, Operations, and Technology teams.

The successful candidate will combine strong software engineering skills with hands-on experience in modern programming languages such as Python, Java, and C#. They will play a key role in the design, development, and enhancement of front-office applications that underpin the Structured Notes business.

Given the highly collaborative nature of the role, it is important that this position is based within the AMRS region to provide effective coverage and partnership with key stakeholders, including the Quantitative Services Group, Trading, Sales, Structuring, and regional Technology teams. Proximity to these groups will enable faster decision-making, stronger collaboration, and more effective execution of strategic initiatives.

This is a critical hire within the Structured Notes Technology organization. The successful candidate will work closely with front-office business partners and technology teams to drive the continued evolution, scalability, and delivery of the Structured Notes technology platform, while contributing to the firm's broader strategic objectives in the Equity Linked Structured Products space.

Responsibilities:

  • Codes solutions and unit test to deliver a requirement/story per the defined acceptance criteria and compliance requirements

  • Designs, develops, and modifies architecture components, application interfaces, and solution enablers while ensuring principal architecture integrity is maintained

  • Mentors other software engineers and coach team on Continuous Integration and Continuous Development (CI-CD) practices and automating tool stack

  • Executes story refinement, definition of requirements, and estimating work necessary to realize a story through the delivery lifecycle

  • Performs spike/proof of concept as necessary to mitigate risk or implement new ideas

  • Automates manual release activities

  • Designs, develops, and maintains automated test suites (integration, regression, performance)

  • Owning the technology stack supporting secondary market activity for Structured Notes within Equity Derivatives

  • Driving delivery of a multi‑year technology roadmap aligned to a major business growth initiative

  • Partnering closely with Trading and Structuring to deliver scalable, performant solutions that meet real‑time front‑office needs

  • Leading system stability, production excellence, and resiliency for mission‑critical platforms

Required Qualifications:

  • Exceptional development skills in any OO or Functional language including but not limited to Python (preferred), C#, Java, or C++

  • 8+ years of experience in technology roles supporting capital markets, derivatives, or structured products

  • Strong technical background with hands‑on experience in modern front‑office systems (e.g., Java, Python, C#, distributed systems, real‑time platforms)

  • Understanding of equity derivatives concepts including pricing, Greeks, lifecycle events, and secondary market dynamics

  • Experience working closely with traders, quants, or structurers in a demanding delivery environment

  • Proven ability to take ownership of complex systems and deliver outcomes in ambiguous problem spaces

  • Strong execution discipline combined with intellectual curiosity and a desire to grow professionally

  • Ability to operate effectively within a large, global organization while driving meaningful change

  • Experience in 3rd line production support.

Job Summary:

As Vice President, People Business Partner, you will lead the People Agenda for the U.S. business and serve as a member of the North America People & Experiences (P&E) leadership team. Reporting to the Chief People Officer and partnering closely with senior business leaders, you will translate business strategy and transformation priorities into organization, talent, workforce, and culture decisions that enable performance and sustainable growth.

You will lead an experienced team of People Business Partners and Talent Acquisition Managers and partner closely across Talent, Organizational Development, Employee Relations, Total Rewards, Legal, Compliance, and other Centers of Excellence and global teams. You will shape organizational effectiveness, talent, employee experience, culture, and workforce strategy across a complex, fast-moving organization.

This role will play an important part in strengthening the organizational capabilities, leadership, and ways of working needed to support the evolving needs of the U.S. business. It requires a commercially minded, high-potential People leader who can move comfortably between enterprise strategy and hands-on execution, using data, judgment, and deep business understanding to create meaningful outcomes for our people and the business. The successful candidate will be visible in the market, staying close to leaders, employees, customers, and the realities of the business.

Who will love this job:

  • A commercially minded People leader who connects business strategy to practical, scalable people solutions.

  • A trusted adviser who builds credibility with senior leaders, challenges constructively, and brings clarity to complex or sensitive decisions.

  • An accomplished, up-and-coming People leader who brings relevant depth across business partnership, organizational effectiveness, talent, and transformation and is ready to grow through a broad, high-impact VP role.

  • A builder who looks critically at operating models, systems, processes, and capabilities and understands what must be strengthened to enable the longer-term People strategy.

  • A people manager who develops strong teams, promotes accountability, and works effectively across Centers of Excellence and global partners.

  • An analytical, pragmatic decision-maker who uses workforce and employee insights to guide decisions, measure impact, and drive meaningful business outcomes.

What you’ll do:

  • Set and execute the U.S. People strategy, translating business and transformation priorities into organization, talent, workforce, and culture plans that strengthen performance, engagement, retention, and operational effectiveness.

  • Serve as a strategic partner to the Pernod Ricard North America Extended Leadership Team, advising on organizational effectiveness, workforce strategy, leadership, talent, culture, and transformation.

  • Lead organizational design and change initiatives, including operating models, workforce structure, decision rights, spans and layers, leadership transitions, role redesign, and new ways of working.

  • Shape the employee experience and engagement agenda by aligning leadership behaviors, people practices, culture, and business priorities and using employee and organizational insights to identify opportunities and measure impact.

  • Strengthen leadership and talent pipelines through talent reviews, succession planning, performance management, development, internal mobility, and strategic career planning in partnership with the Talent Center of Excellence.

  • Lead U.S. strategic workforce planning, including headcount and role prioritization, location and capacity planning, and future capability requirements related to automation, artificial intelligence, evolving business needs, and pipeline growth.

  • Own U.S. Talent Acquisition execution in alignment with Talent COE strategy and standards, ensuring strong pipelines, disciplined hiring delivery, and actionable market and candidate insights that inform talent and business decisions.

  • Use workforce, talent, and business data to measure organizational effectiveness and evaluate the impact of People strategies, investments, and programs.

  • Partner with Total Rewards, Employee Relations, Legal, and Compliance on reward programs, sensitive employee matters, workforce risk, policy, and regulatory requirements across jurisdictions.

  • Lead and develop the People Business Partner and Talent Acquisition teams, strengthening business acumen, analytics, consulting capability, accountability, and operational excellence.

  • Drive continuous improvement across People processes, systems, analytics, and ways of working to strengthen scalability, effectiveness, and the experience of leaders and employees.

  • Act as a credible deputy to the Chief People Officer and contribute to enterprise-wide priorities as a member of the North America People & Experiences leadership team.

What’s in it for me?

Being part of an inclusive and diverse company where professional development and internal career mobility is front-and-center to our talent strategy. This means your career at Pernod Ricard has many possibilities. You'll be part of a culture that celebrates the rich diversity of our people across the globe and be part of our long-standing commitment to making exceptional products, giving back to our communities, and honoring our responsibility to preserve the environment.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • 10+ years of progressive Human Resources leadership experience, including current or recent experience operating at the Vice President level in a business partner or enterprise People leadership role.

  • Demonstrated success advising senior executives and leadership teams through organizational transformation, business change, and complex people decisions.

  • Experience operating successfully in complex, fast-paced, global matrixed organizations, with the leadership maturity and growth potential to make a sustained impact in the role.

  • Deep capability in organizational effectiveness, talent strategy, workforce planning, succession planning, organizational design, change leadership, and employee engagement.

  • Strong business acumen, analytical capability, executive presence, and judgment, with the ability to influence across all levels of an organization.

title: Academic Advisor I or II
description:
Department

College of Health and Human Sciences

About the University

Established in 1965, Metropolitan State University (MSU Denver) was founded to serve students who were underrepresented in higher education whose life paths and experiences did not fit the traditional mold. Sixty years later, the University continues to serve over 16,000 of Colorado’s extraordinary and diverse students, providing them with the foundation on which to build their unique aspirations. As the third largest public institution of higher education in Colorado, MSU Denver is a model university for today’s college students.

Proud of its federal designation as a Hispanic-Serving Institution that also offers graduate programs (gHSI) and the only Seal of Excelencia certified institution in Colorado, the University serves the most diverse undergraduate student population in the state, as well as the most first-generation students. Through affordable, flexible, and holistic education, MSU Denver helps students build essential skills grounded in a multicultural and global perspective that lead to undergraduate and graduate degrees, and career and life success.

At MSU Denver, we are committed to our CADRE values: Community, Access, Diversity, Respect, and Excellence. We strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment where all community members are valued and belong. Our dedication to breaking down barriers to education, fostering open dialogue, and promoting world-class scholarship ensures that we provide exceptional services and innovative learning opportunities for our students, faculty, and staff.

Position Summary

The College of Health and Human Sciences (CHHS) at MSU Denver invites applications for Academic Advisors, either at the Academic Advisor I or Academic Advisor II level.

The Academic Advisor I at MSU Denver is primarily responsible for advising a caseload of students on degree requirements and providing long-term degree planning. Academic advisors help students develop educational goals and define a career path, through use of a variety of advising approaches and tools. Further, they monitor student progress, making targeted outreach to students to address potential obstacles in retention and graduation. Academic advisors also participate in University-wide and unit-specific advising initiatives.

In addition to the responsibilities above, the Academic Advisor II at MSU Denver works with advising leadership, immediate supervisors, and faculty and/or staff where appropriate, to understand advising and retention data and student success implementation strategies. Assisting with and/or participating in recruiting events may also be required.

Responsibilities

Examples of Work Performed

Provide Advising Services to Students

  • Conduct advising sessions with students, assist with course selection, scheduling and registration questions using advising-based technology

  • Utilize knowledge of curriculum to help students with long-term degree planning

  • Prepare and maintain advising documentation in the current student success/customer management system

  • Refer students to appropriate University resources

  • Provide basic information related to career planning, financial literacy, admissions and other applicable information related to student needs

  • Teach students about electronic advising and registration tools and how to best utilize them for success (e.g., Degree Progress Reports, Student Hub, Student Success Collaborative suite, etc.)

  • Participates in New Student Orientation sessions and Registration events.

  • Participation in recruiting events may be required

Monitor Progress and Retention of Assigned Students

  • Utilize advising-based systems to track and engage assigned students who are at-risk of not being retained (Early Alert)

  • Deliver appropriate student-centered outreach

  • Participate in retention initiatives

Professional Development

  • Begin or continue building knowledge of advising techniques and approaches

  • Participate in university-wide and unit specific advising professional development opportunities (e.g., Advising retreats, NACADA webinars, conferences, etc.)

  • Serve on committees, councils, taskforces, etc. where appropriate

Other Duties as Assigned

Required Qualifications

Academic Advisor I

  • Bachelor’s degree

  • Demonstrated experience in a professional setting helping others reach their academic, professional, and/or personal goals

  • Demonstrated experience engaging with the educational needs of a diverse student population

  • Demonstrated problem-solving, prioritizing, and preparation skills

Academic Advisor II

  • Bachelor’s degree

  • Has consistently demonstrated a thorough understanding of and effective execution of Advisor I responsibilities, and alignment with the operational commitments of the MSU Denver advising program

  • Experience using computer-based student information system(s) (e.g., Ellucian Banner, PeopleSoft, CampusVue, etc.)

  • Demonstrated experience with advising techniques or approaches at an accredited institution

  • Demonstrated experience engaging with the educational needs of a diverse student population

  • Demonstrated problem-solving skills

Preferred Qualifications

Academic Advisor I

  • Master’s degree in either Higher Education, College Personnel, Counseling, or an academic discipline

  • Experience using computer-based student information system(s) (e.g., Ellucian Banner, PeopleSoft, CampusVue, etc.)

  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) proficiency desirable

Academic Advisor II

  • Master’s degree in either Higher Education, College Personnel, Counseling, or an academic discipline

  • Demonstrated experience in accessing, understanding, and/or using student data for successful outcomes

  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) proficiency desirable

  • Experience assisting with developing and/or leading trainings, workshops, or presentations

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification. We are most interested in finding the candidate who will best contribute to CHHS and the University.


Schedule Information

  • Full-time

  • Exempt

  • Days of Week: Monday – Friday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

  • Evenings and Weekend Work: Weekend work on rare occasion for orientations

  • Schedule: Hybrid schedule flexibility with in person work as well as some remote opportunities subject to supervisor approval and program needs.

  • Travel: For professional development opportunities only

Salary for Announcement

Under Colorado law, MSU Denver is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. This range takes into account a variety of factors including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

The salary ranges that the University reasonably expects to pay for these positions are established at:

Academic Advisor II: $52,000 – $55,000

These positions are paid monthly and are eligible for MSU Denver benefits.

title: Security Product Manager, Perimeter Defense
description:
Who we are looking for

We are looking for a Security Product Manager, Perimeter Defense reporting directly to the Head of Defensive Engineering.

You will define and drive the strategy, roadmap, governance, and security outcomes for Perimeter Defense. Working across Security, GTS, application teams, and infrastructure teams, you will help ensure the organization's perimeter is continuously understood, assessed, protected, and improved.

This role is focused on bringing together multiple security capabilities and stakeholders to deliver measurable security outcomes and reduce perimeter risk.

Why this role is important to us

The team you will be joining is a part of Global Cyber Security, Defensive Engineering, a function that is vital to protecting the firm, its clients, and its critical business services from cyber threats.

As the organization's technology landscape continues to evolve, maintaining visibility into internet-facing assets and ensuring appropriate security controls are in place is increasingly important. This role helps establish a consistent approach to perimeter security by bringing together capabilities such as attack surface management, vulnerability management, web application protection, responsible disclosure, bug bounty programs, and security testing to improve the overall security posture.

  • Define and maintain the strategy, roadmap, and security outcomes for the Perimeter Defense product.

  • Partner with GTS product owners and engineering teams to ensure security requirements and priorities are reflected in platform roadmaps.
  • Help drive continuous assurance through attack surface management, vulnerability management, security testing, and related security capabilities.
  • Define onboarding requirements and security standards for new perimeter-facing services and technologies.
  • Establish metrics, reporting, and governance processes to measure effectiveness and communicate risk and progress to leadership.

  • Strong communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to translate security risks and requirements into practical business and technology outcomes.
  • Understanding of cybersecurity concepts such as vulnerability management, perimeter security, application security, cloud security, or attack surface management.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

¡Tu energía construye un futuro más sostenible!

title: Mortgage Specialist
description:
Application Deadline:

09/29/2026

Address:

595 8th Ave SW West Tower

Job Family Group:

Retail Banking Sales & Service

Join BMO – imagine the possibilities. Are you looking for a chance to let your entrepreneurial spirit shine and turn potential into performance with great earning possibilities? Becoming a BMO® Mortgage Specialist can offer you all that and much more. Expect to fill an important and rewarding role – helping customers make their dream of home ownership a reality. You will be provided with industry-leading training and support and will be able to build your existing referral network with our competitive referral programs to achieve your full potential.

Cultivates, builds, and manages relationships with a referral network to build a pipeline of new mortgage business and increase BMO’s share of the home financing market. Actively identifies sales opportunities and refers to BMO colleagues as appropriate. Develops and executes effective marketing and sales programs to drive business results. Follows corporate policies, operating directives, legal and regulatory requirements.

  • Proactively contacts referral and origination sources identified through the creation of national partnerships and/or creates local partnerships to lead discussions about home financing solutions.
  • Assists with the implementation of targeted marketing programs, promotions, and other initiatives.
  • Actively searches for cross-sell and up-sell opportunities for positioning to the branch to achieve individual sales and profitability goals.
  • Supports the delivery of targeted marketing programs, promotions, and other initiatives.
  • Seeks opportunities to expand network by obtaining referrals and originations from existing relationships.
  • Establishes and enhances the Bank’s community presence by participating in trade shows, conferences, and related events.
  • Serves a customer advocate during application and processing activities.
  • Completes onboarding activities as required.
  • Delivers exceptional customer service that builds trust through expertise, responsive service, and support.
  • Guides customers throughout mortgage application and processing activities.
  • Partners with branch teams to properly hand off customers, finalize mortgage documentation, and refer customers with non-mortgage needs.
  • Resolves or escalates issues to meet customer expectations and ensures funds are advanced in a timely manner.
  • Provides customers with friendly, courteous, and professional service in response to queries and requests to identify client needs for banking products (e.g. everyday banking, lending, and investment) and refer to appropriate BMO partners.
  • Stays abreast of consumer needs, industry trends, best practices, and the regulatory requirements, policies, and procedures for mortgage products and services.
  • Addresses customer service issues according to established parameters, escalating persistent or complex matters to more senior staff or other departments for resolution.
  • Develops solutions and makes recommendations based on an understanding of the business strategy and stakeholder needs.
  • Provides advice and guidance to assigned business/group on implementation of solutions.
  • Supports the execution of strategic initiatives in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Helps determine business priorities and best sequence for execution of business / group strategy.
  • Conducts independent analysis and assessment to resolve strategic issues.
  • Liaises with various BMO teams and customers to ensure satisfactory completion and/or fulfillment of the home financing application.
  • Documents updates in BMO’s internal systems to ensure employees have access to the status of outstanding customer opportunities, transactions, and problems / issues.
  • Analyzes data and information to provide insights and recommendations.
  • Gathers and formats data into regular and ad-hoc reports and dashboards.
  • Provides input into the planning and implementation of operational programs.
  • Executes routine tasks (e.g. service requests, transactions, queries, etc.) within relevant service level agreements.
  • Organizes work information to ensure accuracy and completeness.
  • Engages with referral network to create strong relationships that generate referrals and mortgage originations for clients requiring real estate lending solutions.
  • Completes all necessary transactions in compliance with guidelines and other requirements to maintain operational integrity.
  • Focus may be on a business/group.
  • Thinks creatively and proposes new solutions.
  • Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
  • Works mostly independently.
  • Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
  • Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

  • Typically between 3 - 5 years of relevant experience and post-secondary degree in related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • If a Credit Qualifiable job, Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the credit portfolio requirements and qualification standards.
  • In-depth understanding of the mortgage lending process and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Strong interpersonal, sales, customer service, and negotiation skills.
  • Expert knowledge of self-management and teamwork, personal lending, relationship sales and management.
  • Functional knowledge of personal banking, investments, trust services, business and commercial lending, and cash management.
  • Strong knowledge of the broader real estate industry and mortgage market.
  • Strong negotiation skills.
  • Specialized knowledge from education and/or business experience.
  • Verbal & written communication skills - In-depth.
