title: Lab Coordination Assistant, Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering
description:
Engineering a world of possibilities

Colorado School of Mines is seeking a Lab Coordinator Assistant to support the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering (MME). Reporting to the Lab Coordinator III, this role assists with building operations, equipment installation and maintenance, facility improvements, and other activities that support the department’s education and research mission.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Laboratory Support (40%)

  • Support efforts for general laboratory improvements (those not managed by specific lab manager) through collaboration directly with faculty and lab managers.
  • Provide supervision, oversight and instruction of students performing projects that require fabrication
  • Ensure that the necessary equipment, materials, and supplies related to the general labs for functional and available to students and faculty
  • Enforce all safety rules and environmental regulations
  • Purchase and when necessary, fabricate equipment, tools and supplies used in the general/shared research labs related to classes, student projects and research lab efforts
  • Ensures all lab equipment is running efficiently and properly in the research labs
  • If needed, repair and/or coordinate the repair of research lab equipment
  • Provide technical support in the design, fabrication and use of various laboratory equipment and tools
  • Coordinate facility modifications and repairs with plant facilities and other departments
  • Identify, and discuss infrastructure problems and propose solutions if lab restructuring is needed
  • As needed, responsible for ensuring that malfunctioning equipment is repaired quickly and economically
  • Assist in managing the Blastercard system for all new Hill Hall personnel
  • Assist with physical cylinder management within Hill Hall
  • Other related tasks as assigned by Lab Coordinator III

Building Management Support (40%)

  • Assists in the submittal of Facilities work orders to get building maintenance performed and or safety issues corrected
  • Assists Lab Coordinator III in Determining how best to repair malfunctioning equipment quickly and economically and ensures completion.
  • Assists Lab Coordinator III to ensure that department laboratories and work spaces are compliant with Fire Safety regulations.
  • Helps make recommendations to faculty concerning new equipment requirements as to support systems and infrastructure required for safe operation
  • Assists Lab Coordinator III in upgrading safety plans. For example, as new equipment is added, ensures that procedures to operate the equipment are added to the safety plan.

Technical Assistance (15%)

  • Students with little or no experience will often overestimate their abilities with equipment. The technician must help make decisions on how to address unsafe or improper machine usage
  • If equipment fails, the technician must be able to diagnose and then troubleshoot and repair (or coordinate repair) of shop and laboratory equipment. Repairs must be timely and economical.

Other Duties as Assigned (5%)

  • Other duties as assigned to meet the objectives goals of the program and/or Mines.

JOB DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Physical Requirements: must be able to lift 50 lbs
  • Potential Environmental Conditions/Hazards: Should be able to use a half mask respirator and pass a fit test.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Level of Education and Experience:

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • One (1) year of experience supporting laboratory, machine shop, fabrication, facilities maintenance, manufacturing, technical operations, engineering, research, or related environments.
  • An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience may be considered.

Certifications and Licenses:

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain training required to safely operate laboratory and fabrication equipment.
  • Must be able to wear a respirator and successfully pass a respirator fit test.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities and Other Attributes (KSAOs):

  • Basic knowledge of shop equipment, hand tools, power tools, laboratory equipment, or mechanical systems.
  • Ability to perform routine troubleshooting, maintenance, and minor repairs on equipment.
  • Knowledge of workplace safety practices and ability to follow established safety procedures.
  • Ability to read and follow technical manuals, operating procedures, and safety documentation.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with faculty, staff, students, vendors, and facilities personnel.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and respond to equipment and facility maintenance needs in a timely manner.
  • Demonstrated customer service and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to supervise and instruct students in the safe operation of tools and equipment.
  • Proficiency with basic computer applications, including Microsoft Office and electronic work-order systems.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and work in laboratory, machine shop, and research environments.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Desired Level of Education and Experience:

  • Associate's degree, technical certificate, or bachelor's degree in Metallurgical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Technology, Industrial Technology, Engineering Technology, or a closely related field.
  • Two (2) or more years of experience in a laboratory, research, fabrication, machine shop, manufacturing, facilities, or engineering support environment.
  • Experience in an academic, research, higher education, or scientific laboratory setting.

Certifications and Licenses:

  • Forklift certification.
  • First Aid/CPR certification.
  • Machine shop, welding, fabrication, or industrial equipment certifications.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities and Other Attributes (KSAOs):

  • Knowledge of laboratory safety programs, hazardous materials handling, and environmental compliance requirements.
  • Experience coordinating equipment installation, maintenance, or repair activities.
  • Experience purchasing laboratory equipment, tools, supplies, or technical materials.
  • Ability to fabricate simple components and fixtures to support laboratory operations.
  • Working knowledge of building systems and facility infrastructure.
  • Electrical troubleshooting, controls, or industrial equipment maintenance experience.
  • Familiarity with compressed gas cylinder management and laboratory access control systems.
  • Experience supporting student design projects, instructional laboratories, or engineering research activities.

TOTAL REWARDS

Salary Rate: $69,085-$76,760 annually

Mines takes into consideration a combination of candidate’s education, training and experience as well as the position’s scope and complexity, the discretion and latitude required in the role, work location, and external market and internal value when determining a salary level for potential new employees.

Benefits: Colorado School of Mines offers a robust portfolio of benefits for all employees. For this role, that includes:

  • Flexible health and dental care options

  • Generous sick/vacation time: 13 paid holidays per year – including a week-long winter break for the entire campus.

  • Fully vested retirement plan on first day of employment, with generous employer contribution

  • Tuition benefits (6 credits per year for employees, 50 percent discount for dependents)

  • Free RTD Ecopass for regional bus and lightrail


All Mines employees also have access to discount programs through the State of Colorado and free tickets for Mines Athletics home games, as well as access to the state-of-the-art Recreation Center (fitness classes and training, swimming pool and more) and equipment rentals through the Outdoor Rec Center. We are proud to have an on-campus daycare center. For more details about benefits at Mines, visit mines.edu/human-resources/benefits.

HOW TO APPLY

Priority review of applications will begin on September 28th and continue until filled. Applications must complete an online application (personal information, demographic information, veteran status) and upload the following (all required):

  • Upload a resume or CV

  • Upload a cover letter

Applicants will notice there is only one upload box for all materials. This posting may be used to fill more than one vacancy based on business needs. Contact Kathleen Feighny in HR at kfeighny@mines.edu​ with any application questions. Successful completion of a background investigation is required for this position.

About Mines & Golden, CO

When the world looks for answers, the world looks to Mines.

Colorado School of Mines is a top-ranked public university solving the grand challenges facing our society, particularly those related to the Earth, energy and the environment. Founded in 1874 with specialties in mining and metallurgy, Mines’ scope and mission have continually expanded to meet the needs of industry and society. Today, we are the No. 36 public university in the nation, recognized for our innovation and undergraduate teaching in science, technology engineering and math (U.S. News and World Report, 2025).

Mines graduates are change makers, boundary breakers and problem solvers. Since our earliest days, a Mines education has been and continues to be a transformational opportunity, with one of the strongest returns on investment out there for talented STEM students of all backgrounds.

At the same time, Mines faculty members are pushing their fields in new directions, whether that’s manufacturing, space resources, quantum engineering, carbon capture or more. Mines was recently classified as a R1 “Very High Activity” research institution by Carnegie, a notable feat for any university but particularly one of our size.

That size – roughly 8,200 undergraduate and graduate students – also translates to a close-knit campus community, where employees have opportunities to get involved in multiple ways, continued professional learning is valued and everyone can make an impact.

Community Alliance groups bring together employees for professional development, networking, and community involvement, and all Mines employees also have access to the wealth of activities happening every day on campus – nationally-renowned speakers, special events and Mines traditions like Engineering Days, just to name a few.

And don’t get us started on our hometown. We are located in the heart of Golden, Colorado --with its charming historic downtown and nearby hiking trails – and in close proximity to all that Denver and the Rocky Mountains have to offer. That includes the sunny, high-altitude climate and outstanding outdoor recreation opportunities that make the Denver area an ideal place to live, work and play.

Are you looking for an inspiring, mission-driven workplace where you can contribute to solving the world’s problems and educating the next generation of change makers? Are you an individual who values a community where our individual perspectives and experiences enrich the educational and work experience?

Look to Mines.

title: Registered Surveyor
description:
This is a key statutory and technical role supporting safe, accurate and compliant underground mining operations. You will lead mine surveying activities, maintain accurate survey control and plans, and provide practical technical support across mine planning, development, longwall and operational activities.

You will work closely with Mining, Technical Services and operational teams to ensure survey information is accurate, accessible and delivered in line with legislative, site and company requirements.

What you will be doing

As the Registered Mine Surveyor, you will:

  • Prepare, maintain and certify statutory mine plans and survey records.
  • Maintain accurate underground and surface survey control.
  • Plan, coordinate and complete underground survey activities.
  • Provide survey support for development, longwall, infrastructure and mine planning activities.
  • Ensure survey data, field notes, calculations, designs and records are accurately maintained.
  • Review survey results and identify any discrepancies, hazards or operational risks.
  • Provide technical advice to mine planning, engineering and operational teams.
  • Oversee and authorise survey work completed by employees and contractors.
  • Maintain clear survey handovers between rosters and shifts.
  • Participate in incident investigations and complete surveys of relevant incident areas when required.
  • Ensure surveying activities comply with legislation, recognised standards and the site Safety and Health Management System.
  • Support the development and mentoring of surveyors and other technical personnel.

Internal surveying standards require clear roster handovers and authorisation by the Registered Mine Surveyor before project survey work is undertaken

What you will bring

To be successful, you will ideally have:

  • A recognised tertiary qualification in Surveying or Spatial Science.
  • Current registration with the Surveyors Board of Queensland.
  • A current mining endorsement suitable for appointment as a Registered Mine Surveyor in Queensland coal mining.
  • Demonstrated experience in underground coal mine surveying.
  • Strong knowledge of Queensland coal mining legislation and mine surveying requirements.
  • Experience preparing, maintaining and certifying statutory mine plans.
  • Practical experience with underground survey control, traverses, set-outs and mine development surveys.
  • Competency using modern survey equipment and relevant mine surveying software.
  • Strong attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining accurate technical records.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively with technical and operational teams.
  • A strong commitment to safety, risk management and compliance.
  • A current Australian driver’s licence.

The internal appointment requirements identify a relevant Surveying or Spatial Science qualification, current competencies and registration with an appropriate mining endorsement. Queensland’s Surveyors Board also states that mine plans must be certified by a registered surveyor with a mining endorsement.

  • Permanent, full-time position – Monday to Friday roster
  • Based at Moranbah North Mine in Moranbah, Queensland.
  • FIFO - Brisbane - Moranbah return flights (salary sacrifice)
  • DIDO, and subsidised residential options available
  • Competitive salary + 12% superannuation and annual bonus
  • Supportive and experienced Technical Services team.
  • Opportunities for ongoing professional and technical development.
  • Pre-employment requirements will include relevant medical, background and qualification checks.

What we offer
When you join Anglo American, you can expect to enjoy a competitive salary and benefits package and a range of flexible work arrangements that support the balance of work, family and individual circumstances. But more than this, you’ll find yourself in an environment where the opportunities for learning and growth are second to none. From technical training to leadership programs, we bring out the best in our people. There are plenty of opportunities to move onwards and upwards too.

Who we are
We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies. Anglo American is a leading global mining company focused on the responsible production of copper, premium iron ore and crop nutrients future enabling products that are essential for decarbonising the global economy, improving living standards, and food security. Our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively to unlock enduring value from precious natural resources for our shareholders, for the benefit of the communities and countries in which we operate, and for society as a whole. Anglo American is re-imagining mining to improve people’s lives.

Background checks
Successful candidates will be required to complete background screening which may include a criminal check and validation of qualifications.

Inclusion and Diversity
Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How we are committed to your safety
Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies from drones to data analytics that are helping to make mining safer.

title: Senior Technical Lead, Index Distribution Engineering
description:
FTSE Russell is a leading global provider of financial services, specialising in the creation and management of indexes, data, and analytic solutions. As part of the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), we support investors worldwide in making informed decisions across asset classes, investment strategies, and market segments. Our products are trusted by institutional and retail investors, asset managers, and pension funds to benchmark performance, build investment portfolios, and manage risk.

Job Summary

We're seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join the team building next-generation distribution capabilities for our index products. You'll be delivering index data to the global financial community across multiple channels including APIs, cloud data platforms, file-based delivery, and AI-native protocols. Reliability, security, and data quality are non-negotiable as we build out scalable, cloud-native infrastructure.

The ideal candidate is a self-sufficient, technically excellent engineer who can lead through architectural clarity, thorough code review, and hands-on delivery. You combine strong expertise in system design, data modelling, and debugging with genuine passion for how AI tooling is redefining software engineering. This is an individual contributor role where you will lead through the quality of your thinking and your engineering standards.

AI-First Engineering This team operates with an AI-first approach. We expect hands-on experience with AI development tooling: terminal-based agents, AI-augmented IDEs, and automated workflows. You are ultimately accountable for production quality, security, and correctness. This means owning infrastructure review, security validation, system observability, and operational guardrails.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and scale cloud-native distribution infrastructure with high resilience and performance requirements.
  • Own system design and data modelling for sophisticated, multi-schema relational databases serving dynamic data workloads.
  • Develop and maintain infrastructure as code, ensuring environments are reproducible, version-controlled, and secure.
  • Design and implement test strategies including integration, contract, and end-to-end validation.
  • Build secure, well-documented APIs and data delivery services for institutional financial clients.
  • Lead technical direction through architectural guidance, code review, and pairing.
  • Partner with product, operations, and client-facing teams to translate requirements into robust technical solutions.

Tech Stack

  • Development: TypeScript, Angular/React, Python, SQL, OpenAPI
  • Cloud: AWS (Lambda, API Gateway, S3, SQS, SNS, Aurora, and others as required)
  • Databases: PostgreSQL, Apache Iceberg, DynamoDB, VectorDB (e.g. ChromaDB)
  • IaC and CI/CD: Terraform, AWS CLI, GitLab
  • AI Development: Agentic AI tooling (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude Code)

Experience We Value

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience.
  • Strong expertise in system design, distributed systems, and relational data modelling.
  • Solid experience building and operating cloud-native applications on AWS.
  • Ability to write and maintain infrastructure as code (Terraform or equivalent).
  • Experience designing test strategies at multiple levels of the testing pyramid.
  • Proficiency with AI development tooling and a clear understanding of how to use AI to accelerate delivery while maintaining quality.
  • Strong debugging skills across distributed systems.
  • Basic understanding of financial services or capital markets.
  • Effective collaboration and the ability to communicate technical decisions to non-technical audiences.

How We Work

The Distribution team drives the development of innovative and secure products that power our services and meet the evolving needs of our clients. We foster a culture of engineering excellence, solving real-world problems with purpose and ambition. We're looking for skilled and passionate engineers to drive the future of modern solutions working with leading AI development tools.

  • Build with purpose. Start with why. Define the problem before reaching for a solution.
  • Customer driven. Work backwards from client needs and build products to address real-world problems.
  • Technically courageous. Go beyond your comfort zone and push boundaries to deliver excellence.
  • Learn and be curious. Continuously seek feedback, learn in formal and informal settings, actively share knowledge.
  • Act as owners. Operate as though it is your business. Make thoughtful trade-offs and deliver long-term value.
  • Lead with data. Validate assumptions, stay close to the details, act decisively.
  • Build responsibly, deliver incrementally. Look for the small opportunities and milestones to build ambitious solutions.
  • AI-native by default. Use AI tooling as a force multiplier, frame problems clearly, validate continually, and own the output.

Location: London (Hybrid, 3 days/week in office)

Career Stage:

Manager

Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, quality, and continuous improvement. If you're ready to take your career to the next level and make a significant impact, we'd love to hear from you.

LSEG is a leading global financial markets infrastructure and data provider. Our purpose is driving financial stability, empowering economies and enabling customers to create sustainable growth.

Our purpose is the foundation on which our culture is built. Our values of Integrity, Partnership, Excellence and Change underpin our purpose and set the standard for everything we do, every day. They go to the heart of who we are and guide our decision making and everyday actions.

title: Software Developer (Mid-Level)
description:
We are seeking a talented Software Developer (Mid-Level) who will contribute independently to the development, integration, and support of modern applications using Java and Go, while gaining exposure to frontend/UI technologies and scripting. This role will focus on delivering high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions, with ownership of assigned components and customer issues from start to finish. The successful candidate will apply sound technical judgment, take responsibility for low-level design decisions, and demonstrate a solid understanding of software security principles, including practical cryptography and PKI, within a collaborative team environment.

Here are the core functions, responsibilities, and expectations for this role:

  • Independently investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve customer and internal issues, including root-cause analysis and implementation of effective solutions.
  • Design and implement backend services, UI applications, third-party integrations, and REST services using Java/Spring, Golang, frontend technologies (such as Angular), and/or scripting solutions.
  • Own and maintain integrations with third-party products and external systems, including handling API changes, failures, and version upgrades.
  • Take responsibility for delivering complete solutions, including production code, unit and integration tests, design documentation, performance analysis, and product support artifacts.
  • Participate actively in code reviews, both receiving and providing constructive feedback to improve code quality and maintainability.
  • Apply low-level design principles to components and services, considering performance, security, scalability, and maintainability.
  • Perform scripting and automation tasks using shell scripting on Linux and PowerShell on Windows to improve efficiency and reliability.
  • Work with containerized applications using Docker and contribute to deployment, monitoring, and troubleshooting in production environments.
  • Demonstrate awareness of production systems by analyzing logs, metrics, and alerts, and participating in incident analysis and remediation.
  • Additional tasks associated with this position may be assigned in response to company initiatives and business needs.

More information about this role:

  • This is a full-time hybrid position reporting to our Ottawa office 3 to 4 days a week.
  • The targeted compensation package for this role is between CAD 95K and CAD 115K, subject to internal equity and years of experience. We may make further adjustments through an approval process if the targeted compensation range needs to be modified based on business needs and market trends.

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or equivalent is strongly recommended

Experience:

  • 3 - 6+ years of relevant corporate or commercial experience in a software development role.
  • Java and Golang are required or strongly preferred, with hands-on exposure to development technologies such as Java (Maven, Spring framework) and Golang toolchains required or strongly preferred.
  • Solid experience designing and consuming REST APIs, working within microservices-based architectures, and integrating with external systems.
  • Experience developing software in a professional environment, including source control, bug tracking systems, testing frameworks, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Strong working knowledge of Linux environments is required.
  • Strong English language communication skills, both written and verbal, are required.

Technical Knowledge (Preferred)

  • Strong understanding of software security principles, including authentication, authorization, practical cryptography, and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI).
  • Experience integrating with third-party products, services, and APIs.
  • Working knowledge of Docker and containerized application concepts.
  • Experience with frontend technologies such as Angular, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS is a plus.
  • Proficiency with scripting languages such as Bash or PowerShell is a plus.

Ideal Candidate Profiles, Talents, and Desired Qualifications:

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work independently.
  • Demonstrated ownership of tasks and the ability to deliver solutions with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to make sound technical decisions at the component level and raise risks or concerns proactively.
  • Strong collaboration and interpersonal skills for working effectively in a global team environment.
  • Clear and confident communication skills, capable of explaining technical topics to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

  • Sustaining Support: Provide advanced technical support for process control and automation configuration during commercial and clinical production.

  • Root Cause Analysis: Lead technical root-cause analyses, deviation investigations, and troubleshooting for complex electrical, instrumentation, and equipment control systems.

  • Project Leadership: Lead approved engineering projects and continuous improvement initiatives, aligning automation upgrades with DMO and site strategies.

  • Tech Transfer & NPI: Lead engineering assessments, design configuration modifications, and support clinical validation runs for New Product Introductions (NPIs).

  • Change Control: Manage high-level system owner duties including automation change control assessments, maintenance scheduling, and compliance oversight.

  • Audit Readiness: Maintain all DeltaV systems in a GMP-compliant, audit-ready state and represent the automation department during internal and external regulatory inspections.

  • Digital Innovation: Identify, design, and deploy paperless and digital manufacturing tools to support the facility's advanced automation vision.

  • Operational Excellence: Actively participate in GEMBA walks and Go-Sees, and author detailed technical specifications and SOPs.

Qualifications

Required

  • In-depth working knowledge of Batch Control Systems (ISA S88/S95) including design, configuration, testing, and commissioning.

  • Advanced understanding of industry standards: cGMPs, GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11, CSV/SDLC methodologies, and deviation management.

Preferred

  • Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and foster a growth mindset in junior engineering team members.

  • Exposure or involvement in Regulatory Audits

Required Skills:

Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing, DeltaV DCS, Emerson DeltaV, ISA88, Manufacturing Automation, Process Control Systems, Root Cause Analysis (RCA)

Preferred Skills:

MES Integration, Technical Leadership, Technical Mentoring

description:
Company Overview

Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

Field Services


Job Description

Técnico de Mantenimiento

El Técnico de Mantenimiento es responsable de asegurar la operatividad y el mejoramiento de los sistemas tecnológicos asignados en terreno. El objetivo principal es garantizar el cumplimiento de los niveles de servicio (SLA) comprometidos con nuestros clientes mineros, actuando como un nexo técnico confiable y autónomo para la resolución de incidencias en faena.

Responsabilidades / Expectativas

  • Asegurar la disponibilidad técnica: Mantener la continuidad operativa de los sistemas de radiofrecuencia, redes y energía en condiciones de misión crítica.

  • Ejecución de mantenimiento: Realizar tareas preventivas y correctivas en infraestructura tecnológica, incluyendo sistemas de antenas, radios y equipos de soporte eléctrico.

  • Gestión de incidencias: Registrar y documentar meticulosamente todas las interacciones y fallas detectadas utilizando sistemas internos de gestión para asegurar el seguimiento de casos.

  • Interfaz con el cliente: Actuar como el principal punto de contacto en terreno para clientes internos y externos que reportan problemas, asegurando una comunicación clara y profesional.

title: Office Coordinator
description:
The Office Coordinator supports the effective day-to-day operation of the Chicago office while providing executive administrative support to designated leaders within the Intellectual Property (IP) team. This role helps ensure a professional, welcoming, and well-organized office environment and serves as a flexible administrative resource for office needs, IP leadership support, and Corporate special projects as business needs arise. Success in this position requires strong organization, sound judgment, discretion, attention to detail, and the ability to manage shifting priorities with a service-oriented mindset.

At J.S. Held, we pride ourselves on fostering a positive work culture that is inclusive. The Office Coordinator will play a key role in championing the company's values and contributing to a dynamic and supportive workplace.

Job Responsibilities:

Visitor and Communication Management

  • Welcome visitors, clients, and employees and maintain professional reception experience.

  • Screen visitors, notify the appropriate party, and support office access and safety procedures.

  • Answer, screen, and route incoming calls and provide accurate information in person, by phone, and by email.

Executive Assistant Support for Intellectual Property

  • Manage calendars, schedule meetings, and help resolve scheduling conflicts for designated IP leaders.

  • Coordinate travel, itineraries, expenses, and related administrative needs.

  • Support internal and external meetings, including rooms, virtual meeting details, materials, catering, and follow-up tracking when needed.

  • Prepare and format routine presentations, reports, correspondence, and other administrative materials.

  • Handle sensitive information with discretion and serve as a professional point of contact for clients and colleagues.

Office Administration and Facilities Support

  • Maintain a professional, organized, and well-stocked office environment, including reception areas, common spaces, supplies, and breakroom inventory.

  • Receive, sort, and distribute mail, deliveries, and office communications.

  • Support office-related payments, approvals, expense tracking, budget inputs, and administrative procedures tied to office operations.

  • Assist with research, coordination, document preparation, meeting support, and follow-up tracking.

description:

title: Social Work Recruitment and Placement Coordinator
description:
Please Note: Internal Employees, please access the Jobs Hub in Workday to apply for the position.

ABOUT US

University of Massachusetts Global is a private, nonprofit affiliate of the University of Massachusetts, created to help working adults change their lives through flexible, high-quality education built for real life. Regionally accredited by the WASC Senior College and University Commission (WSCUC) and recognized by U.S. News & World Report among the Best Online Programs for 13 consecutive years (2013–2025), the university has a long track record of online innovation. Students across 49 states and internationally can upskill, reskill, and move forward without putting life on hold through technology-enabled, real-world learning.​ With 55+fully online, career-focused programs designed around the realities of work, family, and constant change, we remain ever-focused on developing future-ready learners who can thrive in a rapidly shifting world.





Candidates must currently reside in California for consideration.






ABOUT THE ROLE



The grant-funded Social Work Recruitment and Placement Coordinator supports the administration of the California Social Work Education Capacity Expansion grant (SWECE) for the Master of Social Work program. The role focuses on outreach, recruitment, and student field placement in underserved California communities, in collaboration with Strategic Partnership Associates and Social Work faculty and staff. Works closely with the MSW Program Director and MSW Field Director to meet grant requirements and coordinate field placements. Specifically, this position provides comprehensive support to students seeking field placement/supplemental supervision, field faculty, agency supervisors, directors and executive directors through implementation of placement procedures and policy.

The position is grant funded and is anticipated to end by June 30, 2027.​​

TYPE OF SUPERVISION:

Receive ​close supervision​ from the ​Program Director, MSW​.

  • ​​Close Supervision — indicates that the incumbent is assigned duties according to specific procedures. Work is checked frequently, and in addition there may be formal training.​

POSITION DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Percentage

​​Outreach & Recruitment

  • ​Collaborate with Strategic Partnership team to perform outreach in underserved California communities, publicize the MSW program, and recruit students from underrepresented populations​

  • Engage in targeted recruitment for field placement opportunities in students’ local communities supporting students in locating field sites.

​​35%​

Field Placement Coordination & Student Support

  • ​​Coordinate field placement process for students and ensure that applicable students are placed at appropriate field sites that satisfy the Field Program guidelines and HCAI grant’s criteria.
    ​

  • Provide guidance to students in locating field sites.Serve as university liaison and representative around field placement inquiries from internal and external stakeholders.

  • Monitor field agencies to ensure proper supervision and task assignment to students in practicum roles.

  • Respond to field placement questions from students, site supervisors, and agency directors.

  • Troubleshoot student placement issues in coordination with the field director/assistant field director, field instructors, field practicum specialist and other university staff/faculty.

  • Inform students, directors of sites, and site supervisors about field policies, procedures and expectations.

35%

Field Agency Identification & Vetting

  • Identify and assess agencies in underserved California communities to serve as field placement sites for MSW students.

  • Track and maintain data on student intern placements by term in coordination with the Field Director

25%

  • Perform other duties related to the SWECE grant, as assigned.

5%

TOTAL

100%

POSITION SPECIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS:

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, CERTIFICATION AND/OR LICENSES:

  • Master of Social Work degree from a CSWE-accredited MSW program

  • Prefer 2+ years post-master's experience placing MSW students for field practicum in a university online platform

  • Prefer some experience engaging in outreach or student recruitment events

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

​​

  • ​Knowledge of academic processes in college/university setting.

  • ​Excellent interpersonal and communications skills.

  • ​Highly developed organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • ​Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint) or equivalent Google Workspace tools (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides)

  • ​Able to leverage AI-powered tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, ChatGPT, Grammarly, or similar) to improve productivity, streamline communication, draft content, summarize information, and support day-to-day administrative tasks

  • ​Ability to exercise independent judgment, demonstrate tact and diplomacy, and maintain a high level of confidentiality.

  • ​Ability to problem solve, troubleshoot, and work under pressure.

  • ​Ability to work effectively within a collaborative environment.

  • ​Substantial experience in an academic environment is desired.

​​

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Electronic Devices and Software: ​Strong competence in Microsoft Office is expected. Knowledge of SharePoint and Sonia is preferred.​

Contact with Students: ​Frequent​

Contact with Faculty and/or Staff: ​Frequent​

Contact with Community and Vendors: ​Frequent​

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:

Working conditions are generally normal for an office environment. Position may be required to work flexible hours given the varied availabilities of field site agency personnel and other stakeholders. California residency is required, as travel within California is required approximately 1-4 times a year. Applicants for this position are subject to a background check and a criminal history review.

The hiring range for this position is $25.00-$30.00 an hour. Offers are determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to geographical location, knowledge, skills, years

BENEFITS AND PERKS

At the University of Massachusetts Global, we support your total well-being with flexible and meaningful benefits:

title: Senior Cyber Incident Responder
description:
Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. As we shape the future of healthcare, we are leveraging advanced technologies, intelligent digital solutions and data-driven innovation across our operations to enhance how work gets done and deliver greater value to customers and patients. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.


Labcorp is a global leader in diagnostic testing and drug development solutions, helping healthcare providers, researchers, and patients make informed decisions that advance care. Join us in our mission to improve health and improve lives.

Work Schedule

This is a full‑time, exempt (salaried) position assigned to a First Shift schedule, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Business needs may occasionally require flexibility in work hours, including earlier, later, or additional hours, with reasonable notice provided when possible.

Applicants who live within 35 miles of either the Burlington, NC or Durham, NC location will follow a hybrid schedule. This schedule includes a minimum of three in-office days per week at an assigned location, either Burlington or Durham, supporting both collaboration and flexibility.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as the lead responder for validated cyber incidents—prioritizing threats that could impact clinical operations, electronic health records (EHR), connected medical devices, or protected health information (PHI).
  • Coordinate with technical and clinical stakeholders to contain and remediate threats across hospitals, clinics, and remote care environments.
  • Drive improvements to the Incident Response Plan—ensuring readiness for ransomware, business email compromise, and other threats.
  • Lead triage, containment, and root cause analysis of events affecting clinical applications, patient portals, imaging systems, and backend infrastructure.
  • Analyze logs and EDR telemetry from a wide range of systems—medical devices, cloud applications, employee workstations, and data exchange platforms
  • Perform investigations across Windows, Linux, iOS, and cloud platforms, using SIEM and manual log analysis where required.
  • Lead stakeholder briefings during high-severity incidents.
  • Enrich investigations using internal threat intel, OSINT, and health sector-specific sources (e.g., H-ISAC, HC3 bulletins).
  • Contribute to detection engineering and playbook development aligned with healthcare-specific threat vectors.
  • Write post-incident reports with clear insights for operational, risk, and compliance teams.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • 3 or more years of experience in cybersecurity.
  • 5 or more years of experience in Windows and Linux OS investigations, network protocol analysis, and EDR telemetry.
  • 2 or more years of experience with incident response frameworks (NIST 800-61, HITRUST IRM, etc.) and adversary models (MITRE ATT&CK, Cyber Kill Chain).
  • 2 or more years of experience in SIEM (e.g., Splunk, Anvilogic), EDR platforms (e.g., CrowdStrike, SentinelOne), and forensic tools.

ADDITIONAL JOB STANDARDS

  • Hands-on incident response experience in large enterprise environments (30K+ users, multiple business units or hospitals).
  • Strong understanding of HIPAA security rule, HITECH, and how regulatory requirements intersect with incident handling.
  • Familiarity with common healthcare systems such as Epic, Cerner, HL7/FHIR interfaces, or IoMT devices.
  • Proficient in writing detection rules and custom signatures to identify malicious activity.
  • PowerShell, Python, or Bash scripting skills.
  • Clear communicator with experience handling sensitive incidents in regulated industries.
  • Ability to lead investigations that involve patient data and coordinate with privacy and compliance officers.
  • Exposure to healthcare IT, hospital systems, or regulated environments.

As a core member of the Office of Information Security’s Detection and Response Team (DaRT), the Senior Incident Responder plays a mission-critical role in protecting patient care, safeguarding sensitive health information, ensuring clinical continuity, and enabling diagnostic and genetic innovation. This position leads the investigation, containment, and resolution of cybersecurity incidents that could impact the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of systems across the enterprise.

You’ll collaborate across clinical, IT, and compliance teams to respond to security threats. You’ll handle escalated events from the SOC, perform technical investigations, and lead recovery efforts while maintaining compliance with requirements associated with HIPAA, HITRUST, GDPR, etc. If you're driven by purpose, technically sharp, and thrive in fast-paced environments where security meets patient care—this is the role for you.

Benefits: Employees regularly scheduled to work 20 or more hours per week are eligible for comprehensive benefits including: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, STD/LTD, 401(k), Paid Time Off (PTO) or Flexible Time Off (FTO), Tuition Reimbursement and Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Employees regularly scheduled to work less than 20 hours, Casual, Intern, and Temporary employees are only eligible to participate in the 401(k) Plan. Employees who are regularly scheduled to work a 7 on 7 off schedule are eligible to receive all the foregoing benefits except PTO or FTO. For more detailed information, please click here.

title: Managing Director – Implementation Center of Excellence (iCoE)_PMO
description:
Role Purpose

The MD for the Implementation Center of Excellence (iCoE) is accountable for establishing, scaling, and governing State Street’s high‑capability PMO function for client implementation across various workstreams in STT Alpha. The MD ensures that the iCoE becomes a strategic capability, reducing vendor dependency, improving cost efficiency, strengthening internal expertise, and enabling predictable client delivery at scale.

Key Responsibilities

iCoE Strategy, Design & Build‑Out

  • Lead the end‑to‑end design and multi‑year implementation of the iCoE operating model, including functional scope, hiring strategy, location footprint, and resource mix.
    Transition execution‑heavy work from high‑cost vendors into the iCoE through structured knowledge transfer, scaling internal capability, and reducing dependence on vendors

  • Aligning contractor‑to‑FTE transitions and phasing resource migration strategically.
    Drive FTE vs Contractor ratio strategy, establishing a sustainable talent supply model for PMO, and other iCoEs as required

PMO CoE

  • The MD will oversee and build leadership capability across PMO functions – STT End to end implementation planning, Risk management, Reporting , Tools & Automation / Ai initiatives

  • Strengthen the focus on executing the PMO iCoE strategy, including contractor reduction, capability build-out, location strategy and cost optimization

  • Accountable for the global strategy, delivery excellence, operating model, and financial performance of enterprise PMO services supporting large‑scale client implementations and platform transformations.

  • Champion AI‑enabled Program governance, intelligent data driven analytics, and risk management capabilities

  • Establish Standard governance, cadence, reporting standards, milestone planning, and dependencies management.

  • Drive collaboration and partnerships with other CoEs and Alpha implementation teams to deliver client implementation programs successfully

  • Stand up a unified India‑based PMO function with SMEs, leads, and analyst teams.

  • Establish integrated support model with Conversion, Business Integration / Target Operating Model (TOM) Alignment, Environment Management, Alpha Data Services, Governance & Vendor Relations.

  • Ensure consistent delivery across front, middle, and back‑office End to end implementations, complex data flows, and integrations.

  • Enable OBM (Outcome‑Based Model) transition by linking partner payments to outcomes and making sure that sub-outcomes are delivered in a timely manner with expected quality

People Leadership & Capability Development

  • Build and lead a leadership team (VP/AVP layers) across PMO teams.

  • Establish senior leadership layers within iCoE

  • Manage onboarding of new hires, training, knowledge transfer and creation of standard PMO playbooks, frameworks and best practices.

  • Drive capability building across CoEs, ensuring consistent training and best‑practice adoption.

  • Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

  • Accountable for building a sustainable operating model, workforce planning, succession planning and long-term hub growth.

  • Establish career paths, competency frameworks, and succession plans for testing professionals.

  • Lead capability build‑out in India and other strategic hubs, including CoE scale‑up and leadership bench strength.

  • Engage globally and drive PMO strategy

Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Create and operate iCoE governance structures across program reporting (client implementations), risk management, productivity metrics, and leadership oversight.

  • Represent iCoE progress to senior leadership and participate in recurring strategic governance meetings.

  • Provide clear executive‑level reporting on quality, risks, dependencies, and decision points.

  • Ensure alignment with the broader GCI and Alpha three‑year strategy, including OBM rollout and partner consolidation.

Operational Efficiency, Productivity & Financial Management

  • Achieve targeted cost reductions by shifting work from high‑cost locations to the India hub.
    Improve FTE‑to‑contractor and HCL‑to‑Hub ratios, driving labor arbitrage benefits and operational scalability.

  • Responsible for process simplification, automation, digitalization and AI adoption to improve productivity and scalability.

  • Drive automation, standardization, tool adoption, reporting quality, and process enhancement.
    Track financials, onboarding flows, hiring dependencies, and realization of Outcome based milestone payments

  • Accountability for tracking and delivering business benefits/ outcomes, including contractor reduction, productivity improvements and cost savings.

  • Engage with vendor partners to manage consultants and deliver quality results

  • Support sales and pre‑sales activities through estimation models, proposals, and client solution shaping

Required Skills & Experience

Experience

  • 15+ years in large‑scale implementation, transformation, PMO leadership in client implementation programs (global model), or delivery operations in financial services.

  • Proven success managing global delivery hubs or Centers of Excellence at scale.

  • Demonstrated experience transitioning vendor work in‑house and managing hybrid workforce models.

  • Proven track record leading global, complex, client‑facing transformation programmes.

  • Deep understanding of financial services platforms, data‑heavy architectures, and regulated environments.

  • Demonstrated ownership of P&L, operating models, and large global team

Leadership & Execution

  • Exceptional ability to build and lead multi‑disciplinary teams across Testing, PMO, Conversion, Product, Data, and Ops.

  • Strong stakeholder influence across MD/SVP levels in Operations, Technology, and Client organizations.

Technical & Functional Acumen

  • Solid understanding of Front office, middle office and Back office components, implementation workflows, PMO tools and data migration models.

Governance & Change Management

  • Deep knowledge of PMO governance, risk management, performance metrics, and delivery controls.

About State Street

What we do. State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation we’re making our mark on the financial services industry. For more than two centuries, we’ve been helping our clients safeguard and steward the investments of millions of people. We provide investment servicing, data & analytics, investment research & trading and investment management to institutional clients.

Work, Live and Grow. We make all efforts to create a great work environment. Our benefits packages are competitive and comprehensive. Details vary in locations, but you may expect generous medical care, insurance and savings plans among other perks. You’ll have access to flexible Work Program to help you match your needs. And our wealth of development programs and educational support will help you reach your full potential.

Inclusion, Diversity and Social Responsibility. We truly believe our employees’ diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspective are a powerful contributor to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their maximum potential while adding value to both our organization and our clients. We warmly welcome the candidates of diverse origin, background, ability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and personality. Another fundamental value at State Street is active engagement with our communities around the world, both as a partner and a leader. You will have tools to help balance your professional and personal life, paid volunteer days, matching gift program and access to employee networks that help you stay connected to what matters to you.

State Street is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer.

Discover more at StateStreet.com/careers

About State Street

Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. Job Description: Corporate Tax Director (Media)

Location:

NEW GROUND WON'T BREAK ITSELF.

A look into the role

We're looking for a Director to support our Media and Entertainment tax team. You'll work with a broad range of clients across the sector, providing corporate tax advisory and compliance services, and bringing together deep technical knowledge of creative industry reliefs with broader corporate tax expertise.

One day you might be getting into the detail of a Creative Industry Tax Relief claim; the next, you're in the boardroom talking through what an international restructuring or a sale process means for a client's next production or investment round. This role suits someone who moves comfortably between the two.

Portfolio leadership

  • Supporting our portfolio of corporate tax compliance and provision engagements, with particular responsibility for complex Creative Industry Tax Relief claims across TV, film and video games
  • Acting as the primary point of contact for a defined client base, building relationships that go well beyond the engagement in front of you

Audit of tax

  • Leading large and complex audit of tax engagements for media sector clients, managing the relationship with audit teams and reviewing the technical positions that sit behind the numbers

Tax structuring and advisory

  • Advising media clients on tax structuring, including international expansion and migration of operations and rights
  • Providing Enterprise Investment Scheme advice to clients raising investment into qualifying media and entertainment ventures

Transactions

  • Supporting the transactions practice on deal structuring and tax diligence for media companies, including sell-side advisory, and bringing your sector knowledge to bear on the specific risks and reliefs that shape media deals

People and team

  • Managing, coaching and developing a team of tax professionals, and taking an active role in their technical training and career progression
  • Setting the standard for quality and technical rigour across the team's output
  • Playing a part in recruitment and resourcing decisions for the media tax team

Operations

  • Owning financial performance for your portfolio, including billing, recoveries and WIP management
  • Making sure engagements are risk-managed appropriately and in line with firm policy
  • Contributing to the wider operational running of the tax service line

Business development and market presence

  • Building and maintaining a network of contacts across the media sector, including intermediaries, industry bodies and target clients
  • Spotting and converting new business opportunities within existing and new clients
  • Representing the firm at industry events and contributing to thought leadership on media sector tax matters
  • Working with colleagues across the firm to spot cross-selling opportunities

Knowing you're right for us

Ideally, we're looking for someone who is fully tax qualified and comfortable leading an engagement across the entire corporate tax role - compliance, provision, advisory and reliefs. That said, subject to the wider business case, we'd also welcome a candidate whose strength is signing off Creative Industry Tax Relief claims, working alongside a Tax Partner or Director to cover the rest of the corporate tax scope.

  • CTA and/or ACA qualified (or equivalent), with significant post-qualification experience in corporate tax
  • Strong technical knowledge of Creative Industry Tax Reliefs across TV, film and video games
  • Experience advising on tax structuring, including international expansion and migration
  • A track record of managing complex compliance and advisory engagements, ideally including audit of tax work
  • Experience supporting transactions, including sell-side advisory and tax diligence
  • Familiarity with Enterprise Investment Scheme rules and how they apply to media and entertainment clients is an advantage
  • Proven people management experience, with a genuine interest in developing others
  • Existing relationships or credibility within the media and entertainment sector are an advantage
  • Excellent communication skills, with the confidence to advise senior stakeholders and represent the firm externally

Knowing we're right for you

This is a role with real scope to shape our media tax offering, backed by the firm's national tax network and sector specialists across audit and advisory. You'll have autonomy to build your own client relationships and market presence, genuine investment in your development as a leader, and a team that will back you to do it.

Beyond the job

Life is more than work. The things you do, and the people you're with outside of work matter, that's why we're happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles, and we'll always do our best to keep your work and life in balance.

The impact you can make here will go far beyond your day job. From secondments, to fundraising for local charities, or investing in entrepreneurs in the developing world, you'll be giving back to society. It's that drive to do the right thing that runs through our every move, grounded in our firm's values – purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind.

We're looking for people who want to contribute, spark fresh ideas and go beyond expectations. People who want to be able to proudly do what's right, for the firm, our clients, our people and themselves. It's how it should be.

title: Senior Demand Planner, Retail - North America
description:
POSITION TITLE: Senior Demand Planner, Retail - North America

REPORTS TO: Director, Planning

BUSINESS AREA: Merchandising & Planning

LOCATION: Ogden, U

OVERVIEW

This role owns the retail demand plan for North America, ensuring forecasts align with store demand, inventory targets, and financial goals. The Senior Demand Planner connects merchandising, retail, and global planning teams to drive a clear, unified view of demand across stores and channels.

In addition to planning ownership, this role leads the allocation function, managing a team responsible for in-season inventory execution. Success comes from linking strong forecasting with effective allocation to drive in-stock performance, optimize inventory, and support retail growth.

WHAT MAKES THIS A GREAT PLACE TO WORK & PLAY:

  • Hybrid work schedule
  • A generous PTO policy, plus 15 paid annual holidays and 3 floating holidays
  • Half-day Fridays for 5 months of the year
  • An exceptional employee discount on all our products and sister brands (Arc’teryx, Armada, Atomic, Wilson)
  • “Powder Bell” powder days throughout the winter season
  • Healthy Lifestyle Benefit designed to support your well-being and active lifestyle
  • Opportunities to engage in the community and with industry partners

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility satisfactorily:

Demand Planning & Forecast Ownership

  • Own the end-to-end retail demand plan at model, color, size, and monthly levels across stores
  • Develop and maintain a consensus-based forecast aligned to store performance, inventory targets, and commercial plans
  • Translate forecast into actionable inputs for open-to-buy and supply planning
  • Incorporate store-level trends, regional performance, and product lifecycle into forecasting decisions
  • Analyze and challenge assumptions to balance growth opportunities with inventory risk

Retail & Inventory Performance

  • Drive retail performance through strong alignment of forecast, inventory, and store demand
  • Monitor sell-through, inventory levels, and stock productivity across stores and channels
  • Partner with merchandising to influence assortment productivity and lifecycle decisions
  • Ensure alignment between demand plan and in-season trading strategies

Cross-Functional Leadership & Alignment

  • Lead demand alignment across merchandising, retail, finance, and supply chain teams
  • Serve as the key point of contact between retail teams and global planning functions
  • Influence decision-making to align demand, inventory, and financial outcomes
  • Drive clarity and accountability across teams through a single, aligned demand plan

Allocation Leadership & Execution

  • Lead and develop a team of allocators responsible for store-level inventory execution
  • Oversee initial allocations, replenishment strategies, and in-season inventory balancing
  • Ensure consistent in-stock positioning while minimizing excess and fragmentation
  • Guide the team in reacting to business trends and optimizing product flow to stores
  • Set allocation priorities aligned with demand plan and business objectives

Process Improvement & Tools

  • Drive improvements in forecasting, allocation, and retail planning processes
  • Partner on development of reporting, tools, and dashboards to support scalability
  • Standardize ways of working across demand planning and allocation functions

KPIs Owned – Demand Planning

  • Forecast accuracy
  • Inventory targets and turns
  • Store in-stock rates and inventory productivity
  • SKU productivity (80/15/5 framework)
  • Revenue and sell-through performance
  • Allocation effectiveness (stock balance, availability, and flow)

WHAT MAKES THIS A GREAT PLACE TO WORK & PLAY:

  • Hybrid work schedule
  • A generous PTO policy, plus 15 paid annual holidays and 2 floating holidays
  • Half-day Fridays for 6 months of the year
  • An exceptional employee discount on all our products and sister brands (Arc’teryx, Armada, Atomic, Wilson)
  • “Powder Bell” powder days throughout the winter season
  • Healthy Lifestyle Benefit designed to support your well-being and active lifestyle
  • Opportunities to engage in the community and with industry partners

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORKING ENVIRONMENT

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to travel, talk and hear. The employee is frequently required to sit, stand and walk. The employee must occasionally kneel, stoop, crouch, twist and lift to 30 pounds, with or without accommodations.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate, but can involve exposure to varying noise levels, ranging from moderate to loud, as well as flashes of light.

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • 5–8+ years of experience in demand planning, merchandise planning, or retail planning
  • Proven experience linking demand planning with allocation and in-store execution
  • Prior experience managing or mentoring team members (direct or indirect)
  • Strong understanding of retail KPIs (sell-through, weeks of supply, stock-to-sales)
  • Advanced Excel skills; experience with planning/allocation systems strongly preferred
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with ability to turn insights into action
  • Excellent communication and influencing skills across cross-functional teams
  • Experience in apparel, footwear, outdoor, or retail-driven consumer goods preferred
  • Experience operating in a global or matrixed environment is a plus
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-growing, evolving retail environment
  • 20% travel

Success comes from linking strong forecasting with effective allocation to drive in-stock performance, optimize inventory, and support retail growth.

title: Test Engineer
description:
Job Description:

About Packsize,

Packsize is redefining the way businesses and their customers use and experience packaging around the world. We build the technology, design the right solutions, and automate the processes that propel the industry forward. To us, packaging is much more than a box—it’s delivering what’s right for our customers, their customers, our people, and the planet.


Test Engineer (Louisville, KY)


Job Overview
We are seeking a hands-on, detail-oriented Test Engineer to join our Testing & Development team. This role is responsible for planning, executing, and analyzing tests for Packsize machines and related systems to ensure product quality, reliability, and performance. The ideal candidate combines strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with a passion for working directly with electro-mechanical equipment, collaborating across teams, and driving continuous improvement through data-driven testing and validation activities

Role Title
Test Engineer – Testing & Development
Location
Louisville, KY
Travel Requirement
0-75% travel

Primary Responsibilities

  • Develop, execute, and maintain test plans, test procedures, and test reports for Packsize products and subsystems.
  • Independently perform hands-on testing of electro-mechanical systems, software features, consumables, and integrated machine functionality.
  • Lead factory acceptance testing (PFAT), life-cycle management testing, NPD testing and customer-specific validation activities.
  • Analyze test data to identify trends, defects, performance gaps, and opportunities for product improvement.
  • Perform root cause analysis and troubleshooting of mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and system-level issues.
  • Define acceptance criteria, testing methodologies, and data collection requirements for new and existing products.
  • Document test results, findings, risks, and recommendations in Qase, ADO, SharePoint, and other company systems.
  • Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, Production, Materials, and Field Service teams to investigate and resolve product issues.
  • Support machine setup, configuration, commissioning, and test readiness activities.
  • Design and improve test fixtures, tooling, automation concepts, and test processes to increase testing efficiency and repeatability.
  • Mentor Test Technicians and provide technical direction during test execution activities.
  • Participate in design reviews and provide feedback regarding product testability, reliability, manufacturability, and customer impact.
  • Support field investigations, customer escalations, and validation efforts as required.


Key Success Criteria

  • Successfully execute 95%+ of assigned test projects on schedule while maintaining complete and accurate documentation
  • Ensure 100% of test results, defects, observations, and corrective actions are documented in approved systems.
  • Demonstrate ownership of testing activities from planning through final reporting and recommendation
  • Successful completion of PFAT, NPD, and sustaining validation projects with minimal rework or escaped defects.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Engineering Technology, or a related technical discipline.
  • Strong troubleshooting and root cause analysis skills.
  • Knowledge of structured testing methodologies and engineering validation practices.
  • Experience working with electro-mechanical systems, industrial equipment, or automated machinery.
  • Ability to collect, analyze, and interpret technical data through Power-Bi, Databricks and reporting software
  • Experience creating technical documentation, reports, and test procedures.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and project management skills.
  • Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools including Excel and PowerPoint.


Preferred Experience

  • 1-3 years of experience in test engineering, validation engineering, quality engineering, product development, manufacturing engineering, or a related field.
  • Experience with factory acceptance testing (FAT/PFAT), product validation, or reliability testing.
  • Experience with data analysis tools such as Power BI, Databricks or similar platforms.
  • Familiarity with Azure DevOps (ADO), Jira, Qase, or equivalent test management systems.
  • Understanding of electrical controls, sensors, PLCs, motion systems, and industrial automation.
  • Experience designing or improving test fixtures, tooling, or automation solutions.
  • Background in packaging systems, industrial automation, manufacturing equipment, or related industries
  • Work Conditions
  • 100% onsite role based within a manufacturing and testing environment.
  • Regular hands-on work with industrial machinery, mechanical systems, electrical components, and test equipment.
  • Frequently requires standing, walking, bending, lifting, and operating equipment for extended periods.
  • May occasionally require flexible hours to support production schedules, factory acceptance testing, or product validation activities.
  • Required use of appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and adherence to all safety procedures.

title: Technology Cost Intelligence Engineering Lead, VP
description:
Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for an analytics engineering lead, Vice President, reporting to the VP responsible for product, tooling, and transformation within the Global Technology Services Financial Operations Office. This role owns the data and analytics products that make technology cost transparent and actionable, with near-term focus on Technology Financial Management and Total Cost of Ownership, including cost transparency, showback, and progressive chargeback, and Cloud FinOps, including multi-cloud spend, optimization signals, and commitment utilization.

Why This Role Is Important To Us

This role owns the data and analytics products behind State Street's technology cost management and Cloud FinOps capabilities, deciding how cost, cloud, and infrastructure data is modeled, governed, and delivered for technology leaders and finance partners. Success is measured by platforms in production, leadership reporting used without side reconciliation, manual spreadsheets retired, and results that hold up to scrutiny. The lead will determine how data is modeled, how the platform is architected and governed, what should be built or bought, and which standards others must follow.

What You Will Be Responsible For

  • Own the cost intelligence data platforms end to end across technology financial management, total cost of ownership, Cloud FinOps, and future capabilities.

  • Design governed data models and semantic layers that turn cost allocations, infrastructure inventory, cloud billing exports, and commitment schedules into consistent, reusable business measures.
  • Design and operate ingestion, transformation, and refresh across source systems, normalizing keys, schemas, and formats and partnering with source-data owners to enable new feeds.
  • Author and maintain calculation logic in languages such as DAX, keeping deterministic results separate from estimates, forecasts, and advisory scoring.
  • Define and enforce the security and access model, including row-level and role-based access appropriate to sensitive financial data.
  • Maintain lineage, documentation, definitions, versioning, testing, controlled promotion, validation, and exception reporting.
  • Run each product with a roadmap, backlog, and support model covering triage, production stability, and continuous improvement, keeping the platform current as source systems and cost taxonomies evolve.
  • Set architecture and standards for vendor platforms, surge build capacity, analysts, and developers, and partner with finance and FinOps teams to translate methodology into implemented logic.

What We Value

The following skills support success in this role:

  • Analytics engineering discipline across data modeling, transformation, ingestion, and governed release, applied to cost and financial data.
  • Ability to connect engineering rigor with financial questions leaders ask, while clearly separating actuals, forecasts, assumptions, and estimates.
  • Clear communication with subject matter experts, finance partners, and senior leaders, including explaining trade-offs and validating outputs in plain language.
  • Comfort across functions and cost domains, resolving ambiguity where definitions, source data, and ownership are still maturing.
  • Independence to own a platform outright, set direction and standards, make architecture and tooling decisions, guide others, and maintain exacting standards for governance and auditability.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered. Advanced degree or relevant certifications preferred.

  • Experience owning a platform or product outright, setting development standards, and directing supporting analysts, developers, and vendor resources.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering governed data and analytics solutions on enterprise analytics engineering stack and/or Microsoft Fabric and the broader Power Platform ecosystem.
  • Hands-on experience with ingestion and refresh across heterogeneous source systems, plus SQL, Python, APIs, and lakehouse and data warehouse engineering.
  • Strong data and semantic modeling skills across multiple source systems, with proficiency in DAX and transformation tooling such as Power Query or equivalent.
  • Practical command of security and access control for analytics platforms, including row-level and role-based access appropriate to sensitive financial data.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure, cloud, SaaS, CMDB, service catalog, application inventory, or product taxonomy data, and with SDLC and end-user developed tool governance practices.
  • Track record of lineage, documentation, controlled release, validation, and exception reporting that meets auditability and control requirements.
  • Experience with IT financial management, Cloud FinOps, and total cost of ownership data, including cloud provider billing and cost export formats for major public cloud.
  • Familiarity with Cloud FinOps frameworks, TBM taxonomy or comparable cost frameworks, commitment-based discount management, or cloud rate optimization concepts.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud cost management, FinOps, and IT financial management vendor platforms preferred, whether as data sources or delivery platforms.
  • Experience working in financial services or another regulated enterprise environment preferred.

Additional Requirements

The role requires strong partnership across the Financial Operations and Technology Business Offices leadership; FinOps and cost management teams; infrastructure, cloud, application, Finance, Procurement, and service management source-data owners; vendors; and architecture, security, and audit functions. The candidate should be comfortable operating in a matrixed environment where requirements, definitions, and source data are still maturing.

Salary Range:

$120,000 - $202,500 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

Employees are eligible to participate in State Street’s comprehensive benefits program, which includes: our retirement savings plan (401K) with company match; insurance coverage including basic life, medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and other optional additional coverages; paid-time off including vacation, sick leave, short term disability, and family care responsibilities; access to our Employee Assistance Program; incentive compensation including eligibility for annual performance-based awards (excluding certain sales roles subject to sales incentive plans); and, eligibility for certain tax advantaged savings plans.

Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. title: Business Analyst
description:
