title: Summer 2027 Intern: Portfolio Management Team
description:
About Us

Live Oak Bank is a digital bank that serves small business owners across the country. Our groundbreaking spin on service and technology has fueled our mission to be America’s Small Business Bank. Our products help customers buy, build, and expand their business, and our high-yield savings and CD products help them grow their hard-earned money. At Live Oak, we never lose sight of the well-being of our people. We believe our employees are the heart of our company. Our commitment to our customers and culture is intertwined, and we seek those who embody and embrace what it takes to empower the American dream.

Ready to make an impact? We're looking for an onsite intern to join our team for the 10-week Summer 2027 Internship Program (May 17 - July 23, 2027) at our headquarters in Wilmington, NC. Applications are due by 11:59 p.m. ET on Wednesday, September 23.

How This Role impacts Live Oak:

Interns that join the Portfolio Management Team will have the opportunity to understand and support our Portfolio Analysts in the numerous tasks they work on each quarter. The 10-week program will allow interns to work through financial analysis, shadow tasks and customer interactions, learn the lead to loan process and gain an understanding of Live Oak’s risk through Lending and Servicing functions. The Portfolio Analyst role is vital to the health and overall performance of the existing Live Oak Bank loan portfolio.

What You’ll Do at Live Oak:

  • Analyze financial statements from several different industries as part of our quarterly analysis and assist with annual risk grade assessments for relationships with larger exposure.

  • Complete a capstone project and presentation outlining the lead-to-loan process using what you learn over the course of the summer.

  • Shadow the day-to-day functions of the role, such as collateral, payment, and loan structure questions, managed and completed by a variety of Portfolio Analysts.

  • Work with other departments throughout the bank handling customer requests to understand how each role plays a key function. This will also broaden your spectrum on potential future opportunities throughout the bank.

  • Spearhead any internal projects focused on making the group more effective and efficient.

  • Attend Loan Committee weekly listening to an educational debate on deals approved each week.

  • Attend department and internal team meetings for important updates and learning opportunities.

How You’ll Do It:

  • You will be trained on financial statement analysis and the Live Oak Bank approach to cash flow lending.

  • Consistent feedback on job performance during the internship.

  • Enhancing your time management, prioritization, and organization skills

Preferred Experience:

  • Interest in banking or finance

  • Currently enrolled in college/university working toward a degree

  • Authenticity/Genuine

  • Professional Curiosity

  • Trustworthiness

  • Personal Effectiveness/Credibility

  • Nimbleness

  • Initiative/Willingness to Own Your Role

  • Joy in Collaborating

  • Prompt

  • Multi-tasker

#LI-DNI

Our Values

  • Dedication: Possess a deep commitment to Live Oak Bank’s mission and core values, exemplified through a strong work ethic, adaptability and pride in your work.

  • Ownership: Take initiative to deliver positive results by proactively and creatively solving problems, while maintaining a high degree of quality.

  • Respect: Treat everyone with courtesy, politeness, and kindness.

  • Innovation: Embrace fresh ideas and fearlessly contribute new solutions to emerging or existing problems.

  • Teamwork: Foster collaboration, accountability, and trust with others and understand that together, we do more

title: Longwall Superintendent
description:
We are seeking an experienced Longwall Superintendent to join the leadership team at Moranbah North Mine.

This senior operational role is responsible for safely leading the longwall function and delivering consistent production performance. You will coordinate people, equipment and operational priorities while working closely with maintenance, engineering and technical services teams.

This is an opportunity for an experienced underground coal mining leader to influence the safety, reliability and performance of a major longwall operation.

Key responsibilities

  • Provide visible safety leadership across all longwall activities
  • Lead longwall production teams to achieve safety, production and operational objectives
  • Coordinate daily and weekly priorities across production, maintenance and technical functions
  • Monitor longwall performance and respond effectively to changing conditions, risks and production constraints
  • Ensure operations comply with legislative requirements, site standards and the Safety and Health Management System
  • Lead the application and review of operational controls, risk assessments and TARPs
  • Support longwall planning, panel readiness and safe production activities
  • Review production performance, equipment availability and shift reporting
  • Work closely with the Underground Mine Manager, operations leaders, engineering and technical services teams
  • Build leadership capability through coaching, clear expectations and constructive feedback
  • Drive continuous improvement across safety, productivity, reliability and work practices

You are an experienced underground coal mining leader with strong longwall production knowledge and a practical, visible leadership style.

You will also bring:

  • Extensive operational leadership experience within underground coal mining
  • Strong experience in longwall production and second workings
  • Demonstrated experience leading large operational teams
  • Strong knowledge of Queensland coal mining legislation and underground safety systems
  • First class miners or deputy ticket will be highly regarded but not essential
  • Experience managing operational risk, TARPs and changing mining conditions
  • Sound planning, decision-making and problem-solving skills
  • The ability to work effectively across production, maintenance, engineering and technical teams
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management capability
  • A genuine commitment to safety, accountability and workforce engagement
  • Relevant underground coal mining qualifications and competencies
  • A current Australian driver’s licence

Relevant statutory competencies and qualifications required for the position will be considered as part of the selection process.

  • A senior leadership opportunity within an established underground longwall operation
  • Career development and leadership opportunities
  • The opportunity to lead an experienced operational team
  • A workplace focused on safety, inclusion and continuous improvement
  • Residential, FIFO or DIDO options
  • Monday to Friday role with a 9 day fortnight available
  • Competitive Salary + 12% Super + Annual Bonus

What we Offer

When you join Anglo American, you can expect to enjoy a competitive salary and benefits package and a range of flexible work arrangements that support the balance of work, family and individual circumstances. But more than this, you’ll find yourself in an environment where the opportunities for learning and growth are second to none. From technical training to leadership programmes, we bring out the best in our people. There are plenty of opportunities to move onwards and upwards too. We’re a large, successful multinational company – and we’re still growing all the time.

Who we are

We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies. As the custodians of coal and other precious natural resources – diamonds (through De Beers), copper, platinum and other precious metals, iron ore and nickel – our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively, with the utmost consideration for local communities, our customers and the world at large.

Background checks

Successful candidates will be required to complete background screening which may include a criminal check and validation of qualifications.

Inclusion and Diversity

Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How we are committed to your safety

Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies – from drones to data analytics – that are helping to make mining safer.

How to apply

To apply for this role, please complete our online application form. You will have the opportunity to upload your CV and other relevant documentation as part of this process.

REF81476A

Closing date - 18 October 2026

Please note, screening and interviews may take place prior to closing date – applications may also close before this date.

title: Principal Network Engineer
description:
Principal Network Engineer

This role has been designed as 'Hybrid' with a requirement that you will work on average 2 days per week from an HPE office.

Who We Are:

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.

Job Description:

Job Family Definition:

The job family spans across multiple engineering disciplines. Work consists of designing, developing, analyzing, troubleshooting and debugging systems, software and solutions for research and/or research development of product, services, and solutions for HPE’s portfolio. Requires a broad knowledge and application of engineering disciplines, methodologies and tools.

Job Family Definition for Executive Levels only: Directs and manages a diverse team of engineering professionals performing research, development, design and/or implementation of products, services, solutions for the company’s portfolio. Responsible for creating and communicating technical strategy within the organization and/or across the function.

Job Description:

The Resident Engineer reports within the Professional Services (PS) team and is typically dedicated to a single customer. This role requires fluency in Juniper Networks technologies and general networking, as well as a deep understanding of the customer's specific deployments and use cases. Resident Engineers act as the primary technical contact for customers who purchase Advanced Services and work closely with the customer on a daily basis. They are granted access to customer production equipment to perform their duties.

What You’ll Do

Key Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the subject matter expert for HPE products in data center networking technologies, supporting customers with network design, troubleshooting, hardware and software testing, documentation, best practices, and automation.
  • Provide primary technical support for break/fix activities, using advanced diagnostic skills to restore services quickly and reduce the likelihood of recurrence.
  • Advise customers on best practices for Junos configurations and network design.
  • Manage and grow relationships with internal teams and outsourced development partners involved in engineering design and development.
  • Review and evaluate designs and project activities for compliance with technology and development standards; provide constructive feedback to improve product quality.
  • Contribute domain-specific expertise and engineering leadership to cross-organizational projects and programs.
  • Drive innovation by integrating new technologies into engineering projects and designs.
  • Mentor and guide junior staff members.

What you need to bring:

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • Typically, 10 + years’ experience in data center routing, switching, and network architecture, with hands-on experience using HPE Juniper products such as the QFX, PTX, MX, and EX series.
  • Proven ability to develop test automation and write scripts in Python.
  • Up to 10% travel to customer sites is required.

Knowledge and Skills:

  • Experience testing and certifying Junos and Junos EVO software features and associated hardware.
  • Skilled in empirical analysis, modeling, and testing methodologies to validate product designs and specifications.
  • Proficient with engineering design tools and software used to design components and solutions.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and the local language; able to present product architectures and design proposals and to negotiate options with senior management.

Additional Skills:

Cloud Architectures, Cross Domain Knowledge, Design Thinking, Development Fundamentals, DevOps, Distributed Computing, Microservices Fluency, Full Stack Development, Security-First Mindset, User Experience (UX)

Note: This option is reserved for applicants needing assistance/reasonable accommodation related to a disability.

title: Staff Systems Signal Processing Engineer
description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

At the heart of Defining Possible is our commitment to missions. In rapidly changing global security environments, Northrop Grumman brings informed insights and software-secure technology to enable strategic planning. We’re looking for innovators who can help us keep building on our wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies that fuel those missions. By joining in our shared mission, we’ll support yours of expanding your personal network and developing skills, whether you are new to the field, or an industry thought leader. At Northrop Grumman, you’ll have the resources, support, and team to do some of the best work of your career.

We are seeking a Staff Systems Signal Processing Engineer to lead the design, development, integration, and verification of advanced signal processing solutions for complex sensor systems. The ideal candidate will be a technical leader with deep expertise in digital signal processing (DSP), algorithm development, and system-level performance analysis, capable of driving architecture decisions and mentoring junior engineers. This position is based out of Linthicum, MD and will be 100% on-site.

What You’ll get to Do:

  • Lead the system-level architecture and design of signal processing chains for RF or multi‑sensor systems, from requirements through verification

  • Develop and analyze signal processing algorithms for detection, estimation, tracking, classification, filtering, and data fusion.

  • Perform system modeling and simulation (e.g., MATLAB, Python, and/or C++) to evaluate concept performance, trades, and robustness under representative operational scenarios.

  • Define and flow down system and subsystem requirements, including performance budgets, interfaces, and key design parameters.

  • Partner with hardware, software, and integration teams to implement algorithms on embedded processors, FPGAs, or real‑time platforms; support optimization and HW/SW partitioning.

  • Conduct system performance analysis, including SNR/CFAR analysis, detection and false‑alarm trade studies, sensitivity and robustness assessments, and end‑to‑end verification against requirements.

  • Lead or support lab/field test activities, including test plan development, data collection, data reduction, and post‑test analysis.

  • Prepare and deliver technical reviews and briefings to internal leadership, customers, and cross‑functional teams; clearly communicate complex technical concepts and tradeoffs.

  • Provide technical leadership and mentoring to early‑career and mid‑level engineers in signal processing, modeling, and systems engineering practices.

  • Support capture and proposal efforts by contributing to technical concepts, architectures, and requirements

This position is contingent upon the successful transfer of an active U.S Government Secret Clearance and the ability to obtain Special Program Access prior to start.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree with 12 years of experience, master's degree with 10 years of experience or Ph.D. with 8 year of experience in Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, or related technical fields; an additional 4 years of experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

  • U.S Citizenship is required.

  • A current/active U.S. Government Secret Clearance

  • Ability to obtain Special Program Access (SAP) prior to start

  • Experience with digital signal processing theory and application, including detection theory, estimation, filtering, spectral analysis, and time‑frequency methods.

  • Experience developing and analyzing algorithms in MATLAB, Python, or similar scientific computing environments

  • Experience in system‑level signal processing for radar or similar sensing systems.

  • Experience with requirements development, system architecture, and verification in a structured systems engineering environment.

  • Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively in cross‑functional, multi‑disciplinary teams

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's Degree or PhD in a STEM discipline

  • Experience with real‑time implementation of algorithms on embedded processors, FPGAs (e.g., VHDL/Verilog, HDL‑Coder, or FPGA tool flows), or GPUs.

  • Experience with data fusion, multi‑sensor tracking, machine learning applied to signal processing, or adaptive processing techniques.

  • Background in DoD or aerospace/defense programs, including working with government customers, requirements documents, and gated reviews.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical teams, make architecture decisions, and influence system design across disciplines.

Northrop Grumman provides a comprehensive benefits package and a work environment which encourages your growth and supports the mutual success of our people and our company. Northrop Grumman benefits give you the flexibility and control to choose the benefits that make the most sense for you and your family.

Your benefits will include the following: Health Plan, Savings Plan, Paid Time Off and Additional Benefits including Education Assistance, Training and Development, 9/80 Work Schedule (where available), and much more!

Northrop Grumman has approximately 90,000 employees in all 50 states and in more than 27 countries. We strive to attract and retain the best employees by providing an inclusive work environment wherein employees are receptive to diverse ideas, perspectives, and talents to help solve our toughest customer challenges: to develop and maintain some of the most technically sophisticated products, programs, and services in the world.

Our Values. The women and men of Northrop Grumman Corporation are guided by Our Values. They describe our company as we want it to be. We want our decisions and actions to demonstrate these Values. We believe that putting Our Values into practice creates long-term benefits for shareholders, customers, employees, suppliers, and the communities we serve.

Our Responsibility. At Northrop Grumman, we are committed to maintaining the highest of ethical standards, embracing diversity and inclusion, protecting the environment, and striving to be an ideal corporate citizen in the community and in the world.

description:
Location: Overseeing South Florida region.

You want Benefits? You’ve got it! Our generous benefits package includes:

What to Expect?

The Franchise Business Partner serves as the primary Support Office contact for franchise owners within an assigned territory. Using established reports, tools, and operating playbooks, this role helps franchisees improve retail and pool service sales, profitability, inventory productivity, and operational execution. The role also supports product sell-in and consumer sell-through by helping franchisees plan purchases, execute promotions, and convert inventory into profitable sales.

On a daily basis our Franchise Business Partner:

Franchisee Support and Performance Coaching

  • Maintains a consistent cadence of franchisee meetings, business reviews, field visits, and documented follow-up.

  • Reviews store financial and operating results to identify performance gaps and help franchisees implement practical improvement actions.

  • Coaches franchisees on retail operations, pool service growth, customer acquisition and retention, staffing, local marketing, and overall business execution.

  • Tracks agreed actions, monitor progress, and escalate significant or unresolved concerns to Franchise Operations leadership.

Retail, Service, and Brand Standards

  • Coaches franchisees on the consistent execution of Pinch A Penny’s retail, pool service, customer experience, and brand standards.

  • Helps franchisees grow recurring pool service customers and strengthen coordination between retail and service operations.

  • Conducts annual Brand Standards Certification reviews and follow up on required corrective actions.

  • Supports the implementation of new products, promotions, technology, training, and other systemwide initiatives.

  • Ensures franchisees and their teams understand and execute merchandising, promotional, product knowledge, pricing, and customer engagement initiatives that support consumer sell-through.

Support Office Coordination

  • Connects franchisees with the appropriate Support Office departments or approved vendor resources when specialized assistance is required.

  • Communicates relevant store-level feedback and recurring field issues to Franchise Operations leadership and other Support Office teams.

  • Participates in the transition of new locations from the New Store Operations team to ongoing Franchise Operations support.

  • Documents franchisee interactions, field visits, performance plans, and follow-up activity in designated company systems.

What You Will Need:

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred.

  • Three to five years of experience in multi-unit retail, service operations, franchise support, field operations, or a related role.

  • Working knowledge of store-level sales, gross margin, inventory, payroll, and profitability measures.

  • Strong communication, relationship-building, organization, and follow-up skills.

  • Ability to interpret performance reports and translate findings into practical next steps.

  • Ability to influence results without direct authority and balance franchisee support with accountability.

  • Specialty retail and service experience preferred.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and business reporting platforms.

  • Ability to travel regularly throughout the assigned territory.

Looking to work for the best in the industry?
Since opening its first store in 1975, Pinch A Penny, A POOLCORP Company, has become the largest franchised retail pool, patio and spa company. This first store evolved into a full-time, full-service retail pool supply store offering everything needed to operate and enjoy a swimming pool or spa. With our rapid growth we have been able to hire over 300 employees from Marketing directors, sales associates to machine operators and maintenance mechanics. We are proud to serve our community and be an employer of choice. We believe in recognizing our employees for their hard work and encourage work-life balance.

Why join PINCH A PENNY?
Pinch A Penny, a POOLCORP Company is the premier destination for all your swimming pool and backyard needs. With over 300 stores and expanding, we are the nation's largest swimming pool retail, service, and repair franchise. Our relentless dedication to excellence drives us to bring people together through the joy of pools, spas, and the backyard experience. Join us on this exciting journey as we continue to grow, innovate, and set new standards in the swimming pool industry.

title: Engineering Summer Internship Programme
description:
Programme dates: June to August 2027 (exact dates to be confirmed based on university term schedules).

Please review all the internship programme opportunities and make one application.

Our Engineering Summer Internship Programme has been crafted to simulate our Engineering Associate Programme so that you can understand what a career in Technology and Engineering at LSEG would really be like.

To be eligible, you must be in your junior year of your undergraduate studies due to complete all the requirements of your course summer 2028 and studying a ‘STEM’ subject (science, technology, engineering or mathematics).

During your time with us you will have the opportunity to explore potential careers paths by working within our D&A, Markets, Risk Intelligence, FTSE Russell, I&C Engineering functions.

Roles can vary from development and programming to business analysis and tech project management. During the recruitment process we will get to know your skills and interest and how they align with the needs of the business to place you in the right team.

These are real roles. Our 9 weeks summer interns play a part in the success of our organisation, just like they would do as a graduate.

What we are looking for:

We are passionate about recruiting people who are interested in pursuing a career within Technology and would like to learn about the full breadth of our business – and are interested in playing a part of our development, as it grows and diversifies.

  • You will have an interest in technology demonstrated either via your work experience, extracurricular activities, or academic studies. For instance, you may be part of a Computing Society, have taught yourself how to code or have focused on technology as part of a university project.

  • You should be interested in financial markets and how technology supports our business.

  • A curiosity for data and an ability to analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions.

  • Individuals who are able to connect the dots and think creatively.

  • The environment we work in is fast paced, you’ll need to demonstrate focus, resilience and the flexibility to adapt to changing demands.

  • People who can collaborate with others, using their strong communication skills in the process.

You will stand out to us if you can demonstrate and recognise that what you achieve is equally important to how you achieve it.

Application close: 30th October, however we recommend an early application because we consider candidates on a rolling basis. Due to the volume of applications, we might close the applications earlier, so we recommend an early application.

Recruitment Process:

  • The first stage of the recruitment process involves making an application and submitting your resume.

  • The second stage is completing Technical and Coding Assessment. This technical assessment is designed to evaluate your coding ability, logical reasoning and problem-solving skills.

  • The next stage of the application process is an untimed Immersive Online Assessment. The assessment is designed to give you an insight into what it’s like to work at LSEG.

  • The third stage is a video interview where you will answer a series of questions using a strength-based-interview style

  • The final stage is a virtual half day assessment centre which involves several different types of exercises – further information is provided at the point of invite.

Please review all the summer internship opportunities and make one application If you make more than one application, we will review your first application only.

Please note, all our assessment centres are held virtually.

title: Construction Project Manager III
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin corporate functions, providing centralized support across Blue Origin business unit teams, functions, and locations.

Job Description

As part of a small, passionate, and accomplished team of experts, you will push the boundaries of what’s possible in project management, supporting Blue Origin’s Construction Center of Excellence team. You will make substantive contributions to the team’s impact on all aspects of building our infrastructure and world-class facilities. You will manage all aspects of the construction project, including planning, execution, and completion, while also maintaining budgets, schedules, and quality standards. This role requires strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills, as well as the ability to work effectively with teams and stakeholders, and independently.

We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!

Responsibilities:

  • Providing field oversight and assistance, and creating a customized schedule

  • Negotiating contracts with General Contractors and subcontractors

  • Development and management of all project documentation

  • Review compliance with state and government regulations and ensure project or site location follows all guidelines

  • Must be able to manage multiple projects while being innovative and creative in challenging situations

  • Performs site visits and monitors progress of construction activities regularly, and holds regular status meetings with all sub-teams

  • Ensure construction activities move according to pre-determined schedule(s)

  • Develop and deliver progress reports, proposals, required documentation, presentations analyze results, and troubleshoot problem areas

  • Working with project teams to proactively manage changes in project scope, identify potential crises, and devise contingency plans

  • Approves all invoices and manage the billing process

  • Represent the Company in project meetings, client meetings, etc.

  • Initiating, planning, completing, monitoring, and closing construction projects throughout their lifecycles, to include:

    • Developing project plans, budgets, and schedules.

    • Collaborating with internal and external stakeholders.

    • Eliciting and documenting stakeholder requirements

    • Identifying project dependencies, risks, and schedule impacts.

    • Reporting project progress (status, risks, opportunities, roadblocks, and KPIs)

    • Assisting in contract negotiations.

    • Monitoring contractor progress via frequent site visits.

    • Reviewing and approving invoices and payment applications.

    • Evaluating and processing change requests and change orders.

    • Assisting in resolution of payment or performance disputes

    • Solve daily project issues

Qualifications:

  • Prefer B.S. in Engineering, Construction Management, or Project Management

  • Minimum over 8 years of experience with complex facility construction and renovations projects to include both vertical and horizontal construction

  • Experience leading and managing small- to medium-sized teams integrating multiple subsystems to meet a top level system requirement

  • Strong personnel management and mentoring skills

  • Recent facility development or management experience supporting mission critical operations

  • Experience in sub-contract management of suppliers including request for proposal, specification and statement of work

  • Project leadership with the ability to work with stakeholders, knowledge of manufacturing operations, Launch Site environment, assembly processes, and quality control

  • Proficient in project management software (Milestones, MS Project)

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint)

  • Strong project management, budget management and team leadership skills

  • Project planning, schedule and cost estimation

  • Strong safety mindset and experience, including hands-on experience planning and conducting hazardous or critical operations

Desired:

  • Experience with launch site, spacecraft manufacturing, Project leadership with the ability to work with stakeholders, knowledge of manufacturing operations, Launch Site environment, assembly processes, and quality control integration and test

  • Knowledge and experience in Local and National Codes

  • Knowledge and experience in Safety plans and programs to comply with laws, regulations and policies

At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. description:

JOB DESCRIPTION

Workday Financials Associate Director

You Belong Here

The Protiviti Career provides opportunity to learn, inspire, and advance within a collaborative and inclusive culture. We hire curious individuals for whom learning is a passion. We lean into our mission: We Care. We Collaborate. We Deliver.

At every level, we champion leaders who live our values of integrity, inclusion, innovation, and commitment to success. Imagining our work as a journey, we believe integrity guides our way, inclusion moves us forward together, innovation creates new destinations, and our commitment to success empowers us to deliver on our vision to be the most trusted global consulting firm.

Where We Need You

Protiviti is looking for a Technology Consulting Associate Director to join our growing Workday team.

What You Can Expect

As an Associate Director, you'll take a lead role in strengthening our relationships with clients and providing seamless guidance in the completion of engagements. You'll partner with our strategic clients to identify and manage risk. You'll develop strategies to solve complex business problems using new ways of thinking, and devise solutions to support your clients' needs through analytics, automation or the latest tools and methods.

You’ll develop new projects, help identify new business, and build lasting relationships with clients and within the community as you serve as an ambassador of Protiviti in the market. You will also be a mentor and provide growth and development to teams as you oversee the successful completion of project work plans.

What Will Help You Be Successful

  • You enjoy Workday Finance implementations.

  • You are passionate about building trusted relationships with C-level executives and providing exceptional experiences that translate to additional project work.

  • You have an inherent interest in project management and team leadership.

  • You promote a positive team culture that fosters open communication among all engagement team members.

  • You create development opportunities for others, including participating in the creation and rollout of training, and ways for your team to improve our clients and communities.

  • You enjoy discovering prospective project work with current and potential clients through networking, knowledge-building, and client interactions.

  • You excel at identifying opportunities to integrate product solutions and resources to improve client service capabilities.

  • You view client challenges as opportunities to add value and can translate that into new project proposals and sales.

  • You are seen as a valued contributor to thought leadership and encourage knowledge-sharing and collaboration across teams.

  • You have interest in managing a diverse portfolio of clients across multiple industries.

Do Your Talents Include the Following?

  • Demonstrated experience with:

  • Leading / managing future state design and process improvement projects focused on Record to Report (R2R) and/or Order to Cash (O2C) business functions.

  • Functional and systems experience focused on R2R and/or O2C business functions.

  • Serving as a solution architect, project manager and/or workstream lead for R2R and/or O2C during the design and implementation of Workday.

  • Serving as a project manager over large, complex Workday Financials implementations

  • Developing Workday Financials and Account Center implementation plans, including estimating the level of effort, timing and costs

  • Designing and implementing Workday. Key responsibilities as part of these initiatives include leading and performing: requirements definition, facilitating design workshops, testing, data conversion, training, cutover, and post go-live support.

  • Establishing and cultivating business relationships and a professional network, including with senior executives.

  • Successfully pursuing business development opportunities and identifying and implementing strategies to obtain new work or clientele.

  • Ability to translate and communicate issues, risks or challenges to client personnel, including executives.

  • Leadership and direct supervisory experience of teams including conducting performance appraisals, mentoring and coaching, oversight and review of work, coordination across teams, and understanding how to motivate.

Your Educational and Professional Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g., MIS, Finance/Accounting, Engineering)

  • 9+ years working in professional services or industry.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite applications with specific emphasis on Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Secondary emphasis on Visio and Access.

  • Workday certified in Financials is strongly preferred, with certifications in Accounting Center, Adaptive, and/or Prism as a plus.

  • Strong understanding of accounting principles and financial reporting practices.

Our Hybrid Workplace

Protiviti practices a hybrid model, which is a combination of working in person with a purpose and working remotely. This model creates meaningful experiences for our people and our clients while offering a flexible environment. The ratio of remote to in-person requirements vary by client, project, team, and other business factors. Our people work both in-person in local Protiviti offices and on client sites, which can include local or out-of-state travel based on our projects and client requests and commitments.

Starting salary is based on a full-time equivalent schedule. Placement in the range is dependent upon experience, skills and geographic work location. Below is the salary range for this job.

$153,000.00 - $260,000.00

Our annual bonus plan provides eligible employees additional cash and/or discretionary stock compensation opportunities. Below is the bonus target opportunity for this job.

16%

The total cash range is estimated from the sum of the base salary range plus the bonus target opportunity. Below is the estimated total cash range for this job.

$177,480.00 - $301,600.00

Employees are eligible for medical, dental, and vision coverages, FSA and HSA healthcare accounts, life and accident insurance, adoption and fertility assistance, paid parental leave up to 10 weeks, and short/long term disability. We offer eligible employees a company 401(k) savings and investment plan with an employer match of 50% on the first 6% of your contributions. We provide Choice Time Off (CTO) for vacation, personal needs, and sick time. The amount of (CTO) varies based on years of service. New hires receive up to 20 days of CTO per calendar year. Protiviti also recognizes up to 11 paid holidays each calendar year.

At Memorial, we are dedicated to improving the health, well-being and, most of all, quality of life for the people entrusted to our care. An unwavering commitment to our service vision is what makes the difference. It is the foundation of The Memorial Experience.

Summary:

The Patient Financial Services Representative (PFSR) serves as the first point of contact in greeting patients and guarantors in the hospital, ambulatory or medical office setting. The PFSR engages with the patient or guarantor to obtain pertinent information and answer any questions in an effort to ensure that all required demographic, financial, and insurance eligibility information is gathered and verified. Provides patient estimates as requested. title: Director, National Accounts
description:
Position Purpose:

The Director, National Accounts at GMS is responsible for spearheading the strategic expansion and execution of national account initiatives, thereby playing an essential role in driving significant revenue growth and enhancing customer satisfaction. This leadership role demands a visionary approach to building and managing high-performance teams, leveraging comprehensive market analysis, and fostering cross-functional collaborations to deliver innovative solutions that exceed client expectations. Through expert negotiation, strategic planning, and dynamic relationship management with key national clients, the Director will fortify and expand long-term partnerships, ensuring GMS upholds a competitive edge and preferred partner status in the marketplace.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute strategic national account growth initiatives, ensuring alignment with corporate goals and facilitating seamless cross-functional collaboration for effective strategy rollout.

  • Lead and cultivate a high-performing team of national account managers, driving them towards exceeding sales targets through exemplary leadership and comprehensive development programs.

  • Utilize market trend analysis, customer insights, and competitive intelligence to drive strategic account planning and uncover growth opportunities that deliver significant business value.

  • Build and sustain robust relationships with key stakeholders within national accounts, positioning GMS as a trusted and preferred partner in the industry.

  • Implement performance metrics and reporting mechanisms to track and evaluate progress against strategic objectives, promoting accountability and a culture of continuous improvement.

  • Collaborate with cross-departmental teams, including product development, marketing, and operations, to innovate and enhance value propositions tailored to national account needs.

  • Lead complex contract negotiations, crafting mutually beneficial agreements that ensure long-term profitability and enhanced customer satisfaction.

  • Act as the primary representative of GMS at major industry events and forums, advocating the company's brand strengths and thought leadership to enhance market presence.

Direct Manager/Direct Reports:

  • The Director, National Accounts reports directly to the VP of National Accounts, serving as a critical member of the sales leadership team. This position is responsible for managing a team of national account managers who are direct reports. The Director will leverage leadership and strategic oversight to drive team performance, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and maximizing client engagement.

Travel Requirements:

  • The role of Director, National Accounts at GMS requires regular travel to national account locations and industry events, necessitating flexibility and commitment to maintaining strong client relationships and representing the company effectively.

Physical Requirements

  • The position of Director, National Accounts at GMS primarily involves tasks performed in a standard office environment, including extended periods of sitting, focusing on computer-based tasks, and engaging in verbal and written communication. The role may require the ability to travel domestically to facilitate in-person meetings with national clients and participate in industry events. This position necessitates adeptness in performing consistent fine motor tasks and occasional lifting of light materials typically associated with professional office activities. GMS is committed to ensuring accessibility and will provide reasonable accommodations to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role, allowing all candidates equal opportunity to succeed in an inclusive workplace.

Working Conditions

  • The Director, National Accounts at GMS will operate within a hybrid working model, combining remote work flexibility with in-office days , fostering both collaboration and individual productivity. This role demands adaptability and thrives in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, where strategic decision-making and prompt execution are critical to success. The position involves managing multiple priorities simultaneously and requires occasional travel to meet with national accounts and participate in industry events. The successful candidate must be a proactive leader who excels in dynamic settings, maintaining composure and effectiveness under pressure to consistently deliver superior business outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, or a related discipline; MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.

  • At least 10 years of progressive experience in sales, account management, or related functions, with a focus on managing national or key accounts within a Fortune 500 company.

  • Demonstrated leadership experience with proven ability to guide, mentor, and cultivate high-performing teams in a dynamic, matrixed organizational structure.

  • Advanced strategic thinking, negotiation, and analytical skills, with a proven ability to evaluate complex business scenarios and craft innovative, effective solutions.

  • Superior communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with a refined ability to establish and sustain relationships at all levels, both internally and externally.

  • Results-driven approach, emphasizing data-based decision-making and leveraging insights for business advancement.

  • Willingness and ability to travel as required for meetings with national accounts and participation in significant industry events.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced proficiency in the development and execution of large-scale sales strategies and account management initiatives specifically tailored to the unique needs of national accounts within the industry.

  • Extensive experience in leveraging data analytics tools and customer relationship management (CRM) platforms to deliver precise and actionable insights for strategic decision-making and enhanced customer engagement.

  • Demonstrated success in cultivating transformational change through innovative problem-solving methodologies and proactive adaptation to market trends.

  • In-depth understanding of the regulatory and compliance landscape affecting national account sales operations within the industry, with proven ability to navigate complex legal and compliance requirements.

  • Strong financial acumen with expertise in budgeting, forecasting, and pricing strategies to maximize profitability and market share for national accounts.

  • Track record of leading successful cross-functional project teams, driving collaboration and fostering innovation across departments, including marketing, product development, and supply chain management.

  • Proven ability to manage and influence senior-level client relationships and stakeholder engagements to achieve alignment on strategic objectives and foster long-term partnerships.

  • Experience with digital transformation initiatives, including the integration and optimization of digital tools and technologies to enhance customer experiences and operational efficiencies.

Minimum Education:

  • A Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Marketing, or a closely related field is required. An MBA or advanced degree is preferred.

Preferred Education:

  • An MBA or advanced degree in Business Administration, Marketing, or related fields is strongly preferred to enhance strategic leadership capabilities in managing national accounts and driving revenue growth.

Minimum Years of Work Experience:

  • Minimum Years of Work Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in sales, account management, or related roles, with a strong track record of managing national or key accounts in a Fortune 500 environment.

Certifications:

  • Professional certifications relevant to sales, account management, or leadership are considered advantageous.

  • Certification in Strategic Account Management (CSAM) is preferred, demonstrating advanced expertise in managing and growing key client relationships effectively.

  • Certified Sales Executive (CSE) is desirable, indicating a commitment to excellence in sales leadership and strategic account management

Competencies:

Strategic Leadership: Demonstrated ability to set and implement a vision aligned with corporate objectives, ensuring the development of comprehensive national account strategies that drive growth and market leadership. Relationship Management: Proficiency in establishing and nurturing deep partnerships with key decision-makers and stakeholders, positioning the company as a trusted and preferred partner in the marketplace. Analytical Acumen: Strong ability to analyze complex market data, competitive activities, and customer needs to identify growth opportunities and inform strategic decision-making. Negotiation and Influence: Expertise in contract negotiations and proposals, achieving balanced agreements that align with company goals and maximize mutual benefits. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to effectively collaborate with diverse teams, including product development, marketing, and operations, to deliver innovative and customer-centric solutions. Performance Management: Skilled in designing and implementing performance metrics and reporting systems, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement to exceed sales targets and organizational goals. Communication Excellence: Exceptional communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, capable of articulating complex concepts and fostering relationships at all organizational levels. Change and Innovation Leadership: Aptitude for driving innovation and navigating a dynamic business environment, leading teams through change with foresight and adaptability to maintain competitive advantage.

Remote/Virtual, hybrid or in-office: Remote

title: Monitor Tech, Med Surg, Columbia County, FT Nights
description:
How would you like to work in a place where your contributions and ideas are valued? A place where you can serve with compassion, pursue excellence and honor every voice? At Wellstar, our mission is simple, yet powerful: to enhance the health and well-being of every person we serve. We are proud to have become a shining example of what's possible when the brightest professionals dedicate themselves to making a difference in the healthcare industry, and in people's lives.

Work Shift

Night (United States of America)

About the Facility

Learn more about Columbia County Medical Center, including our teams, culture, and campus environment:

Join Wellstar Health System at Columbia County Medical Center

Hours: Full Time Nights, 36 Hours per week (3/12s)

Job Summary:


The Monitor Technician functions under the direction of the Nurse Manager to facilitate safe, age appropriate and culturally aware patient care by observing cardiac monitors to ensure recognition of arrhythmias. Cardiac monitor technicians are responsible for watching patients' heart rates and /or pulse oximetry and reporting important changes to the nursing staff; they often use equipment that tracks several patients simultaneously. They clean and maintain equipment and ensure batteries are charged and installed properly. Additional duties may include clerical and receptionist functions, retrieval of data, preparing and maintaining patient charts, verifying current telemetry orders in an accurate and timely manner, and serving as the pivotal communication source to the clinical staff.


Core Responsibilities and Essential Functions:


Observes Telemetry Monitors
* Recognizes cardiac arrhythmias and reports promptly
* Records telemetry strips each shift and as changes or events are noted. Ensures 12 hour strips are printed and distributed to the units per policy
* Accurately interprets rhythms and measures intervals, able to identify age appropriate differences
Excellence in Customer Service by partnering with health care team, patient and family
* Protects rights and dignity of patient at all times
* Maintains confidentiality
* Answers telephone and call lights promptly and notifies appropriate individual of need for follow-up
* Resolves unit monitoring concerns
* Present self in positive and professional manner and show sensitivity to concerns and needs of others
Performs telemetry functions
* Accurately maintains required units dispensation records and monitor logs
* Ensures appropriate assignment of patient to telemetry unit and documentation of all equipment
* Prepares each telemetry unit for patient use; cleans each unit upon return
* Keeps necessary telemetry supplies available and organized
* Reports broken or defective equipment to immediately to Manager and Biomed
Team Work & Communication
* Supports initiatives of the health care team
* Participates in unit performance improvement initiatives
* Supports professional nursing practice through evidenced-based practice and ethical accountability
* Provides unit supplies, patient care supplies, and equipment as assigned
* Uses effective written and oral communication skills with physicians and healthcare team
* Uses safety communication techniques
* Communicates completion of assignment/duties
* Gives concise report of all patients monitored and status of equipment to oncoming shift
* Communicates patient safety concerns/problems/ emergencies to the RN
* Notifies the appropriate nursing unit promptly of rhythm changes. Communicates need for immediate response, if indicated
* Uses positive and respectful communication with all members of healthcare team, patients and families.
Safety and Infection Control
* Provides safe patient monitoring
* Follows all policies and procedures with regard to safety and emergency preparedness
* Cleans all equipment properly utilizing appropriate cleaning process per isolation guidelines
* Practice accountability
Performs other duties as assigned
Complies with all Wellstar Health System policies, standards of work, and code of conduct.


Required Minimum Education:

  • High School Diploma General or GED General


Required Minimum License(s) and Certification(s):


All certifications are required upon hire unless otherwise stated.

  • BLS - Basic Life Support or ARC-BLS - Amer Red Cross Basic Life Support or BLS-I - Basic Life Support - Instructor

Additional License(s) and Certification(s):


Required Minimum Experience:


Previous experience as monitor technician in an acute care setting Preferred or
Staff members with monitor tech experience are required to provide proof of participation in a EKG monitoring course such as Learn Rhythm or a comparable course. Preferred or
EMT, Paramedic, CNA, or Monitor tech certification Preferred or


Required Minimum Skills:


Ability to read, write and speak the English language
Strong customer service and interpersonal skills
Ability to collaborate with health care providers to facilitate provision of patient care
Ability to multi-task essential
Ability to function in stressful and emergency situations essential
Strong detail orientation required; Computer skills
Knowledge of medical terminology
Personal time management skills

Join us and discover the support to do more meaningful work—and enjoy a more rewarding life. Connect with the most integrated health system in Georgia, and start a future that gives you more.

title: Senior Application Analyst
description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

Position Overview

At Abbott Cancer Diagnostics, we're cancer fighters. That's not a tagline, it's the reason we come to work every day. Our mission is to change lives through advances in cancer detection and treatment guidance, and ultimately to help eradicate the disease and the suffering it causes. Everything we build, including the software you'd be leading, exists to move that mission forward.

As a Senior Application Analyst, you will work on business systems design and configuration, Upgrades, and improvements for assigned technology platforms. As a primary support contact for application end-users, the Senior Application Analyst will work to identify issues that arise in the application area, as well as issues that impact other application teams and work to resolve them. The Senior Application Analyst will perform impact analysis of desired changes, build and test systems changes, and identify areas of improvement associated with platform performance and opportunities to enable business processes and requirements.

The Senior Application Analyst will act as a mentor to more junior analysts on the team, support questions and may delegate activities to other analysts.

Essential Duties

Include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Lead the estimation of enhancement or support requests.
  • Guide workflow design, configure and test system changes, and analyze technical issues.
  • Liaise with business systems stakeholders and software vendor’s implementation staff, ensuring alignment of business needs with delivery of systems changes.
  • Develop an understanding of operational needs to set the direction for the organization's workflows; proactively identify opportunities to improve business workflow with technology improvements.
  • Participate in training and work with end users.
  • Troubleshoot problems and questions.
  • Provide end-user support for issues entered into tracking systems.
  • Review the status of projects and issues with project leadership.
  • Assign or delegate configuration or other activities to Application Analysts or Managed Services team members.
  • Act as delegate for Applications Manager for incident or problem resolution.
  • Provide mentorship for other peers and leadership to solve problems, even if it's outside of their normal responsibilities/scope.
  • Be a leader on internal process design and documentation to drive continuous improvement for the IT department or team.

  • Uphold company mission and values through accountability, innovation, integrity, quality, and teamwork.

title: Assistant to the VP of Division for Mission and Ignatian Imagination
description:
Job Title:

Assistant to the VP of Division for Mission and Ignatian Imagination

Job Summary:

The Assistant to the VP will join the new Division for Mission and Ignatian Imagination within the University, and the Mission Team, which includes the Vice President, the Director of University Ministry (UMin), the University Chaplain, the Director of the Joan and Ralph Lane Center for Catholic Social Thought and the Ignatian Tradition (the Lane Center), the Director of the Office of Antiracism, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (ADEI). The Division is charged with helping to shape how the University lives its Jesuit Catholic mission in service of forming students who will “change the world from here.” The work of the Division helps to ensure that USF remains a place where faith and reason flourish, where justice is pursued with rigor and love, where diverse religious and secular perspectives are welcomed, and where the whole community is invited into the transformative work of Jesuit education.

The Assistant to the VP both supports the work of the Vice President and the other members of the Mission Team, while serving as the hospitable face and primary point of contact within the University for all those seeking to participate in the University’s Mission. The Coordinator provides executive support for the Vice President of Mission and Ignatian Imagination and oversees administrative and operational functions for the Office of the Vice President, the Lane Center, ADEI, and cooperates with the work of UMin and the University Chaplain. Because the Vice President chairs the University Mission Council, the Division Coordinator will sit on the Council and provide administrative and operational support to it. As the Vice President and the Mission Team will staff the Mission Committee of the Board of Trustees, the Coordinator will assist with organizational and administrative support for that Committee’s meetings.

The Assistant to the VP serves as a trusted administrative and strategic partner to highly visible offices of the University, providing high-level executive support to advance the institution’s Catholic, Jesuit mission, academic excellence, and operational effectiveness. This position is responsible for managing executive communications, coordinating priorities and activities, supporting governance and stakeholder relations, and ensuring the efficient operation of the various offices within the Division for Mission and Ignatian Imagination. The Assistant exercises professionalism, discretion, friendliness, and sound judgment while fostering collaboration and reflecting the university’s values.

This position is full time and will support the VP of Mission and Ignatian Imagination 50% of the time; the Lane Center 25%; and ADEI the other 25% of the time. This position is on-site/in-person.

Full Job Description:


    • Serves as liaison for the Division of Mission and Ignatian Imagination, ensuring that all internal and external constituents feel valued, supported, and celebrated through affirming and respectful communications, and coordination of meetings and events.
    • Coordinates and prioritizes the schedule and communications of the Vice President of Mission and Ignatian Imagination, ensuring the most strategic and efficient use of the VP’s time, and briefing/preparing the VP for meetings and events, including meetings with major donors, the Archdiocese of San Francisco, the Jesuit West Province, the Association of Jesuit Colleges and Universities (AJCU), the Catholic Theological Society of America (CTSA), and other external partners and stakeholders.
    • Performs a range of administrative and technical support duties as the primary and confidential administrative support to the VP, relieving the VP of administrative details.
    • Manages budget related items, including expense reports, vendor invoices, and fund transfers for the VP, the Lane Center Director and the Director of ADEI.
    • Arranges travel and accommodations for the VP and, when necessary, for the other Division directors, and for guests of the division who may be visiting the University. Likewise, provides support to the holder of the Lo Schiavo Chair, the boards of the Lane Center and ADEI.
    • Helps facilitate communication and cooperation with the Office of the President, the Office of the Provost, the Academic Deans, the Divisions of Advancement, Enrollment Management, and Student Life, other senior leaders in the University, and the Loyola House Jesuit Community, while ensuring that the Office provides proactive communications and timely responses to inquiries from students, faculty, staff, and stakeholders in a professional, discrete manner.
    • Proactively assists the VP of Mission and Ignatian Imagination in demonstrating care and appreciation for the USF community, by drafting letters of invitation, gratitude, congratulations, acknowledgement, etc.
    • Ensures persons meeting in the Office of Mission are afforded hospitality and the schedule is kept punctual.
    • Serves as the designated committee staff to the Catholic Identity and Jesuit Mission Committee of the Board of Trustees. Maintains confidential membership lists, prepares agendas, sends notices, coordinates quarterly meetings, captures minutes, makes meeting arrangements, and provides administrative support in accordance with the established practices of the standing committees of the Board of Trustees.
    • Provides administrative support to the University Council for Jesuit Mission. Compiles agendas, meeting packets, quarterly reports, presentations, and minutes of the meetings.
    • Provides administrative support and leadership to other Mission Division Initiatives.
    • Maintains discretion and confidentiality in relationships with trustees, major donors, president, and cabinet members.
  • Responsibilities with the Office of the VP, the Lane Center, and the ADEI Office
    • Oversees office procedures, filing systems, and space planning for the Office of the VP.
    • Manages the Office of Mission and Ignatian Imagination, the Lane Center and ADEI’s direct voicemail and office mail. Posts notifications and announcements. Receives and screens a variety of calls. Takes information, answers inquiries, provides information using knowledge of the University and its Jesuit Catholic educational mission.
    • Plans, coordinates, and organizes activities and coordinates events sponsored by our three offices while working with administrative staff from the President’s Office, the Jesuit community, etc.
    • Schedules meetings and assists the directors with scheduling related to Lane Center/ADEI.
    • Manages Lane Center / ADEI events, creating promotional materials, coordinating speaker travel, and coordinating with USF Events Management Services.
    • Assists directors in managing Lane Center/ADEI Funds, Organizations, Accounts, and Programs (FOAPS), creates budget and expense reports, and manages transfers.
    • Manages website and email communication for Lane Center and ADEI.
    • Maintains advisory board membership lists and an archive of documents.
    • Takes minutes at Lane Center/ADEI meetings
    • Assists in coordinating the Lane Center programming and ADEI programming.
    • Purchases of office supplies using Hilltop Shop and other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS

    • Bachelor’s degree required. Master’s or other advanced degree preferred. Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
    • Minimum of five years of administrative experience in an executive office; experience in a higher educational setting is preferred.
    • Understanding and commitment to USF’s Jesuit Catholic educational mission, and the capacity to articulate the mission to members of the USF community and to external partners.
    • Demonstrated appreciation for/working knowledge of the Society of Jesus (“The Jesuits”) and Ignatian spirituality. OR deep familiarity with the Jesuit (Society of Jesus) charism in higher education, Ignatian spirituality and discernment.
    • Experience managing an executive-level calendar.
    • Excellent organizational and planning skills and the ability to prioritize among complex and competing expectations. Highly effective at time and task management, and prioritization.
    • Project management skills, ability to plan, think through, carry out and assess multi-part projects.
    • Ability to exercise a high level of diplomacy, discretion, emotional intelligence and confidentiality.
    • Advanced competency (or the ability to quickly acquire such competency) in using Google Suite, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Concur, Workday, Canner, and task management and task sharing tools (Slack, etc).
    • Experience managing virtual meetings on Zoom.
    • Qualified applicants should submit a cover letter, resume, and the names/contact information for 2-3 references.

Full-Time/Part-Time:

Full time

Pay Rate:

Salary

Salary Range :

$85,000 - $89,000 annualized; commensurate with experience

title: Telecom EIT
description:
The Operational Solutions and Technologies team is dedicated to delivering innovative solutions that enhance the resilience, efficiency, and sustainability of critical infrastructure, systems, and engineering projects. Leveraging expertise in cybersecurity, telecommunications, IT/OT convergence, intelligent automation, software and systems engineering, and systems integration, the team develops resilient, scalable, and optimized solutions that ensure the long-term sustainability of infrastructure throughout its lifecycle. Join us and immerse yourself in a dynamic, innovative, and collaborative environment where you’ll make a real impact. Together, we’ll push boundaries and go above what’s expected of us to meet the challenges of tomorrow and engineer a better world!

CIMA+ offices in Western Canada are on a strong growth trajectory, creating opportunities to contribute to exciting and complex projects, develop new skills, take on new challenges, and advance your career within the organization.

As a Telecom Engineer-in-Training (EIT), you will be engaged in the design and delivery of mission-critical telecommunications systems across a variety of projects for CIMA+'s key clients. Our telecommunications team works with industrial and public-sector clients across power utilities, energy, transportation, telecommunications carriers, and other critical infrastructure sectors.

Working under the guidance and supervision of experienced engineers, you will contribute to telecommunications system design, engineering drawings and technical deliverables; perform engineering calculations and technical analyses; coordinate with other engineering disciplines; and support project teams in developing practical, reliable and resilient telecommunications solutions across a broad range of wired and wireless applications.

This position provides an opportunity to gain hands-on engineering experience, develop your technical and professional competencies, and progress toward Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) registration while working alongside experienced telecommunications professionals. This hybrid role can be based out of our offices in Vancouver, Kelowna, Calgary or Edmonton.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Support the development of telecommunications system designs and engineering deliverables under the guidance and supervision of experienced engineers.
  • Prepare and update network diagrams, schematics, block diagrams, interconnection diagrams and other engineering drawings.
  • Assist with engineering calculations, technical analyses, equipment selection and design documentation.
  • Support the preparation of technical specifications, design reports, bills of materials, equipment lists and procurement documentation.
  • Assist with project scopes, estimates, proposals, schedules and other project documentation.
  • Participate in design reviews and interdisciplinary coordination activities.
  • Support equipment evaluation, staging, FAT/SAT, installation, testing and commissioning activities.
  • Participate in site visits, field investigations and data collection as required.
  • Coordinate with internal project teams, clients, vendors and contractors under the direction of senior project team members.
  • Support responses to site information requests and preparation of record drawings and project closeout documentation.
  • Develop knowledge of applicable engineering standards, client requirements and CIMA+ engineering practices and procedures.
  • Actively develop the technical and professional competencies required for progression toward Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) registration.
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering or an equivalent engineering discipline.
  • Registered as, or eligible for registration as, an Engineer-in-Training (EIT) with the applicable provincial engineering regulator.
  • New graduate or up to 2 years of relevant engineering experience in telecommunications, networking, electrical systems, control/automation or related fields. Co-op, internship and relevant academic project experience are valued.
  • Strong interest in telecommunications systems and their application in operationally critical or mission-critical environments, with a basic understanding of telecommunications and networking fundamentals.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, written and verbal communication skills, with the ability and willingness to learn and work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Integrity, team spirit, and a commitment to excellence

Technical Experience

Academic, co-op, internship, project or work exposure to one or more of the following technologies would be considered an asset. Candidates are not expected to have experience across all areas.

  • Transport & Packet Networks:
    • DWDM/OTN; SONET/SDH and legacy migration; MPLS/MPLS-TP/IP/MPLS; Carrier Ethernet; routing and switching; VLAN; QoS and traffic engineering
  • Wireless Systems:
    • Licensed microwave; LMR; LTE/private wireless; Wi-Fi; satellite communications
  • Utility / OT Telecom:
    • Teleprotection; OPGW and fibre-optic systems; Power Line Carrier (PLC); High Voltage Entrance (HVE); SCADA/RTU communications; IEC 61850 communications
  • Supporting Systems:
    • Telecom DC power; network synchronization/timing; firewalls and secure network interfaces; monitoring and network management systems

Assets

  • Exposure to electric utility telecommunications, including teleprotection, OPGW/fibre systems, Power Line Carrier (PLC), High Voltage Entrance (HVE) and substation communications.
  • Exposure to control and automation systems such as SCADA, RTUs, PLCs and IEC 61850.
  • Knowledge of Operational Technology (OT), IT/OT convergence, cybersecurity principles or critical infrastructure environments.
  • Familiarity with IP networking, routing, switching, VLAN, MPLS, QoS or traffic engineering concepts.
  • Relevant academic projects, co-op/internship experience, laboratory work or industry certifications related to telecommunications, networking, automation or cybersecurity.
  • Demonstrated interest in continuous learning and professional development in telecommunications engineering.
