title: Assistant Coach, Men's Soccer
description:
Working at Regis University

As Regis employees, we embrace our Jesuit Catholic values of respect, inclusion and equity, and welcome employees, faculty and students from all faiths and cultures. Together, we perform our duties in alignment with the mission of the University and seek dedicated individuals to contribute to and strengthen that mission and our service to students. Why Work at Regis?

Job Summary:

The Assistant Men’s Soccer Coach is responsible for assisting with all phases of a division II soccer program while upholding the values and mission of Regis University. Responsibilities of the position include recruiting, scouting opponents, film analysis, assisting with game and practice preparation, player development, on field coaching, student-athlete academic success, and other duties as assigned by the Head Men’s Soccer Coach. The assistant coach will assume the responsibilities of the head coach if the head coach is unable to fulfill these duties.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

The Assistant Coach shall perform all duties pertaining to the men’s soccer program as assigned by the head coach. Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Assist in coaching and scheduling games, practices and conditioning: Responsible for assisting in planning content and organization of the overall program. (All offenses, defenses, fundamentals and techniques, game strategies, and knowledge of all aspects of the sport.) The assistant coach will also assume the responsibilities of the head coach if the head coach is unable to fulfill these duties.

  • Recruit qualified student-athletes: Actively recruit academically and athletically talented student-athletes in accordance with the philosophy of Regis University and in strict adherence to University, NCAA and Conference regulations.

  • Assist the head coach in monitoring and balancing the team budgets: provide input and work cooperatively with the head coach in budgeting for and requisitioning all goods and services needed and used in the sport program. This includes but is not limited to supplies, equipment, apparel, team travel, recruiting, etc. Each sport must operate within the University allotted budget for operating expenses and scholarships. Any expenses in excess of the team budget allotment must be covered by revenue generated funds.

  • Supervise graduate assistants and student employees: Assist the head coach in supervising staff as assigned and managing work study employees; work cooperatively with all members of the staff.

  • Monitor student-athlete’s academic performance: monitor the academic success of the student-athletes in her/his program. Each coach should work cooperatively with Regis University.

  • Professional development: engage in professional development. Assist the head coach in keeping with the current trends and developments as well as the implementation to perform duties more effectively.

  • The assistant coach must attend pertinent professional opportunities including, but not limited to, RMAC and NCAA meetings; the assistant coach may be included, as needed.

  • Fundraise for the Program and Athletic Department: fully participate in both program and department fundraising activities, fundraising events, university campaigns and special project campaigns.

  • Promote the brand of the Athletic Department and Regis University: continually strive to enhance the image of the Regis University Athletics Department and its programs through inter-personal contacts with parents, visitors, university faculty/staff, and community citizens. Additionally, each assistant coach should participate in Athletic Department and University sponsored events and initiatives.

  • Must be able to effectively interact with the head coach, student athletes, trainers, office staff, facilities staff, prospective athletes, parents, faculty, fans etc. daily.

  • Camps and clinics: coordinate soccer camps and clinics at the direction of the head coach; coordinate with residence life office and event services for campus camps and clinics when applicable.

  • Create an atmosphere of compliance: Know, recognize, and comply with the laws, policies, rules, and regulations governing the NCAA, the RMAC and the Regis Athletic Department. Supervise and ensure that work-study and other employees/volunteers for whom you are administratively responsible comply with the aforesaid policies, rules and regulations. Immediately advise the Regis compliance director if you have reasonable cause to believe violations, whether by employees or students, have occurred or will occur.

  • Complete vehicle driver program for certification to operate Regis University vehicles

Working conditions are normal for an office environment. Work requires weekend and/or evening hours. Some local, regional, and/or national travel is required. Hours worked may vary weekly to accommodate practice, game, and travel schedules. Flexibility in availability is essential to meet the demands of this role.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university

  • Minimum of 2 years of coaching experience.

  • The ability to travel easily between athletic facilities. The ability to lift up to 40 lbs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree

  • NCAA experience

  • Experience with recruiting software

Special Instructions to Applicants:
Please submit a resume, cover letter and list of references with your application. Current employees, please submit an application by logging into Workday. Click on the Career Worklet and access the internal site.

This position will remain posted until filled, with a preferred application deadline of September 23rd, 2026. Applications received by this date will receive full consideration.

Regis University offers a broad range of benefits that includes:

  • Comprehensive group health insurance, including medical, dental, vision, disability and life insurance.

  • A generous tuition benefit for employees, spouses and dependents

  • Paid Mission leave to allow our employees to engage in acts of service or to have time for personal reflection.

  • The "Gift of Time" when Regis closes between Christmas Day and New Year's Day.

  • Options for flexible work arrangements based on position.

title: Non-Certified Technician
description:
AutoNation is one of the largest automotive retailers in the United States, offering innovative products, exceptional services, and comprehensive solutions, empowering our customers to make the best decisions for their needs. The Non-Certified Technician inspects and services vehicles when they are delivered to the dealer and makes minor repairs or adjustments to place the vehicles in saleable condition.

.

Apply today and join a team that values your skills and invests in your future.

Exciting Benefits and Perks Await You:

  • Associate purchase and discount programs for new and pre-owned vehicles, services, parts, collision, accessories, and AutoGear

  • Access amazing deals and discounts through YouDecide, a website with offers from top providers and retailers

  • Join our DRVPNK mission to raise and donate millions of dollars to cancer research and treatment, partnering with cancer charities nationwide

AutoNation is committed to creating a diverse, equitable, and inclusive environment in our workplace and the services we provide. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds who are passionate about making a positive impact. Even if you do not meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. Join our team and help us foster a culture of belonging while contributing to our revolutionary work in the automotive industry. We value innovation, teamwork, and a commitment to making a positive impact in the world.

title: Family Engagement Advocate
description:
Are you a socially conscious, dedicated individual who is committed to building a better future for children, families, and their communities? If so, join us as we support early childhood education programs across the country to create positive outcomes for the children and families served.

Are you passionate about building strong partnerships with families and empowering them to support their children's success? Acelero Learning is seeking a dedicated Family Engagement Advocate to strengthen family engagement, promote school readiness, and help families achieve their goals through meaningful relationships, coaching, and community connections.

Why Acelero?

Our mission is bold: To design and deliver research and evidence-based approaches to eliminate the gaps between young children's inherent potential and their achievement in school and life. With our partners, we accelerate child and family outcomes that honor all of the aspirations and cultures of the communities we serve.

The Role:

As a Family Engagement Advocate, you will play a key role in engaging families as active partners in their children's healthy development and school readiness. You will build trusting relationships with families, provide individualized coaching and support, connect families to community resources, and create opportunities that strengthen parent leadership, family self-sufficiency, and community engagement.

Working collaboratively with education, health, disabilities, and family services teams, you will help create a welcoming environment where every family feels valued, supported, and empowered. This position may support multiple center locations based on program needs.

What You'll Do

  • Build Strong Family Partnerships: Develop trusting relationships with families that encourage active participation in their child's education and healthy development.

  • Promote School Readiness: Coach families on positive parent-child interactions, home learning activities, literacy, and family routines that support children's social, emotional, and academic success.

  • Support Family Goals: Partner with families to complete Family Self-Assessments and Family Partnership Agreements while helping them achieve individualized goals related to education, employment, housing, and overall self-sufficiency.

  • Connect Families to Resources: Identify and coordinate community resources, referrals, and support services that address each family's unique needs.

  • Lead Family Engagement Activities: Plan and facilitate family workshops, parent groups, leadership opportunities, and engagement events that foster connection, advocacy, and community involvement.

  • Collaborate Across Teams: Work closely with teachers, health staff, disabilities specialists, and center leadership to provide coordinated support for children and families.

  • Maintain Documentation: Ensure timely and accurate case notes, family records, referrals, electronic documentation, and required program reports.

What You Bring:

  • Passion for Family Engagement: A commitment to strengthening families and creating positive outcomes for children through meaningful partnerships and culturally responsive practices.

  • Communication Excellence: Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills with the ability to build trusting relationships with families, community partners, and colleagues.

  • Education: Associate's degree in Social Work, Family and Child Development, Early Childhood Education, Human Services, or a related field required. Bachelor's degree preferred.

  • Experience supporting families with young children and helping parents advocate for themselves and their children.

  • Experience working in diverse or low-income communities preferred.

  • Bilingual (Spanish/English) preferred.

  • Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, electronic documentation, and data management systems.

  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

Additional Requirements:

  • Valid driver's license and/or reliable transportation.

  • Ability to travel locally up to 10% for meetings, trainings, and family support activities.

  • Successful completion of required background checks and physical examination.

When/Where/How Much:

When: Fall 2026

Where: Acelero Learning, Monmouth Middlesex County – Commerce Center

How Much: Starting at $25.00 per hour + comprehensive benefits package

Why You'll Love Working with Us

  • A meaningful mission that transforms the lives of children and families.

  • A collaborative, inclusive culture where your ideas and professional growth are valued.

  • Opportunities to build lasting relationships with families and create positive community impact.

  • Comprehensive benefits that support your overall well-being, including:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance with multiple plan options

  • Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contributions

  • Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match

  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability and Basic Life Insurance

  • Professional Development Reimbursement

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

  • Wellness Programs, including virtual fitness, nutrition, and mindfulness classes

  • Pet Insurance, Legal Assistance, Identity Theft Protection, and Employee Discount Perks

If you're ready to make a lasting difference by empowering families and helping children thrive, apply today to become our next Family Engagement Advocate. Together, we'll build stronger families, stronger communities, and brighter futures for every child.

Why Acelero Learning or Shine Early Learning?
- Ability to make an impact in the lives of the children, families, and partners we serve
- Career growth and professional development opportunities
- Supportive working environment
- Average of 5 weeks of paid time off during 1st year of employment
- Comprehensive benefits, including 401K matching and 100% vesting program

title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description:
Want to help build and scale Storebrand’s modern data and AI platform?

Storebrand aspires to be a data-driven company, leveraging technology to create new business opportunities and deliver products that resonate with our users. We recognize the crucial role of a modern, cloud-enabled data and analytics platform in achieving this ambition.

We are looking for a senior data platform engineer that will be part of the central team that develops and is responsible for our data - and analytics platform. The position is in Storebrand’s Center of Excellence for Data & AI. This business unit is placed centrally in the Storebrand Group and has responsibility and ownership of processes that spans the different business units of Storebrand.

About the team!

You will be joining the platform-team which is responsible for creating a scalable and high-quality data- and analytics platform that accommodate Storebrand's evolving data and analytical needs. We distribute ownership and our goal is that the data teams across Storebrand have a high degree of self-service when it comes to working with data and AI.

As a senior data platform engineer, you will play a central role in designing and creating a superior developer experience across best-of-breed tools for scaling our data platform. Responsibilities include creating frameworks, infrastructure, systems integration, and building data pipelines. Your focus will extend to enabling data teams to build self-service data products while ensuring high standards for security and compliance.

Our tech stack

You will be working with a wide range of modern tools and technology. We are multi-cloud with both Azure and Google Cloud. Core Components of the data platform include Snowflake, Dagster+ for orchestration, dbt Cloud for data transformation and DLT for data ingestion. Supporting tools include Github for version control, Terraform for infrastructure as code, Kubernetes as a container platform, Databricks for advanced analytics and PowerBI as our enterprise reporting tool.

What you will be doing

At Storebrand, you can look forward to a work environment with a high degree of variety. You will take the lead in building frameworks for data engineering at scale supporting 100+ developers across all areas of the Storebrand Group. A typical week will encompass a diverse set of tasks:

  • Making our data teams more efficient by building and evolving our frameworks for data ingestion, orchestration, data apps, and infrastructure on top of our data platform.

  • Experimenting with, building with and improving the way we use AI and AI-agents on our platform to help us and the data teams scale.

  • Engage in ongoing development and maintenance of our data platform ensuring robust, secure and compliant secure data platform.

  • Take responsibility for developing data products within the data platform team, emphasizing data observability and monitoring.

  • Act as a key resource and technical advisor for data engineers across Storebrand helping with their operational and analytical needs.

Who are you?

You likely hold a technical degree and possess a genuine curiosity for working with data and technology. You want to take ownership of a modern data platform, and you enjoy working in a small team while serving many users. You must be pragmatic while being able to take ownership of what you build, but you don’t compromise on security and compliance.

As for the technical side, proficiency in Python and/or other programming languages, as well as SQL, is crucial. You have hands-on with AI-tools like Claude Code or Github Copilot and know their strengths and weaknesses. Experience with infrastructure as code and system integrations is a plus. Hands-on experience with technologies like Snowflake, Azure, Kubernetes, Databricks, Github, Terraform, dbt, and Dagster is beneficial but not mandatory.

Why choose Storebrand?

At Storebrand, you’ll have the space to make an impact, be heard, and grow within a company offering many opportunities. We take pride in our culture, our drive, and the shared direction we are working towards: A future to look forward to.

We actively work to foster an inclusive and diverse environment, and our efforts are being recognized. In 2025, Equileap ranked Storebrand as the number one company in Norway and among the world's top three companies for gender equality. The following year, we were named ODA Champions and ranked second on the SHE Index for our commitment to diversity and inclusion. As future optimists, we think long term and invest in solutions that strengthen both our organization and the society around us. This is one reason why we are one of only two Norwegian companies included in the Dow Jones Best-in-Class World Index.

At our Lysaker office, you will work in a central location with good public transport connections, bicycle parking, and changing facilities. You will receive health insurance, access to a chiropractor and physiotherapist at the office, and good training facilities at Storebrand Arena. In addition, we offer an excellent pension scheme, attractive insurance benefits, and home loans with subsidized interest rates.

If you are passionate about tackling solid technical challenges and improving the daily work experience for those working with data at Storebrand, we invite you to apply and be a key contributor to our evolving data and analytics platform.

Questions about the team or the role? Contact Eivind Berg (Tech Lead Data Platform) at eivind.berg@storebrand.no.

Application deadline: 07.10.2026. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis. We accept applications in both Norwegian and English.

We look forward to hearing from you!

title: Rotational Associate
description:

The Rotational Associate will rotate through areas such as sales, customer relationship management, inventory, and administrative support while learning departmental workflows, building practical business skills, and assisting where support is needed.

title: Technology Program Manager
description:
The Role

We are looking for a Technology Program Manager who can drive complex, cross-functional technology initiatives from problem definition to execution and delivery.

This is not a traditional Scrum Master / Agile Project Manager role.

You will work in an environment where requirements evolve, priorities change, teams may not be co-located, and there isn't always a well-defined process or single owner for every dependency.

Your job will be to bring clarity, structure and momentum to these situations.

You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, Data, Operations and external technology partners to ensure that complex initiatives move forward and eventually reach production.

What You Will Do

  • Drive end-to-end technology programs — translate high-level objectives into clear plans, milestones, dependencies and execution paths.
  • Navigate complex technical dependencies across multiple engineering teams, services, platforms and third-party systems.
  • Work closely with engineering leads to understand architecture, APIs, data flows, system dependencies and technical constraints well enough to identify execution risks early.
  • Identify the critical path for programs and continuously remove blockers that could impact delivery.
  • Coordinate execution across distributed and non-co-located teams, ensuring alignment without relying purely on formal processes.
  • Bring structure to ambiguous problems — figure out what needs to happen, who needs to be involved and how we get from where we are today to the desired outcome.
  • Identify risks, dependencies and decisions proactively rather than waiting for issues to surface.
  • Facilitate discussions between teams when there are conflicting priorities, unclear ownership or competing technical approaches.
  • Partner with Product Managers and Engineering Managers to convert product/business objectives into executable technology plans.
  • Maintain program visibility for leadership — what is on track, what is blocked, why it is blocked and what decisions are required.
  • Manage execution across multiple parallel workstreams without becoming a task tracker.
  • Work with external vendors/partners where technology integration or operational dependencies are involved.
  • Establish lightweight processes where needed — but avoid adding process for the sake of process.
  • 3–5 years of experience in Technical Program Management, Product Operations, Engineering Program Management, Technology Consulting or a similar role.
  • Strong understanding of software development and technology systems. You don't need to be a coder, but you should be comfortable discussing APIs, databases, services, integrations, data flows, releases and system dependencies with engineers.
  • Demonstrated experience driving cross-functional technology initiatives involving multiple teams.
  • Strong ability to understand technical dependencies and identify risks before they become delivery problems.
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity, changing priorities and incomplete information.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, particularly across teams with different priorities.
  • Ability to operate effectively with distributed / geographically dispersed engineering teams.
  • Strong ownership mindset — you see a problem through to resolution rather than simply escalating it.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Ability to operate in a high-paced startup environment where processes are evolving continuously.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in a consumer internet, marketplace, OTA, fintech, mobility or other high-scale technology environment.
  • Experience working with microservices, APIs, cloud infrastructure or data platforms.
  • Engineering / Computer Science background.
  • Experience working with external technology vendors or partners.
  • Experience managing programs involving multiple engineering teams and complex integrations.
  • Experience in an environment where Product and Engineering operate with high autonomy and lightweight processes.

What Success Looks Like

After 6 months, you should be the person teams rely on to answer:

  • What exactly are we trying to deliver?
  • Which teams and systems are involved?
  • What are the critical dependencies?
  • What is blocking us?
  • Who needs to make a decision?
  • What can derail the program?
  • What needs to happen next?

You don't need to create more meetings or more status reports.

You need to make complex things happen.

Candidates are responsible for safeguarding sensitive company data against unauthorized access, use, or disclosure, and for reporting any suspected security incidents in line with the organization's ISMS (Information Security Management System) policies and procedures.

title: ART 1486 - Application Engineer (Site Reliability)
description:
Summary:

The successful candidate will build and operate the AI platform that the rest of the firm consumes, i.e. the gateway to model providers, the workflow and agent runtime, the enterprise AI portal, and the experimentation environment used by the organization's investment research.

The candidate is responsible to build the automation, infrastructure, observability and release discipline that stops the same class of problem recurring.

He or she will be the release manager, i.e. owning scope, coordination and change records for what goes live. The role will lead the platform carrying more services than it started with, and less manual effort holding it up.

Skillset (Must have)

  • Possess a degree in Computer Science/Information Technology or related fields.
  • Hands-on experience in Production Kubernetes, ideally Amazon EKS. Able to diagnose why a pod is failing, why a rollout is stuck, or why a node is under pressure, without a runbook.
  • Strong practical experience in Infrastructure as Code (IaC), ideally using Terraform. Experience in composing and applying shared modules, managing state across environments, reading a plan and knowing what it will actually do before applying it, and recovering when an apply fails part-way. The candidate does not need to have authored a reusable module library (that is owned centrally here), but need to be genuinely comfortable extending existing IaC.
  • Experience in Core Hyperscaler (AWS, Azure, or GCP) in production, ideally AWS - networking/VPC, IAM, managed Kubernetes, managed relational databases, object storage, and key management with a real understanding of least-privilege access.
  • Experience in release and change ownership. The candidate has personally owned releases into a controlled production environment: scope, notes, coordination with dependent teams, a change record and a rollback plan. This is a must-have requirement, and be able to build a pipeline and owns what goes through it.
  • Experience in CI/CD pipeline ownership, building and maintaining pipelines, and not only consuming them.
  • Experience in observability design judgement. Able to argue why one metric deserves an alert and another does not, and to describe both an alert that is fought to add and deliberately deleted.

title: Research Associate II
description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

08

Role Scope

The Research Associate II is responsible for creating and delivering high-quality financial content from sell-side research, leveraging both advanced data extraction technologies and domain expertise. This role plays a critical part in delivering accurate and actionable financial insights that empower clients to make well-informed investment decisions.

By ensuring the highest standards of data quality and reliability, this position strengthens the credibility and usability of consensus data — directly contributing to client satisfaction, business success, and a strong presence in the financial markets.

Note: This is not an Equity Research or Financial Modeling role. The team does not write research reports or create sell-side models. The role provides an opportunity to deeply learn businesses and financial models by studying the work of leading sell-side analysts across sectors, geographies, and business models.

What You'll Do (Key Responsibilities)

Operational Delivery

  • Prepare insightful financial content from sell-side research using a mix of extraction technologies and sector knowledge.
  • Develop and demonstrate a strong understanding of diverse business models for public-listed companies.
  • Track events for a set of companies — starting with corporate earnings and M&A transactions — with a focus on changes in models.
  • Identify and flag errors in financial models using structured rules and statistics-based tools.

Process Excellence

  • Collaborate actively within the team to continuously improve the efficiency of the overall data collection process.
  • Apply knowledge of financial statements, GAAP/Recurring income, and other financial concepts to ensure data accuracy.
  • Break down and interpret financial models to understand the building blocks of a company's business model.
  • Apply an eye for detail and leverage structured tools to identify and correct modeling errors proactively.
  • Quickly learn the end-to-end process and build the capability to take on a reviewer role.

Stakeholder Management

  • Collaborating on model interpretation, sharing knowledge on sector-specific nuances, supporting consistency in output.
  • Highlight critical errors or modeling anomalies to team leads and cross-functional partners to improve decision-making inputs.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to share best practices and align quality, and operational standards.
  • Articulate findings and insights clearly to stakeholders across the organization, both verbally and in written form.
  • Engaging actively during onboarding and training, raising process-related queries, contributing to knowledge-sharing sessions.

How Impact Will Be Measured (Success Metrics)

  • Accuracy and quality of financial content processed from sell-side research (error rate / quality score).
  • Timeliness of output delivery against defined SLAs and production targets.
  • Reduction in errors identified in consensus models over time, reflecting improved data quality.
  • Depth and breadth of company/sector coverage handled independently.
  • Progression toward reviewer readiness — ability to independently review and validate peer output.
  • Stakeholder feedback on communication clarity and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Effective handling of complex tasks and ownership of challenging assignments.

Skills

Technical Skills

  • Understanding of financial statements (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow Statement).
  • Knowledge of GAAP and non-GAAP/Recurring income concepts.
  • Familiarity with financial concepts and ratio analysis.
  • Ability to interpret and deconstruct sell-side financial models.
  • Experience with data extraction tools and technologies (preferred).
  • Proficiency in Excel and financial data platforms.
  • Understanding of consensus model creation and management (a plus).
  • Familiarity with AI/ML-based data extraction workflows (a plus).

Functional Skills

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to apply structured frameworks to complex financial data.
  • Ability to identify patterns, anomalies, and errors in financial models.
  • Knowledge of diverse business models across sectors, industries, and geographies.
  • Understanding of corporate events (earnings, M&A, restructuring) and their modeling implications.
  • Capability to learn the full end-to-end process and independently take on a reviewer function.
  • Deep sector expertise in specific industries (a plus).
  • Prior experience in creating or validating consensus models (a plus).

Behavioral Skills

  • Positive attitude with a high level of attention to detail.
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting mindset.
  • Excellent critical thinking and analytical aptitude.
  • Effective communication skills — able to clearly articulate findings and insights to stakeholders.
  • Collaborative team player who actively contributes to shared team goals.
  • Willingness to work across shifts on a rotational basis (Day / Morning / Night shifts as required).
  • Self-motivated with the ability to quickly adapt and upskill in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Education & Experience

  • Post Graduate CFA Level 2 cleared (a plus); or Undergraduate with CFA Level 3 cleared (a plus).
  • 0–2 years of experience in financial research, data operations, or related roles. Fresher candidates with strong academic background and interest in financial markets are encouraged to apply.

Key Interfaces & Stakeholders

  • Research Associates and Specialists within the Data Research & Operations team.
  • Cross-functional teams including Data Quality, Technology, and Process Excellence.
  • Internal stakeholders across the investing community who rely on accurate financial content.
  • Sector and domain experts providing guidance on financial models and research methodologies.

What’s In It For You?

Our Mission:

Advancing Essential Intelligence.

Our People:

We're more than 35,000 strong worldwide—so we're able to understand nuances while having a broad perspective. Our team is driven by curiosity and a shared belief that Essential Intelligence can help build a more prosperous future for us all.From finding new ways to measure sustainability to analyzing energy transition across the supply chain to building workflow solutions that make it easy to tap into insight and apply it. We are changing the way people see things and empowering them to make an impact on the world we live in. We’re committed to a more equitable future and to helping our customers find new, sustainable ways of doing business. Join us and help create the critical insights that truly make a difference.

Throughout our history, the world's leading organizations have relied on us for the Essential Intelligence they need to make confident decisions about the road ahead. title: Corporate Strategy, VP
description:
Who we are looking for

We are seeking a highly motivated, intellectually curious Vice President to join the Corporate Strategy team. The Vice President will manage complex strategy projects from problem definition through recommendation and execution planning, working closely with senior leaders across the organization. Strong candidates for this role will have demonstrated the ability to structure ambiguous problems, develop fact-based insights, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations. Typical projects could include enterprise and business strategy development, market and competitive intelligence, client segmentation and market sizing, strategic partnerships and acquisitions, market entry or exit, product and client positioning, profitability, and investment prioritization.

Why this role is important to us

The Corporate Strategy team plays a central role in shaping State Street’s future and translating enterprise priorities into strategic choices and action. Across the globe, institutional investors rely on State Street to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. The team sets the firm-wide strategic direction, evaluates the organization’s most consequential strategic questions, and provides objective, data-driven insight across State Street’s businesses to support decisions by senior management and the Board. This is a great opportunity to join a small, high-impact team with direct exposure to State Street’s senior management and Executive Committee. The group has a strong track record of developing talent that advances into leadership roles across the firm.

Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.

What you will be responsible for

As Vice President of Corporate Strategy, your will be responsible for:

  • Framing ambiguous enterprise and business issues, develop hypotheses, and identify the analyses required to inform strategic choices
  • Managing strategy projects end to end, including scope, workplan, team delegation, stakeholder engagement, quality control, recommendations, and execution planning
  • Directing quantitative and qualitative analysis, synthesizing findings, and applying business and industry knowledge to develop clear, actionable recommendations
  • Developing compelling storylines and executive-ready materials tailored to senior management, the Executive Committee, and the Board
  • Building trusted relationships with business, finance, and functional partners
  • Leading stakeholder discussions and influence outcomes without direct authority
  • Driving rapid-turn analyses for senior leadership while maintaining accuracy, sound judgment, and clear prioritization
  • Providing timely coaching and feedback, and fostering an open, collaborative, high-performance team environment
  • Anticipating risks, questions, and decision points while escalating issues with proposed solutions and maintaining accountability for project outcomes

What we value

These skills will help you succeed in this role:

  • Intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and a willingness to challenge assumptions constructively
  • Excellent critical-thinking and structured problem-solving skills, including the ability to bring clarity to ambiguous questions
  • Strong quantitative and qualitative analytical skills, with the ability to connect evidence to implications and recommendations
  • High accountability, integrity, attention to detail, and commitment to zero-defect work
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, including the ability to tailor strategic narratives to working teams, senior executives, and the Board
  • Strong financial and commercial acumen, including experience evaluating growth, profitability, investment, and strategic trade-offs
  • Demonstrated ability to engage senior stakeholders, lead productive discussions, and influence decisions through analysis and judgment
  • Proven project leadership, including delegation, quality control, coaching, and development of junior talent
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, anticipate risks, and deliver high-quality work under tight deadlines
  • Ability to develop domain knowledge quickly and apply prior experience to new strategic questions

Education & Preferred Qualifications

  • 8+ years of relevant experience in strategy consulting, corporate strategy, or a comparable strategic role with experience leading end-to-end workstreams and project teams required
  • Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred
  • Financial services experience strongly preferred, particularly in asset management, asset servicing, capital markets, data and analytics, financial technology, or wealth services
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; demonstrated ability to use research, data, and AI-enabled tools responsibly to improve the quality and speed of analysis

Salary Range:

$170,000 - $267,500 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

Employees are eligible to participate in State Street’s comprehensive benefits program, which includes: our retirement savings plan (401K) with company match; insurance coverage including basic life, medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and other optional additional coverages; paid-time off including vacation, sick leave, short term disability, and family care responsibilities; access to our Employee Assistance Program; incentive compensation including eligibility for annual performance-based awards (excluding certain sales roles subject to sales incentive plans); and, eligibility for certain tax advantaged savings plans.

title: Staff Eng, Modeling & Controls Engineering
location: LOC5026: Carretera a Villa de García Km. 3.0 , Santa Catarina, NLE, 66350, Mexico
description:
About Carrier

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure the safe transport of food, life-saving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow Carrier on social media at @Carrier.

About the role

The Controls COE is focused on delivering innovative and robust designs for equipment and system control. We serve the entire Carrier product portfolio, offering a unique opportunity to engage with multiple business units across the company. We support the design, development, test, troubleshooting, and maintenance of the controls within the system, offering the controls engineer experience in everything from conceptual design to lab testing and field trial support. We do all of this with a passion for delighting our customers, having fun, and showing genuine respect for our teams.

Key Responsibilities

As a Staff Eng, Modeling & Controls Engineering, you’ll be responsible for:

  • Lead small teams of globally distributed engineers to develop production-ready controls solutions ensuring customer and technical requirements are satisfied, and standard procedures are followed.
  • Support project management with the definition of suitable plans for development and verification, conduct stakeholder technical reviews.
  • Perform dynamic analysis of non-linear systems in development of control algorithms including system identification, controllability, robustness, stability, and optimization.
  • Work with system engineers to develop requirements and subsequently ensure controls requirements are satisfied and verified.
  • Drive decisions on control architecture solutions including allocation of controls functions both within and across physical modules (e.g. PLC, UI modules, connectivity/IoT modules).
  • Recommend updates to equipment design efforts based on control objectives versus system performance capability.
  • Support the development and calibration of physics-based plant models.
  • Develop & execute unit-tests & integration tests for control systems.
  • Perform hands-on testing in psychrometric laboratory and analyze results to direct refinements to plant model fidelity and control algorithms.
  • Apply best-in-class strategies to push testing further upstream in the development lifecycle (MIL/SIL/HIL)
  • Support strategic initiatives to improve organizational quality and efficiency through technology advancement and process improvement.

Requirements

We are seeking a talented, highly motivated, and results-driven engineer with expertise in control systems specification, design, architecture, programming, and verification. The Staff Controls Engineer will work with global, cross-disciplinary teams to design and qualify control solutions for a full range of HVAC and refrigeration systems – with a strong emphasis on model-based design methods. If this is you, get in touch with us!

  • B.S. in Electrical, Control Systems, Mechanical, or Chemical Engineering with 7+ years of controls system experience
  • OR M.S. or Ph.D. in Electrical, Control Systems, Mechanical, or Chemical Engineering with 5+ years of controls system experience

Although not necessary, it would be nice if you have:

  • Proficient knowledge of controls engineering foundations, including feedback control, linear/nonlinear control, multivariable control, system identification, and optimization.
  • Proficient in the use of Matlab-based toolsets to design, implement, and test embedded controls algorithms.
  • Proven ability to work independently with limited supervision.
  • Proven ability to lead small cross-disciplinary teams of engineers to deliver medium-to-large scope projects.
  • Excellent communication skills and a proven track record of delivering results through effective teamwork.
  • Ability to work hands-on in psychrometric laboratory environment to collect and analyze data.
  • Experience with industrial control applications.
  • Familiar with PLC or AUTOSAR styled embedded architecture.
  • Experience with vapor-compression cycles, including heat exchangers and turbomachinery compression technologies.
  • Expertise in heat transfer, two-phase flow, and thermodynamic cycle analytical skills.
  • Experience with software development lifecycle best practices, including version control, change management, release management.
  • Experience in requirements management and system integration, specifically test strategies across model-in-the-loop (MIL), software-in-the-loop (SIL), and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) domains.
  • Strong technical writing skills with ability to produce clear, concise documentation.
  • Understanding of embedded SW architectures.
  • Experience in developing and calibrating physics-based models.
  • Familiar with system optimization techniques and their application to modeling and system design.

Benefits

We offer a competitive total rewards package that may include other benefits and well‑being programs. Offerings vary by role and location and are designed to support employees’ health, security, and success.

If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete the application process, participate in an interview, or otherwise engage in the hiring process, please contact us at Carrier.Recruiting@carrier.com. We will make every effort to meet your needs in accordance with applicable laws.

Carrier is An Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status, age or any other federally protected class.

title: Technology Cost Transparency & Governance Lead
description:
Who we are looking for

We are looking for a Technology Cost Management subject matter expert, Vice President, reporting to the VP leading product, tooling, and transformation within the Global Technology Services Financial Operations Office. In this role you will build and lead a Technology Financial Management and Total Cost of Ownership capability within the Global Technology Services Financial Operations Office.

Why this role is important to us

This role will lead the business design and governance of State Street’s technology cost management capability, helping Global Technology Services provide clear, consistent insight into technology spend, cost ownership, optimization opportunities, and financial decisions for technology leaders and business stakeholders. The successful candidate will combine finance expertise, technology fluency, and strong partnership to build trusted cost transparency practices that support executive reporting, enterprise accountability, and better business decisions.

This Vice President will own the business methodology for cost management, including cost model design, allocation logic, showback, future chargeback enablement, optimization tracking, and benefit validation. The ideal candidate can turn complex cost and operating data into clear, defensible insights for senior leaders.

Why This Role Is Important to Us

Global Technology Services is expanding how it understands, governs, and manages spend across infrastructure, applications, cloud, labor, and services. This role will define how cost is measured, allocated, reported, and optimized, giving technology leadership, finance, and business stakeholders a consistent, well-governed basis for decisions. It will partner with analytics engineering, Finance, Procurement, platform, and technology owners to ensure the methodology is practical, governed, and fit for enterprise use.

What You Will Be Responsible For

  • Own the TCO/ITFM methodology, including cost pools, allocation rules, service and product costing, assumptions, and change history.

  • Establish showback reporting and chargeback preparedness, including methodology, policy inputs, stakeholder alignment, and governance.
  • Define the framework for identifying, sizing, tracking, and reporting cost optimization opportunities.
  • Set logic for validating realized savings against targets, separating deterministic results, estimates, and advisory analysis.
  • Define KPIs, reporting standards, and executive narratives that make cost transparency and optimization performance clear to senior leaders.
  • Translate financial policy, business needs, and operational realities into requirements for analytics and data delivery partners.
  • Validate that implemented calculations and data products reflect the agreed methodology and are suitable for leadership reporting.
  • Partner with finance, procurement, infrastructure, application, cloud, service catalog, and configuration management teams to improve source data.
  • Maintain documentation, assumptions, decision records, and governed methodology artifacts for consistency, repeatability, and auditability over time.
  • Serve as a trusted point of contact for cost questions, aligning technical and non-technical stakeholders on definitions, logic, and results.

What We Value

These skills will help you succeed:

  • Strong understanding of ITFM, TCO, cost allocation, showback, chargeback, and cost transparency.
  • Ability to connect financial discipline with the operating reality of a large enterprise technology organization.
  • Strong analytical judgment, including the ability to distinguish actuals, forecasts, assumptions, estimates, and recommendations.
  • Clear communication style for senior leaders, finance partners, technology teams, and non-technical audiences.
  • Comfort working across functions, resolving ambiguity, and building alignment where definitions and ownership are still maturing.
  • Exacting standards for documentation, governance, consistency, and repeatable decisions.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, Information Systems, Operations Management, or a related field preferred.

  • MBA or relevant advanced degree preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
  • Experience in ITFM, TCO, FinOps, finance transformation, business operations, and related fields.
  • Experience designing or operating cost allocation, showback, chargeback, unit costing, service costing, or benefit tracking frameworks.
  • Experience defining KPIs, allocation methods, and reporting standards for executive financial or operational reporting.
  • Experience translating financial and operational requirements into analytics, reporting, or data product requirements.
  • Familiarity with TBM taxonomy or comparable cost frameworks.
  • Experience with infrastructure, application inventory, cloud, CMDB, service catalog, or product taxonomy data preferred.
  • Relevant certifications or training preferred, such as TBM Practitioner, financial analysis, technology, finance, or service management credentials.
  • Experience working in financial services or another regulated enterprise environment preferred.

Additional Requirements

The role requires strong partnership across finance, technology, procurement, analytics engineering, and governance stakeholders. The candidate should be comfortable operating in a matrixed environment with evolving requirements, data quality considerations, and leadership reporting needs.

$110,000 - $188,750 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

Lead Projects. Connect Teams. Make an Impact.

Great projects don’t happen by accident—they happen when strong leaders bring people, priorities, and technology together.

University Health is seeking a Project Manager to lead Information Technology projects from initiation through completion. In this role, you’ll bring structure, organization, and collaboration to complex projects while keeping teams focused on scope, timelines, deliverables, and business objectives.

You’ll work closely with senior leaders, stakeholders, technical teams, and external vendors to ensure projects move forward successfully and deliver meaningful results. If you’re an organized, collaborative project professional who enjoys solving problems, managing competing priorities, and bringing projects across the finish line, we’d love to have you join our team.

What You’ll Do

As a Project Manager, you will:

  • Direct and manage project development from initiation through completion, ensuring alignment with the IT Vision, Mission, and Values.

  • Manage project scope, goals, and deliverables that support business objectives in collaboration with senior management and stakeholders.

  • Develop comprehensive project plans, communication plans, and resource estimates.

  • Identify and document project stakeholders and define their roles and responsibilities.

  • Communicate project expectations, status, and progress to team members and stakeholders in a clear, timely, and consistent manner.

  • Maintain ongoing stakeholder engagement throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Build and maintain strong business relationships that are critical to project success.

  • Manage project success criteria and ensure alignment and understanding among all involved parties throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Deliver project documentation, including status reports, proposals, requirements, and presentations.

  • Deliver reporting standards, analyze progress, and address issues or risks as they arise.

  • Manage changes in project scope, identify potential risks or crises, and develop contingency and mitigation plans.

  • Participate in ongoing professional development activities to maintain and enhance project management competencies.

  • Promote quality improvement, staff and patient safety, and cultural diversity through department operations and personal performance.

  • Maintain a courteous and helpful demeanor toward patients, visitors, employees, medical staff members, and others encountered while representing the organization.

  • Maintain current knowledge related to applicable statutes, regulations, guidelines, and standards necessary to perform job duties in accordance with the requirements of the Corporate Compliance Plan.

  • Comply with the requirements of the Code of Conduct, Corporate Compliance Plan, and Compliance Policies and Procedures, including training requirements, and participate in compliance activities under the direction of the Department Manager and Corporate Compliance Officer.

What You’ll Bring:

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or equivalent professional project management experience.

  • 2 years of professional-level project management experience.

  • Demonstrated history of successful project management.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with customers, colleagues, and management.

  • Strong organizational, prioritization, and planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks effectively.

  • Experience working with cross-functional technical teams and external vendors.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Project or equivalent project management software.

  • Microsoft Office Suite experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Project management certification such as PMP or Agile/Scrum certification, or plans to pursue a certification within the next 2 years.

  • Working knowledge of Agile, Scrum, and Waterfall project management methodologies.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced IT environment.

Why This Role Matters

Technology plays an important role in how University Health serves our patients, supports our teams, and advances our mission. As a Project Manager, you’ll help turn ideas and business needs into well-planned, successfully delivered technology solutions.

Your ability to coordinate people, manage priorities, anticipate challenges, and keep projects moving will make a direct difference across the organization.

Bring your project management expertise to a team where your work helps move healthcare forward.

At KidStrong, we help parents build stronger, smarter, more athletic kids. KidStrong is a milestone accelerator for kids walking through 11 years old. The KidStrong Childrens Coach - Role and Schedule Details:
  • We are looking for a coach with athletic or coaching experience who ideally has experience coaching kids ages 12 months to 11 years old.
  • KidStrong Coach would focus on coaching children on brain, physical, and character development that stems from the evolving monthly curriculum
  • The ideal candidate must also be comfortable speaking to parents/guardians regarding “the why” behind the KidStrong curriculum
  • Our classes run typically weekdays, 9 am -11 am and evenings until 7 pm, and weekends are typically from 8 am through lunch/noon.
  • Opportunity for a flexible work schedule depending on studio needs.
  • Additional opportunity to increase scheduled hours through private party coaching hours.
  • Prior experience as a pediatric OT/PT is a plus but not required!
Kidstrong Childrens Coach Responsibilities:
  • Coach class sizes of 6 to 15 children, age groups range from roughly 12 months old to 11 years old
  • Teach the KidStrong curriculum as provided by the HQ programming team
  • Must be able to ensure classes both start and end on schedule and follow the appropriate pace of curriculum
  • Greet students as well as the parent(s)/guardian(s) individually prior to and at the beginning of class
  • Maintain a dynamic, fun, motivational, and professional demeanor when leading the class
  • Demonstrate and manage the implementation of various exercises
  • Ensure cleanliness of the center, including the lobby, bathrooms, and blue floors - this includes taking out the trash, sweeping and mopping, wiping down equipment, and sanitizing the mat at the end of a shift
  • Effectively use the KS Coach’s App to record class data and provide records of data for parents (attendance, awards, etc.)
  • Communicate professionally with co-workers in Slack, our company messaging system, including periodic checks of messages when not in centers
  • Complete training through FranConnect as required by the HQ Training and Certification team
  • Must be able to work in a physically intensive environment - coaches may cover multiple miles in a shift moving through class, lifting and repeatedly moving equipment up to 25 pounds in weight.
  • Must be comfortable working "hands-on" with kids to ensure proper technique and ensure student safety.
  • Assist parents of students ages three and younger with the direction and flow of a class
  • Attend monthly center staff programming meetings to receive training for next month's curriculum
  • Attend additional mandatory staff meetings as required by the KidStrong Director
  • Learn and manage Coach KidStrong Academy - special classes held by centers when local schools are not operating (for example Winter Break, Summer Break)
  • Must obtain certified status by the HQ Training and Certification team
  • Attend monthly center staff programming meetings to receive training for next month’s curriculum
KidStrong Childrens Coach Qualifications:
  • Passion for working with children is non-negotiable!
  • Prior experience coaching students within the appropriate KidStrong age is preferred
  • Prior experience speaking to and educating parents on the KidStrong curriculum
  • Intermediate knowledge of physiology, exercise techniques, and body mechanics
  • CPR certified
  • Positive, motivating, and effective interpersonal communication skills
  • Self-starter who just gets a job done
  • If you enjoy the spotlight, this position was meant for you!
Interested? Apply Today!

title: Senior Staff SaaS Security, Defensive Engineering
description:

We are looking for a Senior Staff SaaS Security Engineer reporting directly to a Head of Defensive Engineering organization. You will lead the deployment, integration, and operationalization of SaaS security platforms and controls, driving visibility, governance, and protection across the enterprise SaaS ecosystem.

  • Experience partnering with application owners and platform teams to drive posture improvements and remediation efforts.
  • Strong knowledge of OAuth, SSO/SAML, API permissions, and security models used by modern SaaS platforms.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

title: Risk Strategy & AI Transformation, Director - RQA
description:
About this role

BlackRock's purpose is to help more and more people experience financial well-being. As a fiduciary to investors and a leading provider of financial technology, we help millions of people build savings that serve them throughout their lives by making investing easier and more affordable. Risk & Quantitative Analysis (RQA) is at the center of BlackRock's investment and technology platform. RQA provides independent oversight, risk analytics, portfolio insights, model governance, and strategic risk advisory across the firm's investment and technology activities. As BlackRock accelerates its 2030 strategy, AI transformation and Private Markets growth represent two of the most important strategic priorities for the firm. RQA is playing a central role in both.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly motivated Director to join RQA's Strategy & AI Transformation team. This individual will act as a senior delivery leader across some of the firm's highest-profile strategic initiatives, spanning AI transformation, Private Markets risk management, operating model redesign, and cross-functional innovation programs. The role will partner closely with senior leaders across RQA, Technology & Operations, BlackRock AI Labs, BLK Next, Digital Workplace, Aladdin, PMG Tech, and Private Markets businesses to drive execution of a multi-year transformation agenda. Success in this role requires exceptional organizational leadership, executive presence, strategic thinking, and the ability to translate ambitious ideas into tangible outcomes. This position is based in New York and will work directly with senior leadership across the firm.

What We Are Looking For

The ideal candidate combines the execution discipline of a world-class program leader with the curiosity and adaptability of a startup operator. They are comfortable navigating ambiguity, building relationships across senior stakeholder groups, and driving complex initiatives from concept through implementation. Most importantly, they are excited by the opportunity to help shape the future of risk management, AI-enabled decision making, and Private Markets at BlackRock.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Program Leadership

  • Lead the day-to-day execution of a portfolio of strategic initiatives across AI transformation, operating model redesign, and Private Markets risk management.
  • Drive program governance, prioritization, milestone management, dependency tracking, issue resolution, and executive reporting across multiple workstreams.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on program execution risks, resource allocation, and delivery strategy.
  • Coordinate complex initiatives involving stakeholders across RQA, AI Labs, Technology, Aladdin, Private Markets, and corporate functions.

AI Transformation

  • Support execution of RQA's AI strategy and flagship transformation initiatives, including the firm's "Big Rocks" program.
  • Partner with business leaders to identify, prioritise, and scale AI-enabled workflows.
  • Coordinate efforts across AI governance, model validation, AI risk management, technology teams, and business stakeholders.
  • Help establish repeatable operating models, governance frameworks, and adoption strategies for AI solutions across RQA.
  • Track value realisation, productivity gains, and business outcomes associated with AI investments.

Private Markets Strategy & Innovation

  • Support the evolution of BlackRock's Private Markets risk management operating model.
  • Coordinate strategic initiatives spanning Private Credit, Private Equity, Infrastructure, Real Estate, and related risk functions.
  • Work closely with investment, risk, analytics, and technology teams to drive implementation of new capabilities supporting BlackRock's growth ambitions in private markets.
  • Facilitate collaboration across legacy BlackRock and HPS and GIP teams to accelerate integration and harmonisation efforts.

Executive Engagement & Stakeholder Management

  • Develop materials and recommendations for senior leadership forums, including ExCo and GEC-level discussions.
  • Prepare strategic updates, business cases, operating model proposals, investment requests, and executive communications.
  • Influence stakeholders across organisational boundaries without direct authority.
  • Represent the team in senior meetings and act as an extension of leadership when required.

Operating Model & Team Development

  • Help design scalable operating models for AI-enabled risk management.
  • Contribute to workforce transformation efforts, including AI adoption, capability development, and organisational effectiveness.
  • Support development of governance frameworks, delivery standards, and best practices across strategic programs.
  • Identify opportunities to improve execution discipline, transparency, and cross-functional collaboration.

Required

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 8+ years of relevant experience in strategy, transformation, program management, consulting, technology, risk management, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience leading large-scale cross-functional transformation programs.
  • Strong understanding of AI, data, analytics, or digital transformation initiatives.
  • Exceptional project and program management skills.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to engage credibly with senior executives and technical specialists alike.
  • Proven track record of influencing stakeholders without formal authority.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Ability to operate effectively in highly ambiguous and fast-changing environments.

Preferred

  • Experience within financial services, asset management, fintech, or technology.
  • Knowledge of investment management, risk management, or private markets.
  • Experience working with AI, machine learning, data platforms, or enterprise transformation programs.
  • MBA or advanced degree preferred.

For New York, NY Only the salary range for this position is USD$173,500.00 - USD$270,000.00 . Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy and your total compensation may vary based on role, location, and firm, department and individual performance.


Our benefits

To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits including a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, comprehensive healthcare, support for working parents and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.

Our hybrid work model

BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.


Guidance on AI use for candidates


At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.


About BlackRock


At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.


This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.


To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com. We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and TikTok.

description:

The Associate Principal – Workplace Interior Designer is a strategic design leader responsible for advancing workplace interiors projects from pursuit and conceptual design through documentation and construction administration. This role translates client aspirations, workplace research, organizational goals, and program requirements into compelling, high-performing interior environments.


The Associate Principal brings a forward-looking perspective to workplace design, incorporating evolving models of work—including hybrid work, activity-based working (ABW), employee experience, and workplace wellness—into thoughtful and adaptable environments. title: Senior Analyst, Structures & Pricing
description:
Are you ready to be part of a company that's not just talking about the future, but actively shaping it? Join The AES Corporation, the largest US-based global power company with a team of 8,300 employees across 12 countries.

AES has been ranked #1 by BloombergNEF in renewable energy sales to corporations in the US and Americas for five consecutive years, providing electricity for millions of people worldwide.

We are proud to foster a strong workplace culture, earning prominent positions in Great Place to Work™ rankings across the markets where we operate. AES was also named one of the World’s Most Ethical Companies for the 13th consecutive year in 2026, highlighting our dedication to integrity, transparency, and responsible business practices.

Our spirit of innovation continues to earn industry recognition. AES is the only seven-time winner of the Edison Electric Institute’s Edison Awards in the twenty-first century, a distinction honoring global leadership in advancing the electric power industry.

If you're ready to be part of a company that's not just adapting to change, but driving it, AES is the place for you. We're not just building a more sustainable future, we're powering it. Apply now and energize your career with a true leader in global energy.

At AES, we are accelerating the future of energy through innovation, collaboration, and a shared commitment to building a more sustainable world. As a global energy company and leader in renewable energy solutions, we empower our people to help shape the energy transition while developing meaningful and rewarding careers.

We are seeking a Senior Analyst, Structures & Pricing to join our Commercial team and report to the Vice President, Structured Trading & Analytics.

In this role, you will help drive AES's renewable energy growth strategy by supporting the structuring, valuation, and commercial analysis of solar, wind, energy storage, and thermal generation opportunities. You will collaborate across Origination, Trading, Engineering, Risk Management, and Digital teams to develop innovative solutions for a diverse range of customers, including hyperscalers, utilities, community choice aggregators (CCAs), data centers, and large corporate energy buyers.

This is an opportunity to work on complex and high-impact transactions while building expertise in energy markets, structured products, commercial strategy, and advanced analytics. At AES, we encourage continuous learning, professional growth, and collaboration across disciplines, providing exposure to some of the most dynamic areas of the energy industry.

Key Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with commercial teams to design structured energy products, evaluate transactions, and develop valuation models supporting renewable and thermal generation opportunities.

  • Partner with Origination, Mergers & Acquisitions, Trading, and Development teams to create innovative commercial solutions for utilities, hyperscalers, data centers, and other large energy consumers.

  • Work alongside the ETRM team to support the implementation of approved commercial structures, valuation methodologies, and associated workflows across systems and analytical tools.

  • Partner with Risk Management teams to support model validation, risk assessment, governance, and decision-making processes.

  • Contribute to the ongoing enhancement and automation of analytical models, workflows, and recurring reporting processes.

  • Support the development of scalable analytical capabilities that improve efficiency and commercial insight across the organization.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Data Science, Physical Sciences, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

  • Experience in energy transaction valuation, commercial analysis, quantitative modeling, structured products, trading, asset management, portfolio management, or related areas.

  • Knowledge of wholesale power markets, energy market fundamentals, pricing dynamics, or renewable energy economics.

  • Experience developing analytical or production-level models using one or more tools such as Python, R, MATLAB, VBA, or similar technologies.

  • Strong quantitative, analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

  • Ability to work collaboratively across teams and effectively communicate complex concepts to diverse audiences.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree (MBA, Master's, or equivalent) in a relevant field.

  • Exposure to U.S. wholesale power markets such as ERCOT, CAISO, PJM, NYISO, MISO, or similar energy markets.

  • Experience working with renewable energy projects, energy storage, structured transactions, risk management, or trading organizations.

  • Familiarity with automation, advanced analytics, data visualization, or commercial optimization tools.

Respecting all backgrounds, differences and perspectives enables us to improve the lives of our people, customers, suppliers, contractors, and the communities in which we live and work. Build Technology That Makes a Difference

At University Health, technology plays an important role in helping our teams deliver exceptional care and support the work happening across our organization.

  • Design, develop, and test databases as necessary to support applications.

What You’ll Bring

Minimum Requirements

  • Knowledge of programming languages including Visual Basic, SQL, Shell Script, ASP.NET, C#, VB.NET, HTML, and javascript.

  • Ability to communicate effectively with customers, co-workers, and management through verbal communication and written communication.

  • Ability to understand customer business processes, gather system requirements, create system and application documentation.

  • Ability to organize, prioritize and plan work effectively.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 1-3 years of professional level developer experience.

Why This Role Matters

The applications you develop and support can have a direct impact on how effectively our teams work and how reliably our organization operates. If you’re a developer who enjoys combining technical expertise with problem-solving, collaboration, and customer service, this role offers an opportunity to put your skills to work in a mission-driven healthcare environment.

description:
Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. As we shape the future of healthcare, we are leveraging advanced technologies, intelligent digital solutions and data-driven innovation across our operations to enhance how work gets done and deliver greater value to customers and patients. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.


Labcorp is seeking a Network Infrastructure & Automation Engineering Intern to join our Enterprise Infrastructure team located in Durham, NC with the flexibility of a hybrid work schedule!

Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 40hrs per week

Job Responsibilities:

  • Learning how enterprise data center networks are designed and operated using Arista EOS and CloudVision-as-a-Service
  • Exploring Infrastructure-as-Code and Network-as-Code concepts using Ansible and Arista AVD
  • Building and testing network validation using Arista ANTA
