  • Learning how application traffic is delivered through Citrix NetScaler VPX
  • Working with enterprise DNS, DHCP, IP address management, and NTP services
  • Exploring network telemetry, packet visibility, and analytics using platforms such as ExtraHop and Arista DMF
  • Learning how infrastructure changes are developed, reviewed, version-controlled, tested, and deployed
  • Working with Bitbucket, Linux, APIs, YAML, JSON, and Python-based tooling
  • Building dashboards, reports, or automated infrastructure health checks
  • Assisting with infrastructure documentation and operational runbooks
  • Participating in troubleshooting exercises and root-cause analysis
  • Learning how enterprise infrastructure integrates with security, cloud, compute, and application teams
  • Participating in engineering design discussions and change reviews
  • Presenting the results of your summer project to engineers and IT leadership

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Current enrollment in a Bachelor's degree program in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Engineering, Network Engineering, Information Systems or Electrical/Computer Engineering

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3-6 months experience in TCP/IP networking, Routing and switching, Linux
  • 3-6 months experience in Python
  • 3-6 months experience in Automation or scripting, APIs
  • 3-6 months experience in Cloud computing, Cybersecurity
  • 3-6 months experience in Git or source control

Additional Job Standards:

  • You may have an opportunity to work with or learn technologies including:
  • Data Center Networking - Arista EOS, CloudVision as a Service, Arista AVD, ANTA, and DMF
  • Application Delivery - NetScaler VPX, NetScaler Console, and Venafi certificate management
  • Core Network Services - Infoblox NIOS, DNS, DHCP, IPAM/DDI, public DNS, internal DNS, NTP, and enterprise integrations

  • Observability - ExtraHop and network telemetry/analytics platforms
  • Work directly with senior network and infrastructure engineers

  • Learn how engineers troubleshoot complex production issues
  • Understand enterprise change-management practices
  • Receive code and configuration reviews
  • Learn how technical decisions are communicated to leadership
  • Develop technical documentation and presentation skills
  • Explore different career paths within networking, automation, cloud, security, and infrastructure engineering
  • Example summer projects: Network Automation, Automated Network Validation, Infrastructure Health Dashboard, Configuration Compliance, DNS / DHCP Automation, Network Observability, Infrastructure-as-Code Lab

The Vice President of People Group Business Partnership (VP, PGBP) is a strategic, executive leader responsible for the execution of the organization's global human capital strategy in alignment with business objectives. Reporting to the Chief People Officer, this person oversees the Business Partner function, leads the people-related aspects of mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and integrations, and ensures executional excellence through effective partnership, governance, policies, and compliance programs. The VP, PGBP serves as a trusted advisor to executive leadership and drives the execution of initiatives that enhance organizational performance, employee engagement, talent development, and workforce effectiveness across multiple regions and business segments.

The successful candidate is an accomplished leader who demonstrates exceptional strategic agility, enabling the organization to anticipate and respond effectively to evolving business needs, market dynamics, and workforce challenges. This executive fosters operational excellence by driving accountability, execution and balanced HR solutions that support organizational growth. The VP, PGBP excels at building strong partnerships across all levels of the organization, operating effectively within a matrixed organization, and cultivating trusted relationships with executives, business leaders, team members, and external stakeholders to achieve shared goals. Additionally, this leader possesses an intensive drive for results, balancing strategic vision with disciplined execution to deliver measurable business outcomes, accelerate organizational performance, and support long-term enterprise success.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Human Resources Leadership

  • Partner with the CPO and executive leadership accordingly to develop and execute human capital strategies aligned with organizational goals and growth objectives.
  • Serve as a member of the senior leadership team, providing strategic counsel on workforce planning, targeted organizational design, and change management.
  • Lead enterprise-wide initiatives that support business growth, transformation, culture development, and organizational effectiveness.
  • Monitor industry trends, labor market dynamics, and emerging practices to maintain a competitive advantage.
  • Partner with PG COEs to drive proper alignment between talent and culture solutions with business-related needs.

Global Business Partner Leadership

  • Lead and develop a team of PG Business Partners supporting multiple business units, functions, and geographic regions.
  • Partner with business leaders to identify workforce needs and implement targeted solutions (aligned to enterprise programs and practices) that drive performance, productivity, and team member engagement.
  • Provide guidance on organizational design, leadership development, performance management, employee relations, and change management.
  • Ensure consistency in PG practices while balancing regional requirements and cultural considerations.

Mergers, Acquisitions, and Integration

  • Lead all people-related aspects of mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures, and business integrations.
  • Conduct PG due diligence, including assessment of workforce risks, organizational structures, compensation programs, benefits, labor relations, and compliance issues.
  • Develop and execute integration strategies that align talent, culture, organizational structures (specifically job and compensation), and PG programs and processes.
  • Partner with legal, finance, and executive stakeholders throughout transaction lifecycles.
  • Manage team member communications, retention strategies, workforce transitions, and change management initiatives during M&A activities.
  • Ensure seamless integration of PG systems, policies, and programs following acquisitions.

PG Administration, Policies, and Procedures

  • In partnership with PG Operations, oversee the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of PG policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable employment laws, regulations, and labor requirements across all operating jurisdictions.
  • Maintain employee handbooks, policy manuals, and standard operating procedures.
  • Partner with legal and compliance teams to mitigate employment-related risks.

Talent Management

title: Data Specialist
description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

09

Role Scope

Data Steward is an individual contributor role responsible for executing core data stewardship activities that ensure the accuracy, integrity, and governance of enterprise data assets. The Data Steward manages end‑to‑end lineage monitoring, maintains high‑quality metadata, enforces policy and control compliance, and supports UAT for database changes and product distribution. Within the European Gas and Power Data team, the role supports the controlled transition of source data into internal databases and downstream delivery pipelines, ensuring raw data is validated, reconciled, transformed, and quality checked before it is made available to internal SMEs and external clients. The role performs detailed data validation, vendor data reviews, and works closely with Technology and Data Operations teams to resolve issues and maintain consistent data standards across systems.

Additionally, the Data Steward contributes to process improvement by driving standardization, enhancing documentation, and supporting the adoption of automation and AI‑enabled capabilities to improve data quality, reduce manual effort, and strengthen operational efficiency. We are looking for a process-orientated, methodological thinker with a keen eye for detail. Someone who enjoys dealing with large sets of data and problem solving.

What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)

Operational Delivery

  • Perform data validation checks, lineage tracking, and metadata updates to maintain data quality, integrity, and traceability.

  • Execute data ingestion, validation, and integration activities in alignment with governance and control standards.

  • Ensure consistent adherence to enterprise data policies and governance frameworks.

  • Execute defined controls and compliance requirements to safeguard data integrity and lineage.

  • Support vendor data reviews and onboarding through data quality assessments, validation checks, and issue resolution.

  • Maintain data standardization, stewardship documentation, and process artifacts to ensure accuracy and consistency.

  • Execute medium‑complexity stewardship and validation tasks under established guidelines, escalating exceptions when required.

  • Respond to client data queries, resolving issues and coordinating issue triage with Operations and Client Services teams.

  • Collaborate with Technology teams on defect resolution, enhancement requests, and UAT for backend data and dataflow changes.

  • Contribute to automation and AI‑enabled improvements that enhance efficiency and strengthen stewardship capabilities.

  • Investigate, validate, troubleshoot, and support controlled updates to transformation scripts, data quality rules, and pipeline logic using Python, SQL and PySpark, ensuring automated processes continue to run to schedule producing accurate outputs.

  • Support onboarding of new datasets required by SMEs by reviewing source structures, validating expected outputs, identifying data quality risks, and coordinating required pipeline or source data changes within the existing architecture.

Process Excellence

  • Support User Acceptance Testing (UAT) by validating data, coordinating test execution, and assisting with defect identification and resolution.

  • Ensure adherence to governance, data management standards, and operating procedures by following defined controls and compliance requirements.

  • Maintain high‑quality documentation by updating process flows, data definitions, data dictionaries, and other stewardship artifacts to ensure audit readiness and operational clarity.

Stakeholder Management

  • Collaborate with Data Operations and Technology teams to support governance activities, quality controls, source amendments, validation outcomes and issue remediation while serving as a key liaison between governance expectations and day‑to‑day execution

  • Support Product and Technology teams by assisting with data requirements, validations, and operational coordination throughout change cycles.

  • Assist with vendor data reviews by conducting data quality checks, performing validations, and coordinating onboarding processes.

How Impact Will Be Measured (Success Metrics)

  • Data accuracy and integrity - Maintain high accuracy rates through consistent validation, timely corrections, and adherence to defined quality thresholds.

  • SLA and turnaround adherence - Meet or exceed service‑level timelines for data updates, validations, issue resolution, and stakeholder responses.

  • Documentation completeness and currency - Keep process documentation, data dictionaries, lineage records, and stewardship artifacts up‑to‑date, audit‑ready, and fully aligned with governance standards.

  • Pipeline quality and delivery - Ensure transformation scripts, database workflows, quality checks, and scheduled processes run successfully, with failures investigated, validated, resolved, or coordinated through to closure in line with operational priorities.

For This Role You'll Need to Have (Skills & Competencies)

Technical Skills

  • Intermediate Python scripting skills, including the ability to investigate, maintain, debug, and support controlled updates to transformation logic, automation scripts, and data quality checks.

  • Intermediate SQL capability to query, reconcile, transform, validate, and troubleshoot data across relational databases and pipeline outputs.

  • Hands-on experience with PySpark or distributed data processing to support investigation, validation, reconciliation, and quality checks across large or complex datasets.

  • Working knowledge of Databricks, including notebooks, jobs, clusters, and pipeline monitoring, would be advantageous.

  • Understanding of cloud computing, preferably AWS.

  • Working knowledge of AI/ML workflows.

  • Works with metadata management and lineage tools to maintain data transparency and trace end‑to‑end data flows.

  • Possess foundational familiarity with BI tools and dashboards to review outputs and identify data anomalies.

Functional Skills

  • Possesses solid domain and process understanding

  • Understands data governance fundamentals, including data quality controls, stewardship roles, and ownership models.

  • Supports data standardization by applying consistent data definitions, formats, and controlled processes.

  • Has working knowledge of data ingestion, transformation, validation, reconciliation, and integration workflows, with the ability to investigate pipeline failures, check source-to-target accuracy, support root cause resolution, and coordinate remediation actions.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand their data requirements/issues and generate innovative ideas and solutions.

Behavioral Skills

  • Demonstrates strong attention to detail, ensuring accuracy in data, documentation, and validation activities, functional teams cause analysis.

  • Communicates clearly and collaborates effectively with cross functional teams including Technology, Operations, Product, and Vendor partners.

  • Applies analytical mindset, critical thinking & creative problem solving to build solutions for business problems and while investigating data issues and remediation through root cause analysis.

  • Demonstrates learning agility, digital acumen, initiative, and ownership in data stewardship activities, adapting to evolving tools and technologies while working effectively through ambiguity to investigate issues, and support timely delivery against operational priorities.

Preferred Education & Experience

  • 4+ years of relevant experience in data, analytics, operations, or related functions.

Key Interfaces & Stakeholders

  • Partner with Data Operations and SMEs on data risk, quality checks, and issue resolution.

  • Coordinate with Tech teams on data issues, enhancements, and UAT activities.

  • Support Product teams with data requirements and validation.

  • Ensure alignment with governance and compliance standards.

title: Extreme Weather Response (EWR) Coordinator
description:
Who We Are

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description:

The EWR Coordinator will monitor the weather patterns to determine when the EWR program needs to operate. They will send /gather information on who is operating and send notifications to service providers throughout the community during the winter season about the activation and the mat programs available. The coordinator will assist the ARC and other service providers to prepare for emergency weather events and maintain collaborative relationships key community stakeholders. This position will complete reporting requirements as per the contractual obligations with BC housing.

Accountabilities:

The incumbent may perform all, some, or similar duties to the listed below:

  • Monitor weather patterns and determine the need to operate the EWR.
  • Notify the service providers and determine who is able to operate on any given EWR activation.
  • Send out notification to key stakeholders when the emergency programs are operating and
  • determine when the activation will be rescinded as per the criteria in the community plan.
  • Assist in maintaining strong collaborative relationships with community service providers and stakeholders.
  • Develop strong working relationships with EWR service providers and stakeholder organizations.
  • Monitor weather patterns using Environment Canada and other weather reporting organizations to determine, based on criteria, the operation of the EWR services.
  • Notify the service providers of activation and deactivate when weather improves.
  • Coordinate the formal notification of stakeholder organizations of the activation and deactivation.
  • Coordinate community meetings every two months to discuss processes and activations throughout the winter period. These meetings are designed to improve communication with the community and key service providers with the EWR coordination organization and manage any concerns or issues as they arise.
  • Provide media information and referral of media to appropriate individual to manage and monitor media.
  • Monitor media for information or concerning articles and mitigate with the assistance of BC housing communications and outstanding issues in the community.
  • Gather data, research and required information to support the annual reporting requirements for the EWR program.
  • Develop an annual report for submission to BC housing as per contract obligations
  • Bi-monthly community meetings and report back on EWR program activations, capacity levels, and operational concerns
  • Willingness to develop an understanding and support for the mission and purpose of The Salvation Army in Canada and its implications as related to position responsibilities.
  • Work in compliance with OH&S Act and Regulations and abide by The Salvation Army’s health and safety policies and procedures.
  • Ability to provide an original copy of a Background Check that is satisfactory to The Salvation Army, in its sole discretion, is required, including Child Check (if appropriate).

Education, Qualifications and Certifications:

  • Bachelor level degree in human services or equivalent combination of education and experience required.
  • Clear criminal record check through the BC Criminal Record Review Program.
  • Clear TB skin test required.
  • Occupational First Aid Level 1 or equivalent.

Experience and Knowledge:

  • 2-3 years’ experience coordinating community programs.
  • 2 years’ experiencing building and maintaining relationships with stakeholders.
  • Good understanding of EWR program and familiarity with service providers is an asset.
  • Clear understanding of monitoring and projecting weather patterns is an asset.
  • 2 years’ experience managing media and community relations.
  • Solid knowledge of homeless and unhoused population.

title: Quality and Compliance Coordinator
description:
We're proud to be part of STARK Building Materials UK and dedicated to providing top-quality products and exceptional service to our customers. We're a friendly and collaborative team, passionate about what we do and committed to doing it well.

We’re searching for a Quality and Compliance Coordinator to cover a 12-month maternity contract based out of our Binley Head Office. You will be responsible for coordinating our quality and environmental systems across our civils and drylining/insulation divisions. This role is critical in maintaining our ISO 9001, ISO 4001, Achilles and Constructionline accreditations, ensuring our products, suppliers and operations meet rigorous industry standards. Also, to own, manage and return RFI, PQQ and framework documentation from clients as and when sent through by colleagues.

Key Responsibilities

Quality Management (ISO 9001)

  • Maintain and enhance the Quality Management System (QMS) across civils and drylining/insulation product lines.
  • Conduct internal audits and manage external audit processes to ensure ongoing ISO 9001 certification.
  • Monitor product quality, customer complaints, and non-conformance trends across both divisions.
  • Collaborate with warehouse and sales teams to ensure consistent quality control procedures.

Environmental Management (ISO 14001)

  • Oversee the Environmental Management System (EMS), ensuring compliance with ISO 14001.
  • Implement sustainable practices across logistics, packaging, and product sourcing.
  • Support depot teams in managing waste streams and reducing environmental impact.

Accreditations: Achilles & Constructionline

  • Coordinate and maintain Achilles and Constructionline registrations, ensuring timely renewals and accurate submissions.
  • Coordinate with commercial teams to provide documentation for prequalification and tendering.
  • Stay up to date with accreditation requirements and industry changes.

Supplier & Product Compliance

  • Vet and monitor suppliers of civils materials (e.g., drainage, aggregates, geotechnical) and drylining/insulation systems (e.g., plasterboard, mineral wool, PIR boards).
  • Ensure all products meet relevant standards (e.g., CE marking, BBA certification, fire ratings).
  • Maintain a central compliance database including technical datasheets, declarations of performance, and supplier certifications.

Framework and PQQ Request Ownership

  • Colleagues end through requests from clients for Pre-Qualification Questionnaires, Requests for information, Insurance details and Framework documentation assistance. This is not an exhaustive list.
  • You will be responsible for collating the relevant information and returning it, either directly to the client online via portals, via email or back to the colleague to send on.
  • Reactive and unplanned, usually with little notice and tight deadlines.

Knowledge, Skills, Qualifications and Experience required

  • Proven experience in quality management within a merchant/distribution environment, ideally covering both civils and interior systems.
  • Strong knowledge of ISO 9001, ISO 14001, Achilles, and Constructionline.
  • Familiarity with civils products (e.g., concrete, drainage) and drylining/insulation systems (e.g., plasterboard, insulation boards).
  • Excellent auditing, documentation, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Relevant qualifications in quality or environmental management (e.g., IRCA, CQI, NEBOSH).
  • Ability to influence operational teams and suppliers to uphold quality standards.
  • Strong attention to detail and analytical mindset.
  • Comfortable working across multiple sites and managing remote compliance activities.
  • Experience with digital QMS platforms or supplier portals.

What’s in it for you?

  • Competitive Base salary
  • Hybrid Working – 4 days at our Binley, Coventry office and 1 day WFH.
  • Discretionary bonus
  • Retirement savings plan
  • Life assurance
  • Enhanced maternity/paternity/adoption leave for anyone expecting or adopting a child
  • A wide range of voluntary benefits including holiday buying, discounted gym membership, car salary sacrifice scheme, Cycle2Work, Benenden Healthcare and more.
  • Access to a wealth of health and wellbeing services including access to online GP appointments and mental health support.
  • WorkPerks – A platform home to hundreds of all your favourite high street and online discounts via the provider Reward Gateway.

Why Choose Us?

Quality - We’re unwavering in our commitment to providing outstanding products and service that exceed our customers’ expectations.

Supportive Environment - Join a culture that prioritises your growth, with the resources and support you need to excel. We listen and learn – we know we haven’t always got all the answers – listening and learning with you is what helps provide the best service to our customers.

Professional Development - We are invested in your success! Can we add this instead? You have a real chance to progress- the only limits are your own Explore our apprenticeships, training, and mentoring programs designed to elevate your career.

Great Benefits - Enjoy a compelling package that includes a competitive salary, bonuses, pension schemes, and life assurance, among many other perks!

Work-Life Balance - We value your well-being and offer flexible working hours and a hybrid working model to help you find your ideal rhythm

What's Next

If your application is successful, our Talent team will reach out to arrange an interview and answer any questions you may have. We are committed to providing reasonable adjustments to ensure you can perform at your best throughout the application and interview process.

title: Head, Non-Financial Risk
description:
To provide pro-active management and operational support enabling the implementation of the Non-Financial Risk (NFR) management strategy across the Business and Commercial Banking (BCB), Personal and Private Banking (PPB), and Asset Management (AM). The role is responsible for embedding risk management processes to identify and mitigate NFRs.

Minimum Qualification:

  • First Degree in Business Commerce
  • First Degree in Risk Management

Experience Required :

  • 3–4 years’ experience in Risk and/or Corporate Affairs within financial services.
  • Working knowledge of Information Risk, including familiarity with UK frameworks and regulations such as UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, and industry standards (e.g. ISO 27001, ISF Standard of Good Practice).
  • Practical experience of risk and control frameworks, assurance, and their application in the financial services industry. Good understanding of risk appetite, risk response, and process improvement.
  • Broad understanding of both non-financial risk and financial reporting risk characteristics.

Key Outputs :

  • Act as the NFR interface to support fraud risk management and collaborate with relevant teams on information risk threats and controls across business units.
  • Partner with the business to strengthen risk management capability, equipping teams to mitigate financial, reputational, and regulatory impacts of NFR incidents.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including senior management, audit functions, and regulators.
  • Oversee and challenge the risk and control cycle (RCSA) ensuring risk reporting, escalation, and actions are data-driven with clear accountability.
  • Support delivery through collaboration and continuous improvement, including mentoring where required.
  • Complete RCSA activities across relevant business areas, ensuring all applicable risk types are assessed and captured in the NFR management system.
  • Analyse business impact and support risk acceptance processes for residual risks, including preparing recommendations and escalating where risk levels exceed appetite.

GBP 73,000 to GBP 88,000

Northrop Grumman Defense Systems is seeking an Systems Engineer / Principal Systems Engineer. This position is located in Roy, UT and supports the Sentinel program.

The selected candidate will be responsible for the integration and test of hardware, software, and firmware test stations used for risk reduction and development of GN&C software. The selected candidate will also be involved in defining test set requirements and ensuring design and performance meet acceptance test procedure standards.

Basic Qualifications:


This requisition may be filled at either the Systems Engineer level (T02) or Principal Systems Engineer level (T03).

  • Systems Engineer (T02): Bachelor's degree in a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics) discipline with a minimum 2 years of related experience; 0 years with a Master’s or PhD

  • Principal Systems Engineer (T03): Bachelor's degree in a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics) discipline with a minimum 5 years of related experience; 3 years with a Master’s; or 1 years with a PhD

  • Must be a US Citizen with an active U.S. Government DoD Secret security clearance at time of application with an investigation completed within the last 6 years

  • Must have the ability to obtain and maintain Special Access Program (SAP) approval within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the company to meet its business need

  • 1+ year's of experience supporting requirement development or verification

  • Define test requirements and test objectives, using Systems Engineering principles

  • Assist the team in the development of integration and test documentation (test plans, test procedures and test reports)

  • Participate in the execution of the integration, test, and assembly of the test sets in preparation for developmental flight testing

  • Support the development and implement testing methods and equipment

  • Interface with software developers and systems engineers in support of integration and test activities

  • Perform data analysis against requirements and interfaces for each software build or hardware component

  • Compile data and define changes required in test equipment, test procedures, or new test requirements

  • Maintain design documentation and follow configuration management requirements

  • Experience with Python, MATLAB, or other test scripting SW or tools.

title: Sr. Advanced Services Consulting Engineer
description:
Sr. Advanced Services Consulting Engineer

This role has been designed as ‘’Onsite’ with an expectation that you will primarily work from an HPE office.

Who We Are:

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.

Job Description:

What you'll do:

  • The two main aspect of the role would be to represent HPE customer service to the customer and as representative of the customer back to HPE.
  • Act as an consultant for post-sales customer service account for the customer, partners, and account team.Understand customer lifecycle to deliver efficiency and effectiveness to the customer.
  • Support the account/customer with alignment to services sales and product sales activities.
  • Tracking and managing the deliverables of HPE Premium Care, Advanced Care, and Optimization Service, advanced options including credits.
  • Proactively escalates and brings people with required expertise together in order to bring critical and important issues to closure.
  • Act as an interlock between Customer and HPE Professional Services, Advanced Services and Engineering for the services to be delivered to the customer.
  • Early engagement regarding major projects to consider service requirements, risk management, and expectation setting with the account team, partners, and customer.
  • Conduct Periodic reviews with internal teams / Customer to review HPE service delivery metrics, SLA and quality.
  • Uses professional knowledge to review and assess open software defects. Discovers potential risks associated with the deployment plans and partner with the customer to develop mitigation plans.
  • Delivers proactive consulting services such as technical analysis and recommendations (Impact assessment and analysis, health check analysis, software upgrade analysis, config review, etc…)
  • Partners with Customer in conducting periodic HPE product health checks to identify potential product improvement areas. Based on the evaluation makes a relevant recommendation to optimize operational performance with respect to design/topology/configuration.
  • Reviews and evaluate network plans and assist in the planning of new feature implementation and product deployment. Allies with internal teams to resolve identified risks in software.
  • Engages with HPE engineering teams to improve potential quality issues with products.
  • Document and maintain customer network solutions knowledge and educates other internal HPE resources for a better support experience.

What you need to bring:

The candidate is encouraged to have a deep understanding of core IP networking concepts (TCP/IP, QoS, VLAN, STP, IPSEC, NAT, IPv6). Should possess reasonable expertise in Layer2, Layer3 protocols such as VRRP, OSPF, BGP, Multicast, MPLS VPN.

Knowledge and experience of the newest technologies such as Segment Routing, Traffic engineering, DC switching, VxLAN, EVPN, SD-WAN & Wireless is a plus.

Experience working in large enterprises, Network service providers have added advantage.

Experience and desire to work on automation will be valuable in long run.

Amiable communication, interpersonal and social skills will make a difference!

HPE Juniper /Aruba/ Edge Connect product certifications (JNCIS/JNCIP/JNCIE) or industry equivalents are helpful.

Qualification and Experience:

We generally prefer candidates with bachelor’s degree in electrical/electronic Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent. A Business degree such as MBA would be an advantage.

8+ years’ experience in designing, implementing, and solving technical problems of the state-of-the-art Datacenter, IP/MPLS- Networks. High exposure to network operations environment. Ability to operate independently, including management of priorities in unstructured environment.

Experience with customer facing roles will prove to be an asset.

title: Bottling Scheduler
description:
Bottling Hall Scheduler

Your Manager: Senior Site Scheduler

Team: Supply Chain

Location: Kilmalid, Dumbarton

Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract – 12 months

Pernod Ricard is a worldwide leader in the spirits and champagne industry, blending traditional craftsmanship, state-of-the-art brand development, and global distribution technologies. Our prestigious portfolio of premium to luxury brands includes Absolut vodka, Ricard pastis, Ballantine’s, Chivas Regal, Royal Salute, and The Glenlivet Scotch whiskies, Jameson Irish whiskey, Martell cognac, Havana Club rum, Beefeater gin, Malibu liqueur, and Mumm and Perrier-Jouët champagnes. Our mission is to ensure the long-term growth of our brands with full respect for people and the environment, while empowering our employees around the world to be ambassadors of our purposeful, inclusive, and responsible culture of authentic conviviality

Chivas Brothers is the Pernod Ricard business dedicated entirely to Scotch whisky. Our award-winning portfolio features some of the world’s most revered single malt and blended Scotch whisky brands, including Chivas, Ballantine’s, Royal Salute, The Glenlivet and Aberlour, which are exported from Scotland to over 100 countries worldwide. As the world’s No.2 Scotch whisky producer with a 1,600-strong team across 26 sites, we are committed to upholding the heritage and pursuing the progress of Scotch and ensuring its sustainable future, as well as opening it up to new audiences across the globe.

About the role

We are currently hiring a Bottling Hall Scheduler, on a fixed term contract basis, to deliver excellent customer service by working across the Bottling & Blending supply chain, including internal stakeholders, suppliers and third parties, to ensure deliveries to the site are scheduled and available to meet the supply plan.

What you will do

Materials Planning & Capacity Management

  • Schedule the Materials Plan for delivery and secure agreement from the Dry Goods team, working with them to understand available capacity for the hall by commodity and embed a planning and capacity management process.
  • Communicate required capacity for operational stock holding and stock adjustments or quality issues that impact the materials plan.
  • Identify, populate, and maintain materials capacity fields.

Production Coordination & Schedule Execution

  • Support the aligned production hall by ensuring space and line movement requirements are accommodated.
  • Attend daily production meetings to confirm schedules and anticipate operational risks.
  • Collaborate with the Material Planner to ensure efficient production flow and material availability, highlighting where internal stock adjustments or quality issues require an adjustment to the materials plan.

Continuous Improvement & Performance Management

  • Use the DIR process to manage supplier performance and support clear ownership and follow-up on supplier performance.
  • Hold weekly review meetings with Dry Goods team to evaluate schedule adherence, delivery performance, capacity risks, stock utilisation, and line changes.
  • Support improvements to systems and processes to automate processes and remove non-value-added activities.
  • Actively support and champion supply chain transformation and strategic improvement initiatives.
  • Highlight opportunities for Kanban to the Material Planner.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Personal Development

  • Build effective relationships through 360-degree communication with partner teams.
  • Collaborate across Production, Supply Chain, Materials Planning, and Dry Goods teams to ensure alignment.
  • Engage positively in the CBL personal and professional development process, identifying development opportunities and continuously improving performance.

Your skills and background

  • Bring experience in supply chain, planning, scheduling or manufacturing environments. Experience in drinks, FMCG or a similar fast-paced environment
  • Have an understanding of cross-functional supply chain processes, including suppliers and compliance (HMRC).
  • Have experience using ERP systems or similar planning tools,
  • Hold a clean UK driving license.
  • Are confident using Excel and Microsoft Office, with the ability to analyse information and learn new tools.

Why join us?

Collective Spirit

You will be part of a connected, international community shaped by iconic brands, a performance mindset, and a proud legacy, where collaboration, fun and ambition coexist.

Craft your path

We empower you to own your career, innovate boldly and grow alongside our business, surrounded by leaders who value curiosity, energy, and impact.

Cultivate the future

You’ll help shape a business with a soul — one that cherishes the land, respects communities, and brings good times from a good place, responsibly and sustainably.

People are at the heart of everything we do at Pernod Ricard and are the foundation of our collective spirit as ‘Créateurs de Convivialité’. We promote inclusion throughout our business and supply chain. In our teams, we proactively foster a diverse work force and an inclusive culture, an environment where we can truly be ourselves.

We will assess your application for this role based on your skills, experiences, and achievements, not your gender, age, ethnic or educational background or any other such factors. Our recruiting team are more than happy to provide reasonable adjustments during our application and interview process, in order for you to participate fully in our recruitment experience.

Our mix of benefits

  • Competitive salary, along with performance related bonus
  • Defined Contribution Pension
  • Private medical insurance, including income protection.
  • Comprehensive Employee Assistance Programme
  • Generous annual holiday entitlement (increasing with length of service) plus public holidays.
  • Pernod Ricard share incentive plan and share ownership plan.
  • Life Assurance
  • An allowance each year to spend on our brands.
  • Our reward & recognition scheme
  • Employee discounts from a range of high street retailers
  • Regular events in our very own office bar

title: Aeronautical OR Principal Aeronautical Engineer (Liaison Engineering)
description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Aeronautics Systems has an opening for an Aeronautical OR Principal Aeronautical Engineer (Liaison Engineering) to join our team located at NAS Whidbey in Oak Harbor, WA!

This position will work first shift and will assist with the disposition of withheld supplier tags. To be successful in this role, one should have experience with designing repairs for discrepant detail parts and assemblies fabricated from composite materials.

Duties Include:

  • Interface with multiple suppliers, dispositioning of discrepant material tags, interfacing with stakeholder groups such as Structural Analysis, Materials & Processing, and Manufacturing personnel in the design center and build facilities.
  • Utilize strong communication and collaboration skills
  • Use knowledge of Manufacturing Execution System (MES)

This position can be filled at either the Aeronautical Engineer (Liaison Engineering) level or the Principal Aeronautical Engineer (Liaison Engineering) level, depending upon the qualifications below.

Basic Qualifications for Aeronautical Engineer:

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) discipline with 3 years of related professional/military experience OR a Master's degree in a relevant STEM discipline with 0 years of related professional/military experience.
  • Hands-on experience in a composites manufacturing facility
  • Experience with composite airframe structures.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Secret clearance
  • Ability to obtain and maintain Special Program Access (SAP). This SAP must be obtained within a reasonable amount of time as determined by the company to meet its business needs.

Basic Qualifications for Principal Aeronautical Engineer:

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) discipline with 5 years of related professional/military experience; OR a Master's degree in a relevant STEM discipline with 3 years of related professional/military experience; OR a PhD in a relevant STEM discipline with 1 year of related professional/military experience.
  • Hands-on experience in a composites manufacturing facility
  • Experience with composite airframe structures.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Secret clearance
  • Ability to obtain and maintain Special Program Access (SAP). This SAP must be obtained within a reasonable amount of time as determined by the company to meet its business needs.

Preferred Qualifications for both levels:

  • Experience with military specs and standards.
  • Experience with repair processes for composite materials used in aerospace structures.
  • Experience interfacing with a military customer
  • Masters Degree in Mechanical Engineering or Aeronautical Engineering
  • Active US Government Secret clearance
  • Current applicable SAP access
  • Northrop Grumman MRB EN signature

Primary Level Salary Range: $83,400.00 - $125,200.00

Secondary Level Salary Range: $103,600.00 - $155,400.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.

title: Financial Solutions Advisor Registration Candidate - Pleasant Hill Financial Center
description:
Job Description:

At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection. We do this by driving Responsible Growth and delivering for our clients, teammates, communities and shareholders every day.

Being a Great Place to Work is core to how we drive Responsible Growth. This includes our commitment to being an inclusive workplace, attracting and developing exceptional talent, supporting our teammates’ physical, emotional, and financial wellness, recognizing and rewarding performance, and how we make an impact in the communities we serve.

Bank of America is committed to an in-office culture with specific requirements for office-based attendance and which allows for an appropriate level of flexibility for our teammates and businesses based on role-specific considerations.

At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. Join us!

Job Description:

As a Financial Solutions Advisor Stage I (FSA I), your journey begins obtaining your Securities Industry licenses, where you receive dedicated and personalized classes for your Securities Industry Essentials [SIE], Series 7 and Series 66 Exams. Once you obtain your licenses, you will be taught the foundational skills needed to be an advisor – from acquiring, building and managing client relationships to considering a client’s complex financial picture and guiding them with advice and solutions to help them live their best financial lives, all while humanizing financial interactions. Once you have reached your key milestones, you will begin working in a financial center where you will help to deliver Bank of America’s core banking, investment solutions and approach to client care. We will equip you with everything you need as you move through the stages of development.

Once you have demonstrated success as a licensed Financial Solutions Advisor Stage I, you will typically progress into the next role, Financial Solutions Advisor Stage II, where you will continue to practice the skills you’ve learned by growing and deepening relationships within a portfolio of clients. As a successful Financial Solutions Advisor Stage II, you will have the opportunity to advance in many roles within Bank of America and Merrill. The Academy will support you along the way with dedicated programs, tools, and resources throughout your career journey.

This position is subject to SAFE Act registration requirements. Pursuant to the SAFE Act requirements, all employees engaged in residential loan mortgage originations must register with the federal registry system and remain in good standing. Since your position requires SAFE Act registration, you will be required to register and to submit to the required SAFE Act background check and registration process. Failure to obtain and/or maintain SAFE Act registration may result in your immediate termination.

We’ll help you:

  • Build a successful career at Bank of America through world-class training and on-boarding programs that set you up for success.

  • Get training and one-on-one coaching from Academy managers who are invested in your success.

  • Grow your business knowledge by using a defined consultative approach with clients to systematically identify client needs and appropriate solutions.

  • Earn your Security Industry Essentials (SIE), Series 7 and Series 66 licenses (63 & 65 accepted, in lieu of 66) though structured lessons and dedicated study time. You must obtain your SIE within 30 days of being hired & your Series 7 & 66 within 120 Days - a requirement for the role.

  • Build your network. Starting at a financial center, you’ll interact with banking customers, small business owners and higher net worth clients alike. You’ll be able to leverage our relationships with one out of two households in the U.S. to help eventually grow your business.

  • Provide end-to-end comprehensive advice, deliver client reviews/presentations with confidence, and recommend strategies to help clients achieve their financial goals and life priorities.

  • Collaborate with core banking and investment partners. Connect clients to the solutions we provide through Bank of America and Merrill to meet virtually all their financial needs.

Required Qualifications

  • Aptitude in obtaining required industry licenses.

  • Must be self-disciplined in managing time and capacity.

  • Experience in cultivating client relationships, accessing needs and recommending solutions.

  • Success creating strong peer relationships through effective communication and collaboration.

  • Demonstrates a results-driven mindset while prioritizing client’s interest in a complex, fast-paced environment.

  • Executes multiple tasks simultaneously.

  • Learns and adapts to new technology or applications.


Desired Qualifications

  • Currently holds FINRA Securities Industry Essentials (SIE)

  • Bachelor's degree and/or a minimum of one year of financial services industry or sales experience

Skills:

  • Client Experience Branding

  • Client Solutions Advisory

  • Investment Management

  • Pipeline Management

  • Referral Management

  • Client Management

  • Customer and Client Focus

  • Portfolio Management

  • Prospecting

  • Referral Identification

  • Business Acumen

  • Executive Presence

  • Oral Communications

  • Risk Management

Weekly Schedule: Monday thru Friday, some Saturdays required

Shift:

1st shift (United States of America)

Hours Per Week:

40

title: Electrical EIT E&R
description:
CIMA+’s Energy & Resources team is a key player in the energy transition. With more than 700 highly qualified professional in this business sector, we are one of the largest teams specializing in this discipline among consulting engineering firms in Canada. Guided by an entrepreneurial culture based on innovation, sustainability, multidisciplinary agility and collaboration, we support our clients at all stages of their projects, from feasibility studies to commissioning. From the production of electricity from renewable sources to resource transformation, our expertise markets are the driving force of a successful energy transition. Regardless of the delivery mode our clients choose, we have the skills and experience required to deliver innovative solutions adapted to their reality. Join us and immerse yourself in a dynamic, innovative, and collaborative environment where you’ll make a real impact. Together, we’ll push boundaries and go above what’s expected of us to meet the challenges of tomorrow and engineer a better world!

We are looking for an Electrical EIT to support our Electrical substation team in Vancouver office. Our team is highly collaborative and exceptionally motivated to continue to develop a fast growing section of the organization. This role will be responsible for working within our local electrical team and designing project across various sectors such as commercial, institutional, educational, and healthcare while under the guidance of a senior engineer.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Preparation of engineering drawings, calculations, analyses, reports, and designs for electrical substations (low, medium, and high voltage), generation facilities, and industrial facilities.
  • Working with Designers and CADD Technicians to develop drawings in accordance with national design standards, safety codes and project specifications and requirements.
  • Developing design deliverables including one-line diagrams, substation physical layouts, material lists, conduit and cable sizing/routing, AC and DC systems calculations and sizing, and substation grounding.
  • Performing site visits during the design, construction, and as-built phases of projects

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering.
  • Strong written and confident verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a team environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Self-motivated and ability to take initiative.
  • Exposure to general Civil Engineering experience a plus.
  • Prior experience in substation design considered a plus.
  • Experience using AutoCAD and/or Microstation considered a plus.
  • Prior experience consulting or working for an electric utility considered a plus.
  • Experience using electrical design software such as SKM PowerTools, ETAP, or EasyPower considered a plus.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering
  • Engineer In Training (EIT) certificate
  • Computer skills in Microsoft Office
  • An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture.
  • Integrity, team spirit, and a commitment to excellence

At CIMA+, we value diversity of talent and perspective. You think you can add value, but don't meet all the job requirements? We invite you to apply, because everyone has something unique to offer. The outstanding talents that choose to join us at CIMA+ soon realize that we go all out to encourage them to grow. We look forward to hearing how you can contribute to our success.

Why choose CIMA+? Because we offer you:

  • Comprehensive Group Benefits available from day one for all permanent employees working at least 20 hours per week
  • Employee and Family Assistance Program
  • Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) with up to 4% employer contribution
  • As an employee-owned company, an annual opportunity to purchase shares for all eligible employees
  • Flexible work schedule in a hybrid work mode
  • Work/Life balance policy across Canada
  • 3-5 weeks of vacation, based on years of relevant experience
  • Tailored training to improve your existing skills

At CIMA+, we recognize the richness and diversity of each individual’s experience. Compensation for this role is therefore based on the candidate’s experience, skills, and qualifications, while maintaining internal equity. The level and associated salary may vary depending on the candidate’s profile.

CIMA+ uses an applicant tracking system that includes an automated match score feature. However, this score is not used to screen, assess, or select applicants. All hiring decisions are made through human review.

Ethics and integrity are fundamental values at CIMA+. That is why we are committed to ensuring equal access to resources and opportunities for candidates, regardless of their identity (race, ethnicity, colour, religion, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, socio-economic status or background, etc.).​

In keeping with the principles of employment equity, we encourage all applications, including, but not limited to, those from women, Indigenous people, people with disabilities and visible minorities. We also encourage candidates to complete the self-identification form when applying for employment.​

We are committed to providing a workplace that is accessible. Accommodations are available in accordance with CIMA's policies. If you require an accommodation, please let us know.

10/29/2026

title: Command Center & Loss Prevention Supervisor - Winter 26-27
description:
The Command Center & Loss Prevention Supervisor partners with the Mountain Sales & Schools management team to safeguard revenue and system integrity across Mountain Sales operations. This role monitors real-time gate scan activity, investigates irregular scan behavior and potential pass fraud, and coordinates with Lift Operations, IT, and frontline teams to resolve access issues. The Supervisor supports and coaches’ staff while serving as the central point of contact for incident intake, escalation, and reporting. This position reports to the Mountain Sales Director of Operations with dual reporting to the Senior Manager of Sales & Reservations.

  • The budgeted salary range for this position is $60,416 - $70,416 . Actual pay will be dependent on budget and experience, all our salaried roles are eligible for bonus.
  • Applications for this position will be considered on a rolling basis.

Essential Job Functions / Key Job Responsibilities

  • Provide supervision and support to agents within the Mountain Sales & Schools team to ensure consistent delivery of exceptional guest service and achievement of goals
  • Model and uphold exemplary customer service standards to foster a guest-focused and sales-driven team culture
  • Manage employee workflow and create effective team schedules that optimize guest service coverage and sales opportunities
  • Develop and maintain reporting processes, dashboards, and documentation to support operational visibility and risk mitigation
  • Gain working knowledge of all Mountain Sales systems including access gates, self-service kiosks, reservation platforms, and training tools to support seamless guest transactions and sales flow
  • Monitor real-time gate scan data across all mountains to identify irregular activity, system errors, and potential misuse; escalate and resolve issues in coordination with Mountain Sales & Schools, Lift Operations, IT
  • Conduct investigations into potential fraud, unauthorized pass use, and irregular scan behavior, documenting findings and presenting to leadership
  • Analyze team performance metrics to identify sales trends and guest feedback, providing actionable insights to management and training teams
  • Address and resolve guest issues promptly and professionally while communicating outcomes to relevant parties to ensure guest loyalty and retention
  • Develop strong working relationships with key personnel to enhance interdepartmental communication and collaboration that benefits guest experience and operational success
  • Demonstrate flexibility to work across multiple locations as business needs require to maintain consistent guest service and sales support
  • Other duties as assigned

Education & Experience Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; bachelor’s degree in business, hospitality, or related field preferred
  • Minimum of three years of professional experience required; mountain operations, sales, or related ski industry experience preferred
  • Minimum of one year of experience in a supervisory or lead role preferred
  • Minimum of one year experience using RTP, gate systems, or access systems required

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Strong computer proficiency including typing skills and ability to navigate multiple computer systems required to support efficient monitoring and investigation
  • Familiarity with Resort Technology Partners (RTP) software a plus for smooth ticketing operations and investigation
  • Money handling experience with US currency required ensuring accuracy and trust in guest transactions required
  • Basic understanding of point-of-sale (POS) systems required to facilitate quick and accurate processing
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills required to engage guests effectively and collaborate with team members
  • Attention to detail and problem-solving skills required to resolve guest issues promptly and maintain sales accuracy
  • Familiarity with loss prevention, auditing, fraud detection, or investigative processes a plus to support proactive identification and resolution of irregular activity
  • Ability to multitask and manage time effectively in a fast-paced environment to sustain excellent guest service and sales flow
  • Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team required to deliver consistent guest experiences and meet sales goals
  • Ability to handle guest inquiries and resolve issues with professionalism and tact preferred to ensure guest satisfaction and loyalty
  • Flexibility and adaptability to changing operational needs and guest demands preferred to maintain seamless sales and service delivery

Work Environment & Physical Demands

title: Workforce Operations Resource Assistant
description:
The Workforce Operations Resource Assistant is part of a collaborative team supporting accurate, fair and efficient rostering. The role focuses on building and maintaining fixed-pattern rotas, completing routine roster updates and keeping workforce information accurate. The Resource Assistant checks information carefully, resolves straightforward issues and escalates exceptions to a Resource Coordinator at the right time. This is an entry-level opportunity for someone who is organised, dependable and confident using systems. It suits a person who enjoys detailed work, communicates clearly and wants to develop their understanding of workforce planning in a fast-moving live broadcast environment.

What you’ll do

  • Build and maintain fixed-pattern rotas in line with agreed templates, staffing arrangements and published deadlines.

  • Check rota information for gaps, clashes, missing data and differences from the agreed pattern, correcting straightforward errors and escalating exceptions.

  • Keep workforce and rostering system data accurate and up to date, following agreed data standards and handling information appropriately.

  • Communicate routine rota information and confirmed changes clearly to colleagues and stakeholders, referring complex queries to a Resource Coordinator.

  • Support the team during busy periods by completing allocated rostering tasks accurately and in priority order.

  • Follow established processes, guidelines and approval routes, keeping clear records of updates and decisions.

  • Develop an understanding of production roles, working patterns and operational requirements to build capability for broader rostering responsibilities.

  • Support the Resource Coordinators and Workforce Planning Manager on ad hoc projects when needed and the wider Workforce Operations team.

What you’ll bring

Essential Criteria:

  • A careful, methodical approach and strong attention to detail.

  • Good organisation skills, with the ability to follow a repeatable process and meet deadlines.

  • Ability to spot errors or inconsistencies, take action within agreed boundaries and ask for help when needed.

  • Clear and professional communication skills, both written and verbal.

  • A calm, dependable and collaborative approach in a busy operational environment.

  • Willingness to learn about rostering, workforce planning and live production requirements.

  • Adaptability and a positive approach to changes in priorities, processes and systems.

Desirable skills and experience:

  • Experience of rostering, scheduling or coordinating shifts.
  • An understanding of fixed working patterns, leave records or workforce systems.
  • Experience in broadcast, live events, sport or another operational environment.

Benefits and perks

There's one thing people can't stop talking about when it comes to life at Sky: the perks. Here’s a taster:

  • Free Sky TV or NOW package, including Sky Sports and Sky Cinema

  • Pension package with up to 9% employer contribution

  • Private healthcare with mental health support

  • Aviva Digital GP and dental insurance

  • Discounts on Sky products, including Sky Mobile, Sky Broadband, Sky Glass and Sky Protect

  • Sharesave and Tech schemes

  • A range of Sky VIP rewards and experiences

How you’ll work

We've adopted a hybrid working approach to give more flexibility on where and how we work. The hybrid working expectations for this role are 3 days in the office per week.

Your office base

Osterley

Our Sky Group HQ. Equipped with state-of-the-art technology and workspaces, there’s plenty of space to see your big ideas come to life. Here you’ll find 13 subsidised restaurants and cafes. You can re-energise at our gym, catch the latest films at our cinema, get your car washed and even get pampered at our beauty salon.

Our Osterley Campus is just a 10-minute walk from Syon Lane train station, or you can get one of our free shuttle buses from Osterley, Gunnersbury and Ealing Broadway stations. Plus, there’s free onsite parking available for cars, motorbikes and bicycles.

Who we are

We’re Sky, a leading media and entertainment company who connect millions with entertainment, sports, news and arts through innovative products and services. Working with us means you’ll be bringing the joy of a better experience to more people, every day. All so we can do better and deliver better for our customers, colleagues and society.

We’re an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We're a Disability Confident Accredited Employer, and welcome and encourage applications from all candidates. We will look to ensure a fair and consistent experience for all and will make reasonable adjustments to support you where appropriate. Please flag any adjustments you need as early as you can.

Just so you know: if your application is successful, we’ll ask you to complete a criminal record check. And depending on the role you have applied for and the nature of any convictions you may have, we might have to withdraw the offer.

To be eligible for this role you are required to have the appropriate right to work in the UK. Please be aware Sky does not offer sponsorship for this position.

title: Summer 2027 Intern: Technology Project Management
description:
About Us

Live Oak Bank is a digital bank that serves small business owners across the country. Our groundbreaking spin on service and technology has fueled our mission to be America’s Small Business Bank. Our products help customers buy, build, and expand their business, and our high-yield savings and CD products help them grow their hard-earned money. At Live Oak, we never lose sight of the well-being of our people. We believe our employees are the heart of our company. Our commitment to our customers and culture is intertwined, and we seek those who embody and embrace what it takes to empower the American dream.

Ready to make an impact? We're looking for an intern(s) to join our team for the onsite 10-week Summer 2027 Internship Program (May 17 - July 23, 2027) at our headquarters in Wilmington, NC. Applications are due by 11:59 p.m. ET on Wednesday, September 23.

How This Role Impacts Live Oak and its People

Live Oak Bank is a dynamic and innovative digital bank on a mission to be America’s Small Business Bank. In Technology, we are committed to revolutionizing the way small business customers achieve financial success through a unified, frictionless experience that meets them wherever they do business. Our team is driven by a passion for creating exceptional products that delight our customers and drive business growth. We are seeking a Summer Intern to join our Technology Portfolio Management Office and contribute directly to the delivery of technology that will shape the future of our industry.

Position Overview

The Technology Portfolio Management Office drives the successful delivery of new technology and business process efficiency in support of our enterprise strategy and ongoing customer needs. As a Summer Intern, you will work alongside other project managers, and perform similar work on real, active projects. You will support project teams, help coordinate delivery activities, and see firsthand how technology moves from idea to customer impact. Your communication and collaboration skills will be instrumental in helping your team be successful. Your curiosity about technology, and a willingness to learn agile methodologies, will be keys to your success in this role.

How You’ll Do It

  • Domain Knowledge: Build your project management and agile knowledge and apply it to help the Technology organization deliver on its goals.

  • Project Management: Support the coordination of people, processes, and technology to deliver projects in line with business goals.

  • Agile Delivery: Participate in agile ceremonies and help coordinate the delivery of technology increments with continuous customer feedback loops.

  • Process Improvement: Contribute ideas to the improvement and optimization of processes affecting multiple teams, fostering collaboration and efficiency.

  • Problem Solving: Identify, explore, and resolve problems in collaboration with your team.

  • Communication & Collaboration: Communicate and collaborate effectively with members of your project teams.

  • Relationships: Build and nurture working relationships with others and leverage those relationships to achieve greater outcomes.

Capstone Project and Mentorship

  • Capstone Project: You will own a summer capstone project scoped with your manager in the first two weeks, and present your outcomes and recommendations to Technology leadership at the end of the internship.

  • Mentorship: You will be paired with an experienced project manager who serves as your mentor, plus a peer buddy for day-to-day support, with regular check-ins throughout the summer.

  • Exposure: You will have opportunities to meet with leaders across Technology and the broader bank to understand how our work supports small business customers.

Preferred Experience

  • Currently enrolled in an undergraduate program

  • Coursework, campus involvement, or prior experience related to project management, business, information systems, or a related field

  • Interest in project management and agile best practices

  • Knowledge of and/or experience using tools such as SmartSheet, Jira, Confluence, and Office 365 is a plus

  • Demonstrated ability to:

  • Solve problems

  • Communicate and collaborate with teams

  • Manage time and follow through on commitments

  • Passion for technology and innovation

#LI-DNI

Our Values

  • Dedication: Possess a deep commitment to Live Oak Bank’s mission and core values, exemplified through a strong work ethic, adaptability and pride in your work.

  • Ownership: Take initiative to deliver positive results by proactively and creatively solving problems, while maintaining a high degree of quality.

  • Respect: Treat everyone with courtesy, politeness, and kindness.

  • Innovation: Embrace fresh ideas and fearlessly contribute new solutions to emerging or existing problems.

  • Teamwork: Foster collaboration, accountability, and trust with others and understand that together, we do more

title: Electronic Technician 3/4
description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman, has an opening for a Electronic Technician 3/4 to join our team of highly qualified and diverse individuals to support our Test and Evaluation Team. This position will be located in Rancho Bernardo, CA.

Test Engineering is looking to fill a Electronic Technician to help support all aspects/disciplines of Test. The selected candidate must possess excellent communication skills and exceptional abilities to work well within a diverse team. The selected individual is expected to work for and under the direction of a senior level personnel, Engineers and or Engineering Manager.

PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES are not limited to the following:

  • Performs routine technical functions related to the support of development engineering activities such as design, test, checkout, fabrication, modification, and assembly of electronics and Electro-mechanical systems, experimental design circuitry, prototype models or specialized test equipment.

  • Applications may include analog, digital and/or video type circuits and logic systems. Guidance is readily available from superiors.

  • Works from schematics, diagrams, written and verbal descriptions, layouts or defined plans to perform routine testing, checkout, troubleshooting, prototype building, environmental testing, and simple developmental engineering tasks.

  • Performs routine operational tests and fault isolation on development systems and equipment to ensure conformance with design specifications.

  • Diagnoses and isolates malfunctions down to component level.

  • Conducts defined engineering tests and collects data as assigned.

  • Utilizes routine development or diagnostic equipment including oscilloscope, VOM, DVM, signal generators and similar test apparatus.

  • Normally assigned in area such as development, engineering, test equipment design, or the like.

  • Build systems using engineering drawings, configuration & recovery documentation

  • Support startup and shutdown procedures, ATP/Delivery, as well as post-delivery support.

  • Produce engineering documentation, reports, drawings (flow charts, block diagrams, and schematics

  • Perform manual labor including but not limited to lifting and moving heavy test equipment, trench covers, often heavy cables and harnessing

  • Ability to work flexible, changing schedules which could include including weekends as necessary.

We offer flexible work arrangements, 9/80 work schedule with every other Friday off, phenomenal learning opportunities, and exposure to a wide variety of projects and customers, and a very friendly team environment. We are looking for self-motivated, proactive, and goal-oriented people to help us grow our services and become even better at what we do.

This role may be filled at a Electronic Technician 3 or 4 based on the qualifications below.

Basic Qualifications Level 3:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent and 4 years or relevant experience in cable wiring, test, electrical installations, or similar.

  • Must have the ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Secret clearance within a reasonable amount of time as determined by business needs.

  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings in accordance with Industry standards, including rack assembly drawings, interconnect wiring diagrams and custom cable assemblies.

  • Working experience with industry standards for connectors.

  • Must be physically able to move up to 50 lbs.

  • Must have color vision to identify cables and wires.

Basic Qualifications Level 4:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent and 6 years or relevant experience in cable wiring, test, electrical installations, or similar.

  • Must have the ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Secret clearance within a reasonable amount of time as determined by business needs.

  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings in accordance with Industry standards, including rack assembly drawings, interconnect wiring diagrams and custom cable assemblies.

  • Working experience with industry standards for connectors.

  • Must be physically able to move up to 50 lbs.

  • Must have color vision to identify cables and wires.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proficiency with general instrumentation, data acquisition, and load control set up and operation

  • Ability to assess anomalies and develop resolutions in conjunction with Engineering.

  • Ability to lead small-scale integration and test team including troubleshooting and modifying test sets to meet requirements

  • Ability to adhere to necessary processes, procedures, and protocols.

  • Desire to learn and assume multi-disciplined technician roles such as: instrumentation, mechanical setup, dynamic testing, environmental/thermal testing

  • Active DoD Secret clearance or higher.

  • Experience with the design and laboratory integration of communication systems and/or networked systems

  • Experience in industry standards for connectors including, but not limited to D38999, Dsub, twinax, RJ45, etc.

  • Candidate must have strong communication and interpersonal skills with an aptitude to learn new material quickly.

  • Experience in aerospace or military environment

What We Offer:

At Northrop Grumman, we are on the cutting edge of innovation -- building the next generation of sophisticated aircraft to protect our country. Our diverse portfolio of programs means there are endless paths to cultivate your career. We are well-known for our inclusive, family environment, phenomenal learning opportunities, and exposure to a wide variety of projects and customers. We also offer exceptional benefits/healthcare and a great 401K matching program!
